28.s: iti nityavidhiḥ prokto naimittikamathocyate // 1
28.d: इति नित्यविधिः प्रोक्तो नैमित्तिकमथोच्यते ॥ 1
28.m: Thus the obligatory rite has been taught; now the occasional rite is explained.

28.s:
niyataṃ bhāvi yannityaṃ tadityasminvidhau sthite /
mukhyatvaṃ tanmayībhūtiḥ sarvaṃ naimittikaṃ tataḥ // 2
28.d:
नियतं भावि यन्नित्यं तदित्यस्मिन्विधौ स्थिते ।
मुख्यत्वं तन्मयीभूतिः सर्वं नैमित्तिकं ततः ॥ 2
28.m: Since what is obligatory is that which is invariable, under this rule / primacy belongs to identity with That; therefore, everything is occasional.

28.s:
dinādikalpanotthe tu naiyatye sarvanityatā /
dinamāsarkṣavarṣādinaiyatyāducyate tadā // 3
28.d:
दिनादिकल्पनोत्थे तु नैयत्ये सर्वनित्यता ।
दिनमासर्क्षवर्षादिनैयत्यादुच्यते तदा ॥ 3
28.m: When regularity arises from the construction of days and so forth, there is universal obligatoriness; / it is called [obligatory] then because of the regularity of days, months, lunar mansions, years, and so on.

28.s:
aśaṅkitavyāvaśyantāsattākaṃ jātucidbhavam /
pramātraniyataṃ prāhurnaimittikamidaṃ budhāḥ // 4
28.d:
अशङ्कितव्यावश्यन्तासत्ताकं जातुचिद्भवम् ।
प्रमात्रनियतं प्राहुर्नैमित्तिकमिदं बुधाः ॥ 4
28.m: That which has a presence occurring occasionally, whose inevitability is not to be doubted, / and which is not fixed to a [single] conscious subject, the wise declare to be occasional.

28.s:
sandhyādi parvasaṃpūjā pavitrakamidaṃ sadā /
nityaṃ niyatarūpatvātsarvasmin śāsanāśrite // 5
28.d:
सन्ध्यादि पर्वसंपूजा पवित्रकमिदं सदा ।
नित्यं नियतरूपत्वात्सर्वस्मिन् शासनाश्रिते ॥ 5
28.m: The twilight rites and the like, festival worship, and this Pavitraka are always / obligatory, because of having an invariable nature, for anyone who takes refuge in the teaching.

28.s:
jñānaśāstragurubhrātṛtadvargaprāptayastathā /
tajjanmasaṃskriyābhedāḥ svajanmotsavasaṃgatiḥ // 6
28.d:
ज्ञानशास्त्रगुरुभ्रातृतद्वर्गप्राप्तयस्तथा ।
तज्जन्मसंस्क्रियाभेदाः स्वजन्मोत्सवसंगतिः ॥ 6
28.m: Likewise, the acquisition of knowledge, scriptures, gurus, spiritual brothers, and their circle; / the various rites of passage of their birth, and arrival at the celebration of one's own birth;

28.s:
śrāddhaṃ vipatpratīkāraḥ pramodo'dbhutadarśanam /
yoginīmelakaḥ svāṃśasantānādyaiśca melanam // 7
28.d:
श्राद्धं विपत्प्रतीकारः प्रमोदोऽद्भुतदर्शनम् ।
योगिनीमेलकः स्वांशसन्तानाद्यैश्च मेलनम् ॥ 7
28.m: ancestral rites, counteracting adversity, rejoicing, witnessing a wonder, / meeting of yoginīs, and meeting with one's own lineage, spiritual descendants, and the like;

28.s:
śāstravyākhyāpurāmadhyāvasānāni kramodayaḥ /
devatādarśanaṃ svāpnamājñā samayaniṣkṛtiḥ // 8
28.d:
शास्त्रव्याख्यापुरामध्यावसानानि क्रमोदयः ।
देवतादर्शनं स्वाप्नमाज्ञा समयनिष्कृतिः ॥ 8
28.m: the beginning, middle, and end of expounding scriptures; the rise of the transmission; / vision of the deity in a dream; receiving a command; and expiation of rules.

28.s:
iti naimittikaṃ śrīmattantrasāre nirūpitam /
trayoviṃśatibhedena viśeṣārcānibandhanam // 9
28.d:
इति नैमित्तिकं श्रीमत्तन्त्रसारे निरूपितम् ।
त्रयोविंशतिभेदेन विशेषार्चानिबन्धनम् ॥ 9
28.m:
Thus the occasional [ritual] has been described in the venerable Tantrasāra,
classified into twenty-three types, as the basis for special worship. // 9

28.s:
tatra parvavidhiṃ brūmo dvidhā parva kulākulam /
kulāṣṭakakṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ proktaṃ śrīyogasaṃcare // 10
28.d:
तत्र पर्वविधिं ब्रूमो द्विधा पर्व कुलाकुलम् ।
कुलाष्टककृतं पूर्वं प्रोक्तं श्रीयोगसंचरे ॥ 10
28.m:
There we explain the rule for the festival day: the festival day is twofold, pertaining to Kula and Akula.
The first, produced by the eight Kulas, was taught in the venerable Yogasaṃcāra: // 10

28.s:
abdhīndu munirityetanmāheśyā brahmasantateḥ /
pratipatpañcadaśyau dve kaumāryā rasavahniyuk // 11
28.d:
अब्धीन्दु मुनिरित्येतन्माहेश्या ब्रह्मसन्ततेः ।
प्रतिपत्पञ्चदश्यौ द्वे कौमार्या रसवह्नियुक् ॥ 11
28.m:
[The tithis numbered] ocean (4), moon (1), and sage (7) belong to Māheśī of the Brahmā lineage;
the first and fifteenth belong to Kaumārī, joined with six (taste) and three (fire); // 11

28.s:
abdhirakṣīndu vaiṣṇavyā aindryāstvastraṃ trayodaśī /
vārāhyā randhrarudrau dve caṇḍyā vasvakṣiyugmakam // 12
28.d:
अब्धिरक्षीन्दु वैष्णव्या ऐन्द्र्यास्त्वस्त्रं त्रयोदशी ।
वाराह्या रन्ध्ररुद्रौ द्वे चण्ड्या वस्वक्षियुग्मकम् ॥ 12
28.m:
ocean (4), eyes (2), and moon (1) belong to Vaiṣṇavī; thirteen and weapon (14) belong to Aindrī;
nine (aperture) and eleven (Rudra) belong to Vārāhī; eight (Vasus) and pair of eyes (2) belong to Caṇḍī. // 12

28.s:
dve dve tithī tu sarvāsāṃ yogeśyā daśamī punaḥ /
tasyā apyaṣṭamī yasmāddvitithiḥ sā prakīrtitā // 13
28.d:
द्वे द्वे तिथी तु सर्वासां योगेश्या दशमी पुनः ।
तस्या अप्यष्टमी यस्माद्द्वितिथिः सा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 13
28.m:
Two lunar days belong to each of all [the goddesses], but the tenth belongs to Yogeśī;
the eighth also belongs to her, because she is proclaimed to possess two lunar days. // 13

28.s:
anyāścākulaparvāpi vaiparītyena lakṣitam /
kulaparveti tadbrūmo yathoktaṃ bhairave kule // 14
28.d:
अन्याश्चाकुलपर्वापि वैपरीत्येन लक्षितम् ।
कुलपर्वेति तद्ब्रूमो यथोक्तं भैरवे कुले ॥ 14
28.m:
The other is the Akula festival, also characterized by contrast;
we explain that Kula festival as stated in the Bhairava Kula [tradition]. // 14

28.s:
haiḍare trikasadbhāve trikakālīkulādike /
yo'yaṃ prāṇāśritaḥ pūrvaṃ kālaḥ proktaḥ suvistarāt // 15
28.d:
हैडरे त्रिकसद्भावे त्रिककालीकुलादिके ।
योऽयं प्राणाश्रितः पूर्वं कालः प्रोक्तः सुविस्तरात् ॥ 15
28.m:
In the Haiḍara, the Trikasadbhāva, the Trikakālīkula, and similar texts,
that time which was previously described at great length as resting upon the vital breath— // 15

28.s:
sa cakrabhedasaṃcāre kāṃcit sūte svasaṃvidam /
svasaṃvitpūrṇatālābhasamayaḥ parva bhaṇyate // 16
28.d:
स चक्रभेदसंचारे कांचित् सूते स्वसंविदम् ।
स्वसंवित्पूर्णतालाभसमयः पर्व भण्यते ॥ 16
28.m:
that [time], moving through the piercing of the cakras, brings forth a certain awareness belonging to oneself;
the moment of attaining the fullness of one's own awareness is called a festival day. // 16

28.s:
parva pūraṇa ityeva yadvā pṝ pūraṇārthakaḥ /
parvaśabdo niruktaśca parva tatpūraṇāditi // 17
28.d:
पर्व पूरण इत्येव यद्वा पॄ पूरणार्थकः ।
पर्वशब्दो निरुक्तश्च पर्व तत्पूरणादिति ॥ 17
28.m:
"Festival day" (parvan) [derives from the root] 'parv' meaning filling, or from 'pṝ' meaning filling;
and the word 'parvan' is etymologized as 'parvan' because it fills that up. // 17

28.s:
haiḍare'tra ca śabdo'yaṃ dvidhā nāntetaraḥ śrutaḥ /
taccakracāraniṣṇātā ye kecit pūrṇasaṃvidaḥ // 18
28.d:
हैडरेऽत्र च शब्दोऽयं द्विधा नान्तेतरः श्रुतः ।
तच्चक्रचारनिष्णाता ये केचित् पूर्णसंविदः ॥ 18
28.m:
And here in the Haiḍara, this word is heard twofold, ending in 'n' and otherwise.
Whoever are skilled in the movement through that cakra, whose awareness is full, // 18

28.s:
tanmelakasamāyuktāste tatpūjāparāḥ sadā /
yo'pyatanmaya eṣo'pi tatkāle svakramārcanāt // 19
28.d:
तन्मेलकसमायुक्तास्ते तत्पूजापराः सदा ।
योऽप्यतन्मय एषोऽपि तत्काले स्वक्रमार्चनात् ॥ 19
28.m:
joined in assembly with them, are always dedicated to that worship.
Even one who is not yet identified with it, by worshipping according to his own sequence at that time, // 19

28.s:
tadyoginīsiddhasaṅghamelakāt tanmayībhavet /
yathā prekṣaṇake tattaddraṣṭṛsaṃvidabheditām // 20
28.d:
तद्योगिनीसिद्धसङ्घमेलकात् तन्मयीभवेत् ।
यथा प्रेक्षणके तत्तद्द्रष्टृसंविदभेदिताम् ॥ 20
28.m:
becomes identified with it through meeting with that assembly of Yoginīs and Siddhas.
Just as at a dramatic spectacle, one immediately attains oneness // 20

28.s:
kramoditāṃ sadya eva labhate tatpraveśanāt /
yogābhyāsakramopāttāṃ tathā pūrṇāṃ svasaṃvidam // 21
28.d:
क्रमोदितां सद्य एव लभते तत्प्रवेशनात् ।
योगाभ्यासक्रमोपात्तां तथा पूर्णां स्वसंविदम् ॥ 21
28.m:
with the consciousness of the various spectators that arises in sequence through immersion in it,
so they immediately attain their own full awareness, // 21

28.s:
labhante sadya evaitatsaṃvidaikyapraveśanāt /
tatkālaṃ cāpi saṃvitteḥ pūrṇatvāt kāmadogdhṛtā // 22
28.d:
लभन्ते सद्य एवैतत्संविदैक्यप्रवेशनात् ।
तत्कालं चापि संवित्तेः पूर्णत्वात् कामदोग्धृता ॥ 22
28.m:
which is acquired through the sequence of yoga practice, by entering into unity with that consciousness;
and at that time, because consciousness is full, it grants all desires. // 22

28.s:
tena tattatphalaṃ tatra kāle saṃpūjayācirāt /
yathā ciropāttadhanaḥ kurvannutsavamādarāt // 23
28.d:
तेन तत्तत्फलं तत्र काले संपूजयाचिरात् ।
यथा चिरोपात्तधनः कुर्वन्नुत्सवमादरात् ॥ 23
28.m:
Therefore, through worship at that time, one quickly obtains that respective fruit.
Just as a man who has long accumulated wealth, respectfully holding a festival, // 23

28.s:
atithiṃ so'nugṛhṇāti tatkālābhijñamāgatam /
tathā suphalasaṃsiddhyai yoginīsiddhanāyakāḥ // 24
28.d:
अतिथिं सोऽनुगृह्णाति तत्कालाभिज्ञमागतम् ।
तथा सुफलसंसिद्ध्यै योगिनीसिद्धनायकाः ॥ 24
28.m:
favors a guest who has arrived knowing that time,
likewise, for the complete accomplishment of good fruits, the leaders of Yoginīs and Siddhas, // 24

28.s:
yatnavanto'pi tatkālābhijñaṃ tamanugṛhṇate /
uktaṃ ca tatra teneha kule sāmānyatetyalam // 25
28.d:
यत्नवन्तोऽपि तत्कालाभिज्ञं तमनुगृह्णते ।
उक्तं च तत्र तेनेह कुले सामान्यतेत्यलम् ॥ 25
28.m:
even though requiring effort, favor him who knows that time.
And on this point it has been declared: "Therefore, enough of general rules here in Kula! // 25

28.s:
yasya yaddhṛdaye devi vartate daiśikājñayā /
mantro yogaḥ kramaścaiva pūjanāt siddhido bhavet // 26
28.d:
यस्य यद्धृदये देवि वर्तते दैशिकाज्ञया ।
मन्त्रो योगः क्रमश्चैव पूजनात् सिद्धिदो भवेत् ॥ 26
28.m:
Whatever resides in someone's heart by command of the spiritual guide,
whether mantra, yoga, or sequence, will bestow accomplishment through worship. // 26

28.s:
kulācāreṇa deveśi pūjyaṃ siddhivimuktaye /
ye parvasveṣu deveśi tarpaṇaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ // 27
28.d:
कुलाचारेण देवेशि पूज्यं सिद्धिविमुक्तये ।
ये पर्वस्वेषु देवेशि तर्पणं तु विशेषतः ॥ 27
28.m:
O Goddess of the gods, one should worship according to Kula practice for accomplishment and liberation.
Those who, on these festival days, O Goddess of the gods, especially [for] the offering of libations // 27

28.s:
gurūṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca na kurvanti pramādataḥ /
durācārā hi te duṣṭāḥ paśutulyā varānane // 28
28.d:
गुरूणां देवतानां च न कुर्वन्ति प्रमादतः ।
दुराचारा हि ते दुष्टाः पशुतुल्या वरानने ॥ 28
28.m:
to gurus and deities, do not perform it out of negligence,
they are ill-behaved, wicked, and equal to beasts, O lovely-faced one! // 28

28.s:
abhāvānnityapūjāyā avaśyaṃ hyeṣu pūjayet /
aṭanaṃ jñānaśaktyādilābhārthaṃ yatprakīrtitam // 29
28.d:
अभावान्नित्यपूजाया अवश्यं ह्येषु पूजयेत् ।
अटनं ज्ञानशक्त्यादिलाभार्थं यत्प्रकीर्तितम् ॥ 29
28.m:
Because daily worship is absent, one must certainly worship on these [days].
The wandering that is proclaimed for obtaining knowledge, power, and the like, // 29

28.s:
śaktiyāgaśca yaḥ prokto vaśyākarṣaṇamāraṇam /
tatsarvaṃ parvadivaseṣvayatnenaiva siddhyati // 30
28.d:
शक्तियागश्च यः प्रोक्तो वश्याकर्षणमारणम् ।
तत्सर्वं पर्वदिवसेष्वयत्नेनैव सिद्ध्यति ॥ 30
28.m:
and the sacrifice to the Śaktis that has been taught, subjugation, attraction, and killing—
all that is accomplished effortlessly on festival days." // 30

28.s:
tatsāmānyaviśeṣābhyāṃ ṣoḍhā parva nirūpitam /
māsasyādyaṃ pañcamaṃ ca śrīdinaṃ paribhāṣyate // 31
28.d:
तत्सामान्यविशेषाभ्यां षोढा पर्व निरूपितम् ।
मासस्याद्यं पञ्चमं च श्रीदिनं परिभाष्यते ॥ 31
28.m:
Through the general and the specific, the festival day is explained as sixfold:
the first and the fifth of the month are defined as "glorious days" (śrīdina). // 31

28.s:
utkṛṣṭatvāt parvadinaṃ śrīpūrvatvena bhāṣyate /
samayo hyeṣa yadguptaṃ tannānupapadaṃ vadet // 32
28.d:
उत्कृष्टत्वात् पर्वदिनं श्रीपूर्वत्वेन भाष्यते ।
समयो ह्येष यद्गुप्तं तन्नानुपपदं वदेत् ॥ 32
28.m:
Because of its pre-eminence, a festival day is designated with the prefix "śrī";
for this is the rule: one should not speak that which is secret without an honorific epithet. // 32

28.s:
turyāṣṭamānyabhuvanacaramāṇi dvayorapi /
pakṣayoriha sāmānyasāmānyaṃ parva kīrtitam // 33
28.d:
तुर्याष्टमान्यभुवनचरमाणि द्वयोरपि ।
पक्षयोरिह सामान्यसामान्यं पर्व कीर्तितम् ॥ 33
28.m:
The fourth, eighth, fourteenth (other world), and last (full/new moon) of both
fortnights are proclaimed here as the general-general festival day. // 33

28.s:
yadeteṣu dineṣveva bhaviṣyadgrahabhātmakaḥ /
ubhayātmā viśeṣaḥ syāttatsāmānyaviśeṣatā // 34
28.d:
यदेतेषु दिनेष्वेव भविष्यद्ग्रहभात्मकः ।
उभयात्मा विशेषः स्यात्तत्सामान्यविशेषता ॥ 34
28.m:
When on these very days there is a twofold specific feature
consisting of the coming planetary position and asterism, that is the general-specific nature. // 34

28.s:
sā caikādaśadhaikasminnekasminvibhunoditā /
sajātīyā tu sotkṛṣṭetyevaṃ śambhurnyarūpayat // 35
28.d:
सा चैकादशधैकस्मिन्नेकस्मिन्विभुनोदिता ।
सजातीया तु सोत्कृष्टेत्येवं शम्भुर्न्यरूपयत् ॥ 35
28.m:
And that was stated by the all-pervading Lord to be elevenfold in each single [month];
and that which belongs to the same class is superior: thus Śambhu explained. // 35

28.s:
kṛṣṇayugaṃ vahnisitaṃ śrutikṛṣṇaṃ vahnisitamiti pakṣāḥ /
arkendujīvacandrā budhayugmendvarkakaviguruvidhu syāt // 36
28.d:
कृष्णयुगं वह्निसितं श्रुतिकृष्णं वह्निसितमिति पक्षाः ।
अर्केन्दुजीवचन्द्रा बुधयुग्मेन्द्वर्ककविगुरुविधु स्यात् ॥ 36
28.m:
The fortnights are: two dark, fire (3) bright, four (Vedas) dark, three (fire) bright.
[The weekdays] should be Sun, Moon, Jupiter, Moon, two Mercury, Moon, Sun, Venus, Jupiter, Moon. // 36

28.s:
paraphalguścaitramaghe tiṣyaḥ prākphalgukarṇaśatabhiṣajaḥ /
mūlaprājāpatye viśākhikā śravaṇasaṃjñayā bhāni // 37
28.d:
परफल्गुश्चैत्रमघे तिष्यः प्राक्फल्गुकर्णशतभिषजः ।
मूलप्राजापत्ये विशाखिका श्रवणसंज्ञया भानि ॥ 37
28.m:
The asterisms are designated as: Uttaraphālgunī, Citrā, Maghā, Puṣya, Pūrvaphālgunī, Śravaṇa (ear), Śatabhiṣaj,
Mūla, Rohiṇī (Prājāpatya), Viśākhā, and Śravaṇa. // 37

28.s:
randhre tithyarkapare vasurandhre śaśivṛṣāṅkarasarandhrayugam /
prathamaniśāmadhyaniśe madhyāhnaśarā dinodayo madhyadinam // 38
28.d:
रन्ध्रे तिथ्यर्कपरे वसुरन्ध्रे शशिवृषाङ्करसरन्ध्रयुगम् ।
प्रथमनिशामध्यनिशे मध्याह्नशरा दिनोदयो मध्यदिनम् ॥ 38
28.m:
On the ninth, fifteenth (lunar day), twelfth (sun), after that, eighth and ninth, Moon (1), Taurus-marked (11), six, and two nines;
the first part of the night, midnight, midday, five [ghaṭikās], sunrise, midday, // 38

28.s:
prathamaniśeti ca samayo mārgaśiraḥprabhṛtimāseṣu /
kanyāntyajātha veśyā rāgavatī tattvavedinī dūtī // 39
28.d:
प्रथमनिशेति च समयो मार्गशिरःप्रभृतिमासेषु ।
कन्यान्त्यजाथ वेश्या रागवती तत्त्ववेदिनी दूती ॥ 39
28.m:
and the first part of the night: this is the time in the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa.
A maiden, an outcaste woman, a courtesan, an impassioned woman, a messenger-consort knowing ultimate reality, // 39

28.s:
vyāsasamāsāt kramaśaḥ pūjyāścakre'nuyāgākhye /
sarvatra ca parvadine kuryādanuyāgacakramatiśayataḥ // 40
28.d:
व्याससमासात् क्रमशः पूज्याश्चक्रेऽनुयागाख्ये ।
सर्वत्र च पर्वदिने कुर्यादनुयागचक्रमतिशयतः ॥ 40
28.m:
should be worshipped in detail and in summary successively in the cakra called Anuyāga;
and everywhere on a festival day, one should especially perform the circle of the secondary sacrifice, // 40

28.s:
guptāguptavidhānādiyāgacaryākrameṇa sampūrṇam /
anuyāgaḥ kila mukhyaḥ sarvasminneva karmaviniyoge // 41
28.d:
गुप्तागुप्तविधानादियागचर्याक्रमेण सम्पूर्णम् ।
अनुयागः किल मुख्यः सर्वस्मिन्नेव कर्मविनियोगे ॥ 41
28.m:
complete according to the procedure of ritual practice, such as the concealed and unconcealed rules;
for the secondary sacrifice is primary in the application of every ritual. // 41

28.s:
anuyāgakālalābhe tasmātprayateta tatparamaḥ /
bhagrahasamayaviśeṣo nāśvayuje ko'pi tena tadvarjam // 42
28.d:
अनुयागकाललाभे तस्मात्प्रयतेत तत्परमः ।
भग्रहसमयविशेषो नाश्वयुजे कोऽपि तेन तद्वर्जम् ॥ 42
28.m:
Therefore, intent on that, one should strive to obtain the time of the secondary sacrifice.
In the month of Āśvayuja there is no specific asterism, planet, or time, so it is excluded. // 42

28.s:
velābhagrahakalanā kathitaikādaśasu māseṣu /
phālgunamāse śuklaṃ yatproktaṃ dvādaśīdinaṃ parva // 43
28.d:
वेलाभग्रहकलना कथितैकादशसु मासेषु ।
फाल्गुनमासे शुक्लं यत्प्रोक्तं द्वादशीदिनं पर्व ॥ 43
28.m:
The determination of the time-period, asterism, and planet is stated for the eleven months;
the festival proclaimed in the month of Phālguna is the twelfth day of the bright fortnight. // 43

28.s:
agratithivedhayogo mukhyatamo'sau viśeṣo'tra /
divasaniśe kila kṛtvā tribhāgaśaḥ prathamamadhyamāparavibhāgaḥ // 44
28.d:
अग्रतिथिवेधयोगो मुख्यतमोऽसौ विशेषोऽत्र ।
दिवसनिशे किल कृत्वा त्रिभागशः प्रथममध्यमापरविभागः ॥ 44
28.m:
The junction piercing the preceding lunar day is the most essential particularity here;
having divided the day and night each into three parts: the first, middle, and last parts, // 44

28.s:
pūjākālastatra tribhāgite mukhyatamaḥ kālaḥ /
yadi saṃghaṭeta velā mukhyatamā bhagrahau tathā cakram // 45
28.d:
पूजाकालस्तत्र त्रिभागिते मुख्यतमः कालः ।
यदि संघटेत वेला मुख्यतमा भग्रहौ तथा चक्रम् ॥ 45
28.m:
the time of worship among those tripartite divisions is the most primary time.
If the most primary time-period, asterism, planet, and cakra should coincide, // 45

28.s:
tadyāga ādiyāgastatkāmyaṃ pūjayaiva parvasu siddhyet /
dinavelābhagrahakalpanena tatrāpi saumyaraudratvam // 46
28.d:
तद्याग आदियागस्तत्काम्यं पूजयैव पर्वसु सिद्ध्येत् ।
दिनवेलाभग्रहकल्पनेन तत्रापि सौम्यरौद्रत्वम् ॥ 46
28.m:
that sacrifice is the primordial sacrifice; desired ends will be accomplished by worship alone on festival days.
Having known mildness and ferocity even there by determining the day, time-period, asterism, and planet, // 46

28.s:
jñātvā sādhakamukhyastattatkāryaṃ tadā tadā kuryāt /
ukto yo'rcākālastaṃ cedullaṅghya bhagrahatithiḥ syāt // 47
28.d:
ज्ञात्वा साधकमुख्यस्तत्तत्कार्यं तदा तदा कुर्यात् ।
उक्तो योऽर्चाकालस्तं चेदुल्लङ्घ्य भग्रहतिथिः स्यात् ॥ 47
28.m:
the foremost of adepts should perform each specific rite at each respective time.
If the lunar day with asterism and planet should transpire, transgressing the stated time of worship, // 47

28.s:
tamanādṛtya viśeṣaṃ pradhānayetsāmayamiti kecit /
neti tvasmadguravo viśeṣarūpā hi tithiriha na velā // 48
28.d:
तमनादृत्य विशेषं प्रधानयेत्सामयमिति केचित् ।
नेति त्वस्मद्गुरवो विशेषरूपा हि तिथिरिह न वेला ॥ 48
28.m:
disregarding that specific [astrological factor], one should prioritize the conventional time: so say some.
"Not so," say our gurus; for here the lunar day, not the time-period, constitutes the specific factor. // 48

28.s:
saṃvedyarūpaśaśadharabhāgaḥ saṃvedakārkakaranikaraiḥ /
yāvānyāvati pūrṇaḥ sā hi tithirbhagrahaiḥ sphuṭībhavati // 49
28.d:
संवेद्यरूपशशधरभागः संवेदकार्ककरनिकरैः ।
यावान्यावति पूर्णः सा हि तिथिर्भग्रहैः स्फुटीभवति ॥ 49
28.m:
To whatever extent the lunar portion, whose nature is the knowable, is filled
by the rays of the sun, whose nature is the knower: that lunar day is made manifest by asterisms and planets. // 49

28.s:
tasmānmukhyātra tithiḥ sā ca viśeṣyā graharkṣayogena /
velātra na pradhānaṃ yuktaṃ caitattathāhi parameśaḥ // 50
28.d:
तस्मान्मुख्यात्र तिथिः सा च विशेष्या ग्रहर्क्षयोगेन ।
वेलात्र न प्रधानं युक्तं चैतत्तथाहि परमेशः ॥ 50
28.m:
Therefore the lunar day is primary here, and it is qualified by conjunction with planets and asterisms;
the time-period is not primary here, and this is logical. For the Supreme Lord // 50

28.s:
śrītrikabhairavakulaśāstreṣūce na parvadivaseṣu /
velāyogaṃ kaṃcana tithibhagrahayogato hyanyam // 51
28.d:
श्रीत्रिकभैरवकुलशास्त्रेषूचे न पर्वदिवसेषु ।
वेलायोगं कंचन तिथिभग्रहयोगतो ह्यन्यम् ॥ 51
28.m:
in the venerable Trika, Bhairava, and Kula scriptures did not state for festival days
any conjunction of time-periods other than the conjunction of lunar day, asterism, and planet. // 51

28.s:
tithistu pūjyā pradhānarūpatvāt /
śvetābhāve kṛṣṇacchāgālambhaṃ hi kathayanti // 52
28.d:
तिथिस्तु पूज्या प्रधानरूपत्वात् ।
श्वेताभावे कृष्णच्छागालम्भं हि कथयन्ति ॥ 52
28.m:
The lunar day, however, must be honored because it is primary;
for they say that in the absence of a white goat, a black goat should be immolated. // 52

28.s:
yatpunarūrmiprabhṛtini śāstre veloditāpi tatkāmyam /
mukhyatayoddiśya vidhiṃ tathāca tatra pauṣaparvadine // 53
28.d:
यत्पुनरूर्मिप्रभृतिनि शास्त्रे वेलोदितापि तत्काम्यम् ।
मुख्यतयोद्दिश्य विधिं तथाच तत्र पौषपर्वदिने ॥ 53
28.m: Furthermore, what is taught as a proper time in scriptures such as the Ūrmi is desire-driven, / taking the primary rite as its aim; thus there, on the day of the Pauṣa festival,

28.s:
kṛtvārcanamardhaniśi dhyātvā japtvā bahirgatasya yathā /
ādeśaḥ phalati tathā māghe cakrādvacaḥ phalati // 54
28.d:
कृत्वार्चनमर्धनिशि ध्यात्वा जप्त्वा बहिर्गतस्य यथा ।
आदेशः फलति तथा माघे चक्राद्वचः फलति ॥ 54
28.m: having performed worship at midnight, meditated, and recited, just as an instruction bears fruit / for one who goes outside, so speech from the cakra bears fruit in Māgha.

28.s:
acirādabhīṣṭasiddhiḥ pañcasu maitrī dhanaṃ ca melāpaḥ /
cakrasthāne krodhāt pāṣāṇasphoṭanena ripunāśaḥ // 55
28.d:
अचिरादभीष्टसिद्धिः पञ्चसु मैत्री धनं च मेलापः ।
चक्रस्थाने क्रोधात् पाषाणस्फोटनेन रिपुनाशः ॥ 55
28.m: Soon comes the attainment of one's desired aim, friendship with five [people], wealth, and assembly [with Yoginīs]; / and at the site of the circle, destruction of enemies occurs by shattering a stone out of anger.

28.s:
siddhādeśaprāptirmārgāntaṃ kathyate vibhunā /
bhagrahayogābhāve velāṃ tu titheravaśyamīkṣeta // 56
28.d:
सिद्धादेशप्राप्तिर्मार्गान्तं कथ्यते विभुना ।
भग्रहयोगाभावे वेलां तु तिथेरवश्यमीक्षेत ॥ 56
28.m: The attainment of infallible prediction up to the end of the road is proclaimed by the all-pervasive Lord. / But in the absence of an astrological conjunction of asterism and planet, one must certainly examine the proper time of the lunar day.

28.s:
sā hi tathā sphuṭarūpā titheḥ svabhāvodayaṃ dadyāt /
bhagrahatithivelāṃśānuyāyi sarvāṅgasundaraṃ tu dinam // 57
28.d:
सा हि तथा स्फुटरूपा तिथेः स्वभावोदयं दद्यात् ।
भग्रहतिथिवेलांशानुयायि सर्वाङ्गसुन्दरं तु दिनम् ॥ 57
28.m: For that [time], being thus manifest in form, grants the rise of the intrinsic nature of the lunar day. / A day that conforms to the asterism, planet, lunar day, and portion of time is beautiful in all its limbs;

28.s:
yadi labhyeta tadāsminviśeṣatamapūjanaṃ racayet /
naca kāmyameva kevalametatparivarjane yataḥ kathitaḥ // 58
28.d:
यदि लभ्येत तदास्मिन्विशेषतमपूजनं रचयेत् ।
नच काम्यमेव केवलमेतत्परिवर्जने यतः कथितः ॥ 58
28.m: if it is obtained, then on this [day] one should perform worship of the most exceptional kind. / Nor is this purely for a desired result, since it is stated that upon omitting it,

28.s:
samayavilopaḥ śrīmadbhairavakula ūrmiśāstre ca /
duṣṭā hi durācārāḥ paśutulyāḥ parva ye na viduḥ // 59
28.d:
समयविलोपः श्रीमद्भैरवकुल ऊर्मिशास्त्रे च ।
दुष्टा हि दुराचाराः पशुतुल्याः पर्व ये न विदुः ॥ 59
28.m: there is a breach of the rule in the venerable Bhairavakula and in the Ūrmiśāstra: / ‘Vile indeed are the ill-behaved, equal to bound souls, who do not know the junction-day!’

28.s:
naca kāmyasyākaraṇe syājjātu pratyavāyitvam /
tatrānuyāgasiddhyarthaṃ cakrayāgo nirūpyate // 60
28.d:
नच काम्यस्याकरणे स्याज्जातु प्रत्यवायित्वम् ।
तत्रानुयागसिद्ध्यर्थं चक्रयागो निरूप्यते ॥ 60
28.m: And there is never any guilt of transgression in not performing an optional rite. / For the sake of accomplishing the secondary sacrifice therein, the circle-sacrifice is expounded.

28.s:
mūrtiyāga iti prokto yaḥ śrīyogīśvarīmate /
nityaṃ naimittikaṃ karma yadatroktaṃ maheśinā // 61
28.d:
मूर्तियाग इति प्रोक्तो यः श्रीयोगीश्वरीमते ।
नित्यं नैमित्तिकं कर्म यदत्रोक्तं महेशिना ॥ 61
28.m: It is taught as the ‘sacrifice of forms’ in the venerable Yogīśvarīmata. / Whatever regular and occasional rite is taught here by the great Lord,

28.s:
sarvatra cakrayāgo'tra mukhyaḥ kāmye viśeṣataḥ /
jñānī yogī ca puruṣaḥ strī vāsminmūrtisaṃjñake // 62
28.d:
सर्वत्र चक्रयागोऽत्र मुख्यः काम्ये विशेषतः ।
ज्ञानी योगी च पुरुषः स्त्री वास्मिन्मूर्तिसंज्ञके ॥ 62
28.m: in all [such cases] the circle-sacrifice here is primary, especially in an optional rite. / A man or a woman who is a knower and a yogi, in this [sacrifice] called ‘of forms’,

28.s:
yoge prayatnato yojyastaddhi pātramanuttaram /
tatsaṃparkātpūrṇatā syāditi traiśirasādiṣu // 63
28.d:
योगे प्रयत्नतो योज्यस्तद्धि पात्रमनुत्तरम् ।
तत्संपर्कात्पूर्णता स्यादिति त्रैशिरसादिषु ॥ 63
28.m: should be engaged with effort in yoga, for that indeed is the unexcelled vessel; / from contact with them fullness arises—thus [it is taught] in the Traiśirasa and other texts.

28.s:
tena sarvaṃ hutaṃ ceṣṭaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram /
jñānine yogine vāpi yo dadāti karoti vā // 64
28.d:
तेन सर्वं हुतं चेष्टं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ।
ज्ञानिने योगिने वापि यो ददाति करोति वा ॥ 64
28.m: By him all has been offered into fire, and the three worlds with their moving and unmoving beings have been worshipped, / whoever gives to a knower or a yogi, or performs [the rite for them].

28.s:
dīkṣottare'pi ca proktamannaṃ brahmā raso hariḥ /
bhoktā śiva iti jñānī śvapacānapyathoddhareat // 65
28.d:
दीक्षोत्तरेऽपि च प्रोक्तमन्नं ब्रह्मा रसो हरिः ।
भोक्ता शिव इति ज्ञानी श्वपचानप्यथोद्धरेअत् ॥ 65
28.m: And in the Dīkṣottara it is taught: ‘Food is Brahmā, flavour is Hari, / the consumer is Śiva’—thus a knower may even liberate outcastes.

28.s:
sarvatattvamayo bhūtvā yadi bhuṅkte sa sādhakaḥ /
tena bhojitamātreṇa sakṛtkoṭistu bhojitā // 66
28.d:
सर्वतत्त्वमयो भूत्वा यदि भुङ्क्ते स साधकः ।
तेन भोजितमात्रेण सकृत्कोटिस्तु भोजिता ॥ 66
28.m: If that adept eats, having become identified with all tattvas, / merely by his being fed, ten million [beings] are fed at once.

28.s:
atha tattvavidetasminyadi bhuñjīta tat priye /
parisaṃkhyā na vidyeta tadāha bhagavāñchivaḥ // 67
28.d:
अथ तत्त्वविदेतस्मिन्यदि भुञ्जीत तत् प्रिये ।
परिसंख्या न विद्येत तदाह भगवाञ्छिवः ॥ 67
28.m: Furthermore, if a knower of reality eats in this [rite], O dear one, / there is no counting [the merit]; so said the blessed Śiva:

28.s:
bhojyaṃ māyātmakaṃ sarvaṃ śivo bhoktā sa cāpyaham /
evaṃ yo vai vijānāti daiśikastattvapāragaḥ // 68
28.d:
भोज्यं मायात्मकं सर्वं शिवो भोक्ता स चाप्यहम् ।
एवं यो वै विजानाति दैशिकस्तत्त्वपारगः ॥ 68
28.m: ‘Everything to be eaten consists of Māyā; Śiva is the consumer, and he is I.’ / Whoever truly knows thus is a teacher who has crossed beyond reality.

28.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā devamāyāntaṃ krīḍantyoṣadhayo gṛhe /
nivṛttamadyaivāsmābhiḥ saṃsāragahanārṇavāt // 69
28.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा देवमायान्तं क्रीडन्त्योषधयो गृहे ।
निवृत्तमद्यैवास्माभिः संसारगहनार्णवात् ॥ 69
28.m: Beholding that divine being arriving, the plants playing in the house [say]: / ‘We have turned back this very day from the impenetrable ocean of transmigratory existence!

28.s:
yadasya vaktraṃ saṃprāptā yāsyāmaḥ paramaṃ padam /
anye'pānabhujo hyūrdhve prāṇo'pānastvadhomukhaḥ // 70
28.d:
यदस्य वक्त्रं संप्राप्ता यास्यामः परमं पदम् ।
अन्येऽपानभुजो ह्यूर्ध्वे प्राणोऽपानस्त्वधोमुखः ॥ 70
28.m: Because, having reached his mouth, we shall go to the supreme state!’ / Others, indeed, are consumers of apāna upwards, but prāṇa and apāna [go] downwards.

28.s:
tasminbhoktari deveśi dātuḥ kulaśatānyapi /
āśveva parimucyante narakādyātanārṇavāt // 71
28.d:
तस्मिन्भोक्तरि देवेशि दातुः कुलशतान्यपि ।
आश्वेव परिमुच्यन्ते नरकाद्यातनार्णवात् ॥ 71
28.m: When he is the consumer, O Goddess of the gods, even hundreds of families of the giver / are quickly freed from the ocean of hellish torments and the like.

28.s:
śrīmanniśāṭane'pyuktaṃ kathanānveṣaṇādapi /
śrotrābhyantarasaṃprāpte guruvaktrādvinirgate // 72
28.d:
श्रीमन्निशाटनेऽप्युक्तं कथनान्वेषणादपि ।
श्रोत्राभ्यन्तरसंप्राप्ते गुरुवक्त्राद्विनिर्गते ॥ 72
28.m: In the venerable Niśāṭana also it is taught: ‘Even through reciting and searching [for it], / when it enters into the hearing, having issued from the guru's mouth,

28.s:
muktastadaiva kāle tu yantraṃ tiṣṭhati kevalam /
surāpaḥ steyahārī ca brahmahā gurutalpagaḥ // 73
28.d:
मुक्तस्तदैव काले तु यन्त्रं तिष्ठति केवलम् ।
सुरापः स्तेयहारी च ब्रह्महा गुरुतल्पगः ॥ 73
28.m: he is liberated at that very moment; only the bodily mechanism remains behind. / Whether a drinker of liquor, a thief, a killer of a brahmin, a violator of the guru's bed,

28.s:
antyajo vā dvijo vātha bālo vṛddho yuvāpi vā /
paryantavāsī yo jñānī deśasyāpi pavitrakaḥ // 74
28.d:
अन्त्यजो वा द्विजो वाथ बालो वृद्धो युवापि वा ।
पर्यन्तवासी यो ज्ञानी देशस्यापि पवित्रकः ॥ 74
28.m: an outcaste or a twice-born, a child, an old man, or even a youth, / the knower who dwells at the boundary purifies even the country;

28.s:
tatra saṃnihito devaḥ sadevīkaḥ sakiṅkaraḥ /
tasmātprādhānyataḥ kṛtvā guruṃ jñānaviśāradam // 75
28.d:
तत्र संनिहितो देवः सदेवीकः सकिङ्करः ।
तस्मात्प्राधान्यतः कृत्वा गुरुं ज्ञानविशारदम् ॥ 75
28.m: in him is present the God accompanied by his Goddess and his attendants.’ / Therefore, having placed principally the guru who is skilled in knowledge,

28.s:
mūrtiyāgaṃ carettasya vidhiryogīśvarīmate /
pavitrārohaṇe śrāddhe tathā parvadineṣvalam // 76
28.d:
मूर्तियागं चरेत्तस्य विधिर्योगीश्वरीमते ।
पवित्रारोहणे श्राद्धे तथा पर्वदिनेष्वलम् ॥ 76
28.m: one should perform the sacrifice of forms. Its procedure in the Yogīśvarīmata [is applied] / at the investiture of the sacred thread, in the ancestral rite, as well as on all junction-days,

28.s:
sūryacandroparāgādau laukikeṣvapi parvasu /
utsave ca vivāhādau viprāṇāṃ yajñakarmaṇi // 77
28.d:
सूर्यचन्द्रोपरागादौ लौकिकेष्वपि पर्वसु ।
उत्सवे च विवाहादौ विप्राणां यज्ञकर्मणि ॥ 77
28.m: during eclipses of the sun and moon and the like, even during worldly festivals, / at celebrations, weddings, and the like, and in the sacrificial rites of brahmins,

28.s:
dīkṣāyāṃ ca pratiṣṭhāyāṃ samayānāṃ viśodhane /
kāmanārthaṃ ca kartavyo mūrtiyāgaḥ sa pañcadhā // 78
28.d:
दीक्षायां च प्रतिष्ठायां समयानां विशोधने ।
कामनार्थं च कर्तव्यो मूर्तियागः स पञ्चधा ॥ 78
28.m: at initiation and consecration, and in the purification of vows. / And for the sake of desires, the sacrifice of forms must be performed; it is fivefold:

28.s:
kevalo yāmalo miśraścakrayugvīrasaṅkaraḥ /
kevalaḥ kevalaireva gurubhirmiśritaḥ punaḥ // 79
28.d:
केवलो यामलो मिश्रश्चक्रयुग्वीरसङ्करः ।
केवलः केवलैरेव गुरुभिर्मिश्रितः पुनः ॥ 79
28.m: solitary, dyadic, mixed, circle-joined, and hero-mingled. / The ‘solitary’ is with gurus alone; but the ‘mixed’ is

28.s:
sādhakādyaiḥ sapatnīkairyāmalaḥ sa dvidhā punaḥ /
patnīyogāt krayānītaveśyāsaṃyogato'thavā // 80
28.d:
साधकाद्यैः सपत्नीकैर्यामलः स द्विधा पुनः ।
पत्नीयोगात् क्रयानीतवेश्यासंयोगतोऽथवा ॥ 80
28.m: with adepts and others with their wives. The ‘dyadic’ is again of two kinds: / from union with a wife, or from union with a courtesan obtained by purchase.

28.s:
cakriṇyādyāśca vakṣyante śaktiyogādyathocitāḥ /
tatsaṃyogāccakrayukto yāgaḥ sarvaphalapradaḥ // 81
28.d:
चक्रिण्याद्याश्च वक्ष्यन्ते शक्तियोगाद्यथोचिताः ।
तत्संयोगाच्चक्रयुक्तो यागः सर्वफलप्रदः ॥ 81
28.m: The circle-women and others, appropriate according to their union with śaktis, will be described; / joined with them, the sacrifice is circle-joined, bestowing all fruits.

28.s:
sarvaistu sahito yāgo vīrasaṅkara ucyate /
madhye gururbhavetteṣāṃ guruvargastadāvṛtiḥ // 82
28.d:
सर्वैस्तु सहितो यागो वीरसङ्कर उच्यते ।
मध्ये गुरुर्भवेत्तेषां गुरुवर्गस्तदावृतिः ॥ 82
28.m: The sacrifice accompanied by all is called ‘hero-mingled’. / The guru should be in their centre, surrounded by the group of gurus.

28.s:
tisra āvṛtayo bāhye samayyantā yathākramam /
paṅktikrameṇa vā sarve madhye teṣāṃ guruḥ sadā // 83
28.d:
तिस्र आवृतयो बाह्ये समय्यन्ता यथाक्रमम् ।
पङ्क्तिक्रमेण वा सर्वे मध्ये तेषां गुरुः सदा ॥ 83
28.m: There are three outer circuits in order, ending with the initiates into the rule; / or all [may sit] in order of rows, with the guru always in their centre.

28.s:
tadā tadgandhadhūpasraksamālambhanavāsasā /
pūjyaṃ cakrānusāreṇa tattaccakramidaṃ tviti // 84
28.d:
तदा तद्गन्धधूपस्रक्समालम्भनवाससा ।
पूज्यं चक्रानुसारेण तत्तच्चक्रमिदं त्विति ॥ 84
28.m: Then with this scent, incense, garland, unguent, and cloth / each respective circle should be worshipped according to the circle, [thinking:] ‘This is that [deity].’

28.s:
ekārake yathā cakre ekavīravidhiṃ smaret /
dvyare yāmalamanyatra trikamevaṃ ṣaḍasrake // 85
28.d:
एकारके यथा चक्रे एकवीरविधिं स्मरेत् ।
द्व्यरे यामलमन्यत्र त्रिकमेवं षडस्रके ॥ 85
28.m: Just as in a one-spoked circle one should remember the rite of the Single Hero, / so in a two-spoked one [that of] the dyad, elsewhere the Trika, likewise in a six-cornered one

28.s:
ṣaḍyoginīḥ saptakaṃ ca saptāre'ṣṭāṣṭake ca vā /
anyadvā tādṛśaṃ tatra cakre tādṛksvarūpiṇi // 86
28.d:
षड्योगिनीः सप्तकं च सप्तारेऽष्टाष्टके च वा ।
अन्यद्वा तादृशं तत्र चक्रे तादृक्स्वरूपिणि ॥ 86
28.m: the six Yoginīs, and the heptad in a seven-spoked [circle], or in an eightfold-eight [group], / or whatever else is of such kind in a circle having such an intrinsic nature.

28.s:
tataḥ pātre'lisaṃpūrṇe pūrvaṃ cakraṃ yajetsudhīḥ /
ādhārayukte nādhārarahitaṃ tarpaṇaṃ kvacit // 87
28.d:
ततः पात्रेऽलिसंपूर्णे पूर्वं चक्रं यजेत्सुधीः ।
आधारयुक्ते नाधाररहितं तर्पणं क्वचित् ॥ 87
28.m: Then, in a vessel filled with liquor, the wise one should first worship the circle; / [the vessel must be] placed on a base; oblation is never [made] without a base.

28.s:
ādhāreṇa vinā bhraṃśo naca tuṣyanti raśmayaḥ /
pretarūpaṃ bhavetpātraṃ śāktāmṛtamathāsavaḥ // 88
28.d:
आधारेण विना भ्रंशो नच तुष्यन्ति रश्मयः ।
प्रेतरूपं भवेत्पात्रं शाक्तामृतमथासवः ॥ 88
28.m: Without a base there is a fall, and the rays [of consciousness] are not satisfied; / the vessel would become of the nature of a corpse, whereas the liquor is the nectar of Śakti.

28.s:
bhoktrī tatra tu yā śaktiḥ sa śambhuḥ parameśvaraḥ /
aṇuśaktiśivātmetthaṃ dhyātvā saṃmilitaṃ trayam // 89
28.d:
भोक्त्री तत्र तु या शक्तिः स शम्भुः परमेश्वरः ।
अणुशक्तिशिवात्मेत्थं ध्यात्वा संमिलितं त्रयम् ॥ 89
28.m: The power that is the consumer therein is Śambhu, the supreme Lord. / Having thus meditated on the three united—the soul, power, and Śiva—

28.s:
tatastu tarpaṇaṃ kāryamāvṛterāvṛteḥ kramāt /
pratisaṃcarayogena punarantaḥ praveśayet // 90
28.d:
ततस्तु तर्पणं कार्यमावृतेरावृतेः क्रमात् ।
प्रतिसंचरयोगेन पुनरन्तः प्रवेशयेत् ॥ 90
28.m: the offering of libations must then be made in succession from circuit to circuit; / by means of reabsorption, he should cause [the libation] to enter within once more,

28.s:
yāvadgurvantikaṃ taddhi pūrṇaṃ bhramaṇamucyate /
tatrādau devatāstarpyāstato vīrā iti kramaḥ // 91
28.d:
यावद्गुर्वन्तिकं तद्धि पूर्णं भ्रमणमुच्यते ।
तत्रादौ देवतास्तर्प्यास्ततो वीरा इति क्रमः ॥ 91
28.m: up to the vicinity of the guru; that is called the complete circuit. / Therein the deities are to be offered libation first, and after them the heroes: such is the sequence.

28.s:
vīraśca vīraśaktiścetyevamasmadgurukramaḥ /
tato'vadaṃśānvividhān māṃsamatsyādisaṃyutān // 92
28.d:
वीरश्च वीरशक्तिश्चेत्येवमस्मद्गुरुक्रमः ।
ततोऽवदंशान्विविधान् मांसमत्स्यादिसंयुतान् ॥ 92
28.m: The hero and the hero's consort: such is the tradition of our guru. / Then the excellent adept should scatter in front various snacks

28.s:
agre tatra pravikiret tṛptyantaṃ sādhakottamaḥ /
pātrābhāve punarbhadraṃ vellitāśuktimeva ca // 93
28.d:
अग्रे तत्र प्रविकिरेत् तृप्त्यन्तं साधकोत्तमः ।
पात्राभावे पुनर्भद्रं वेल्लिताशुक्तिमेव च ॥ 93
28.m: accompanied by meat, fish, and the like, until satisfaction [is attained]. / In the absence of a vessel, the wise one should make the ‘auspicious’ [hand-gesture]

28.s:
pātre kurvīta matimāniti siddhāmate kramaḥ /
dakṣahastena bhadraṃ syādvellitā śuktirucyate // 94
28.d:
पात्रे कुर्वीत मतिमानिति सिद्धामते क्रमः ।
दक्षहस्तेन भद्रं स्याद्वेल्लिता शुक्तिरुच्यते ॥ 94
28.m: and the ‘rolled pearl-oyster’ into a vessel; such is the sequence in the Siddhā school. / The ‘auspicious’ is made with the right hand; the ‘rolled pearl-oyster’ is taught [as follows]:

28.s:
dakṣahastasya kurvīta vāmopari kanīyasīm /
tarjanyaṅguṣṭhayogena dakṣādho vāmakāṅgulīḥ // 95
28.d:
दक्षहस्तस्य कुर्वीत वामोपरि कनीयसीम् ।
तर्जन्यङ्गुष्ठयोगेन दक्षाधो वामकाङ्गुलीः ॥ 95
28.m: One should place the little finger of the right hand over the left, / [and] with the joining of the forefinger and thumb, [place] the fingers of the left hand beneath the right;

28.s:
niḥsandhibandhau dvāvitthaṃ vellitā śuktirucyate /
ye tatra pānakāle tu bindavo yānti medinīm // 96
28.d:
निःसन्धिबन्धौ द्वावित्थं वेल्लिता शुक्तिरुच्यते ।
ये तत्र पानकाले तु बिन्दवो यान्ति मेदिनीम् ॥ 96
28.m: the two clasps thus being without gaps is called the ‘rolled pearl-oyster’. / Whatever drops fall to the ground at the time of drinking therein,

28.s:
taistuṣyanti hi vetālaguhyakādyā gabhastayaḥ /
dhārayā bhairavastuṣyet karapānaṃ paraṃ tataḥ // 97
28.d:
तैस्तुष्यन्ति हि वेतालगुह्यकाद्या गभस्तयः ।
धारया भैरवस्तुष्येत् करपानं परं ततः ॥ 97
28.m: the rays consisting of Vetālas, Guhyakas, and others are satisfied by them. / Bhairava is satisfied by the stream; therefore drinking from the hand is supreme.

28.s:
praveśo'tra na dātavyaḥ pūrvameva hi kasyacit /
pramādāttu praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ naiva carcayet // 98
28.d:
प्रवेशोऽत्र न दातव्यः पूर्वमेव हि कस्यचित् ।
प्रमादात्तु प्रविष्टस्य विचारं नैव चर्चयेत् ॥ 98
28.m: No entrance at all should be granted to anyone beforehand; / but in the case of someone who has entered through inadvertence, one should not raise an inquiry.

28.s:
evaṃ kṛtvā kramādyāgamante dakṣiṇayā yutam /
samālambhanatāmbūlavastrādyaṃ vitaredbudhaḥ // 99
28.d:
एवं कृत्वा क्रमाद्यागमन्ते दक्षिणया युतम् ।
समालम्भनताम्बूलवस्त्राद्यं वितरेद्बुधः ॥ 99
28.m: Having thus performed the sacrifice in proper order, accompanied by a fee at the end, / the wise one should distribute unguent, betel, cloth, and the like.

28.s:
rūpakārdhāt paraṃ hīnāṃ na dadyāddakṣiṇāṃ sudhīḥ /
samayibhyaḥ kramāddvidviguṇā gurvantakaṃ bhavet // 100
28.d:
रूपकार्धात् परं हीनां न दद्याद्दक्षिणां सुधीः ।
समयिभ्यः क्रमाद्द्विद्विगुणा गुर्वन्तकं भवेत् ॥ 100
28.m: The wise one should not give a fee less than half a silver coin; / [beginning] from the initiates into the rule, it should double successively up to the guru.

28.s:
eṣa syānmūrtiyāgastu sarvayāgapradhānakaḥ /
kāmye tu saṃvidhau saptakṛtvaḥ kāryastathāvidhaḥ // 101
28.d:
एष स्यान्मूर्तियागस्तु सर्वयागप्रधानकः ।
काम्ये तु संविधौ सप्तकृत्वः कार्यस्तथाविधः ॥ 101
28.m: This bodily sacrifice (mūrtiyāga) is the chief among all sacrifices; / in an optional rite (kāmya), however, it should be performed seven times in this manner. // 101

28.s:
jānanti prathamaṃ gehaṃ tatastasya samarthatām /
balābalaṃ tataḥ paścādvismayante'tra mātaraḥ // 102
28.d:
जानन्ति प्रथमं गेहं ततस्तस्य समर्थताम् ।
बलाबलं ततः पश्चाद्विस्मयन्तेऽत्र मातरः ॥ 102
28.m: First they perceive the house, then his competence, / and then his strength and weakness; thereafter, the Mothers are struck with wonder here. // 102

28.s:
tato'pi saṃnidhīyante prīyante varadāstataḥ /
devīnāmatha nāthasya parivārayujo'pyalam // 103
28.d:
ततोऽपि संनिधीयन्ते प्रीयन्ते वरदास्ततः ।
देवीनामथ नाथस्य परिवारयुजोऽप्यलम् ॥ 103
28.m: Then they become present, then they are pleased and grant boons, / as do exceedingly the retinues of the Goddesses and of the Lord. // 103

28.s:
vallabho mūrtiyāgo'yamataḥ kāryo vipaścitā /
rāktau gupte gṛhe vīrāḥ śaktayo'nyonyamapyalam // 104
28.d:
वल्लभो मूर्तियागोऽयमतः कार्यो विपश्चिता ।
राक्तौ गुप्ते गृहे वीराः शक्तयोऽन्योन्यमप्यलम् ॥ 104
28.m: Hence, this bodily sacrifice is beloved [to them], and should be performed by the wise person. / At night, in a secluded house, the heroes and the powers among themselves [are gathered] abundantly. // 104

28.s:
asaṃketayujo yojyā devatāśabdakīrtanāt /
alābhe mūrticakrasya kumārīreva pūjayet // 105
28.d:
असंकेतयुजो योज्या देवताशब्दकीर्तनात् ।
अलाभे मूर्तिचक्रस्य कुमारीरेव पूजयेत् ॥ 105
28.m: Unbound by conventional codes, they should be applied by chanting the names of the deities. / If the circle of bodily deities is unavailable, one should worship young maidens instead. // 105

28.s:
kāmyārthe tu na tāṃ vyaṅgāṃ stanapuṣpavatīṃ tathā /
pratipacchrutisaṃjñe ca caturthī cottarātraye // 106
28.d:
काम्यार्थे तु न तां व्यङ्गां स्तनपुष्पवतीं तथा ।
प्रतिपच्छ्रुतिसंज्ञे च चतुर्थी चोत्तरात्रये ॥ 106
28.m: For an optional aim, however, one must not [worship] a deformed maiden, nor one with breasts or menstruation. / Now, the first tithi [paired with] Śravaṇā, the fourth [with] the three Uttarās, // 106

28.s:
haste ca pañcamī ṣaṣṭhī pūrvāsvatha punarvasau /
saptamī tatparā pitrye rohiṇyāṃ navamī tathā // 107
28.d:
हस्ते च पञ्चमी षष्ठी पूर्वास्वथ पुनर्वसौ ।
सप्तमी तत्परा पित्र्ये रोहिण्यां नवमी तथा ॥ 107
28.m: and the fifth [paired with] Hasta, the sixth with the Pūrvās, then the seventh with Punarvasu, / the eighth with Maghā (the Pitṛs' asterism), and the ninth with Rohiṇī, // 107

28.s:
mūle tu dvādaśī brāhme bhūtāśvinyāṃ ca pūrṇimā /
dhaniṣṭhāyāmamāvasyā so'yamekādaśātmakaḥ // 108
28.d:
मूले तु द्वादशी ब्राह्मे भूताश्विन्यां च पूर्णिमा ।
धनिष्ठायाममावस्या सोऽयमेकादशात्मकः ॥ 108
28.m: the twelfth with Mūla, the fourteenth with Rohiṇī (the asterism of Brahmā), the full moon with Aśvinī, / and the new moon with Dhaniṣṭhā—this set of eleven, // 108

28.s:
arkāditrayaśukrānyatamayukto'pyahargaṇaḥ /
yogaparveti vikhyāto rātrau vā dina eva vā // 109
28.d:
अर्कादित्रयशुक्रान्यतमयुक्तोऽप्यहर्गणः ।
योगपर्वेति विख्यातो रात्रौ वा दिन एव वा ॥ 109
28.m: joined with Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, or Friday (the three beginning with the Sun, or Venus), / is known as a conjunction-junction (yogaparvan), occurring either by night or by day. // 109

28.s:
yogaparvaṇi kartavyo mūrtiyāgastu sarvathā /
yaḥ sarvānyogaparvākhyān vāsarān pūjayetsudhīḥ // 110
28.d:
योगपर्वणि कर्तव्यो मूर्तियागस्तु सर्वथा ।
यः सर्वान्योगपर्वाख्यान् वासरान् पूजयेत्सुधीः ॥ 110
28.m: On a conjunction-junction, the bodily sacrifice must by all means be performed. / The wise one who worships on all days called conjunction-junctions // 110

28.s:
mūrtiyāgena so'pi syāt samayī maṇḍalaṃ vinā /
ityeṣa mūrtiyāgaḥ śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate // 111
28.d:
मूर्तियागेन सोऽपि स्यात् समयी मण्डलं विना ।
इत्येष मूर्तियागः श्रीसिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते ॥ 111
28.m: by means of the bodily sacrifice becomes an initiate into the rule (samayī) even without a maṇḍala. / Such is the bodily sacrifice according to the doctrine of the venerable Siddhayogīśvarī. // 111

28.s:
athocyate śivenoktaḥ pavitrakavidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ /
śrīratnamālātriśiraḥśāstrayoḥ sūcitaḥ punaḥ // 112
28.d:
अथोच्यते शिवेनोक्तः पवित्रकविधिः स्फुटः ।
श्रीरत्नमालात्रिशिरःशास्त्रयोः सूचितः पुनः ॥ 112
28.m: Now the clear rite of the sacred thread (pavitraka) spoken by Śiva is explained, / which was further indicated in the venerable Ratnamālā and Triśirobhairava scriptures, // 112

28.s:
śrīsiddhāṭanasadbhāvamālinīsāraśāsane /
tatra prādhānyataḥ śrīmanmālokto vidhirucyate // 113
28.d:
श्रीसिद्धाटनसद्भावमालिनीसारशासने ।
तत्र प्राधान्यतः श्रीमन्मालोक्तो विधिरुच्यते ॥ 113
28.m: and in the scriptures Siddhadharmāṭana, Sadbhāva, and Mālinīsāra. / Among these, the rite taught in the venerable Ratnamālā is related primarily: // 113

28.s:
kṣīrābdhimathanodbhūtaviṣanidrāvimūrcchitaḥ /
nāgarājaḥ svabhuvane meghakāle sma nāvasat // 114
28.d:
क्षीराब्धिमथनोद्भूतविषनिद्राविमूर्च्छितः ।
नागराजः स्वभुवने मेघकाले स्म नावसत् ॥ 114
28.m: Fainting in the slumber caused by the poison arising from the churning of the milk-ocean, / the serpent king could not dwell in his own realm during the rainy season. // 114

28.s:
kevalaṃ tu pavitro'yaṃ vāyubhakṣaḥ samāḥ śatam /
divyaṃ daśaguṇaṃ nāthaṃ bhairavaṃ paryapūjayat // 115
28.d:
केवलं तु पवित्रोऽयं वायुभक्षः समाः शतम् ।
दिव्यं दशगुणं नाथं भैरवं पर्यपूजयत् ॥ 115
28.m: Being wholly pure (pavitra) and feeding only on wind, he worshipped the Lord Bhairava / for a divine century multiplied ten-fold. // 115

28.s:
vyajijñapacca taṃ tuṣṭaṃ nāthaṃ varṣāsvahaṃ nije /
pātāle nāsituṃ śaktaḥ so'pyenaṃ parameśvaraḥ // 116
28.d:
व्यजिज्ञपच्च तं तुष्टं नाथं वर्षास्वहं निजे ।
पाताले नासितुं शक्तः सोऽप्येनं परमेश्वरः ॥ 116
28.m: And he petitioned the pleased Lord: "During the rains I am unable to remain / in my own subterranean realm (Pātāla)." And the Supreme Lord // 116

28.s:
nāgaṃ nijajaṭājūṭapīṭhagaṃ paryakalpayat /
tataḥ samastadevaughairdhārito'sau svamūrdhani // 117
28.d:
नागं निजजटाजूटपीठगं पर्यकल्पयत् ।
ततः समस्तदेवौघैर्धारितोऽसौ स्वमूर्धनि ॥ 117
28.m: placed the serpent upon the throne of his own matted hair. / Then he was held upon their heads by the entire assembly of gods. // 117

28.s:
mahatāṃ mahitānāṃ hi nādbhuta viśvapūjyatā /
tasmānmaheśiturmūrdhni devatānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ // 118
28.d:
महतां महितानां हि नाद्भुत विश्वपूज्यता ।
तस्मान्महेशितुर्मूर्ध्नि देवतानां च सर्वशः ॥ 118
28.m: For it is not surprising that the great who are honoured [by Śiva] are revered by all the universe. / Therefore, upon the head of the Great Lord, of the deities in every respect, // 118

28.s:
ātmanaśca pavitraṃ taṃ kuryādyāgapuraḥsaram /
daśa koṭyo na pūjānāṃ pavitrārohaṇe samāḥ // 119
28.d:
आत्मनश्च पवित्रं तं कुर्याद्यागपुरःसरम् ।
दश कोट्यो न पूजानां पवित्रारोहणे समाः ॥ 119
28.m: and of oneself, one should place that sacred thread preceded by sacrifice. / A hundred million acts of worship are not equal to the investiture of the sacred thread. // 119

28.s:
vṛthā dīkṣā vṛthā jñānaṃ gurvārādhanameva ca /
vinā pavitrādyenaitaddharennāgaḥ śivājñayā // 120
28.d:
वृथा दीक्षा वृथा ज्ञानं गुर्वाराधनमेव च ।
विना पवित्राद्येनैतद्धरेन्नागः शिवाज्ञया ॥ 120
28.m: Vain is initiation, vain is knowledge, and [vain is] worship of the guru; / without the sacred thread and similar rites, the serpent seizes this by Śiva's command. // 120

28.s:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena sa kāryaḥ kulavedibhiḥ /
āṣāḍhaśuklānmithunakarkaṭasthe ravau vidhiḥ // 121
28.d:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन स कार्यः कुलवेदिभिः ।
आषाढशुक्लान्मिथुनकर्कटस्थे रवौ विधिः ॥ 121
28.m: Therefore, it must be performed with every effort by the knowers of the Kula. / Beginning from the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, while the sun is in Gemini or Cancer, // 121

28.s:
kartavyaḥ so'nirodhena yāvatsā tulapūrṇimā /
tulopalakṣitasyāntyaṃ kārtikasya dinaṃ matam // 122
28.d:
कर्तव्यः सोऽनिरोधेन यावत्सा तुलपूर्णिमा ।
तुलोपलक्षितस्यान्त्यं कार्तिकस्य दिनं मतम् ॥ 122
28.m: this rite should be carried out unobstructed up to the full moon of Libra. / The final day of the [solar period] marked by Libra is held to be [that of] Kārttika. // 122

28.s:
kulaśabdaṃ paṭhanto'nye vyākhyābhedaṃ prakurvate /
nityātantravidaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ kārtikāccaramaṃ dinam // 123
28.d:
कुलशब्दं पठन्तोऽन्ये व्याख्याभेदं प्रकुर्वते ।
नित्यातन्त्रविदः कृष्णं कार्तिकाच्चरमं दिनम् ॥ 123
28.m: Others reciting the word *kula* offer a different interpretation: / the knowers of the Nityātantra hold the last dark day after Kārttika // 123

28.s:
kulasya nityācakrasya pūrṇatvaṃ yatra tanmatam /
māghaśuklāntyadivasaḥ kulaparveti tanmatam // 124
28.d:
कुलस्य नित्याचक्रस्य पूर्णत्वं यत्र तन्मतम् ।
माघशुक्लान्त्यदिवसः कुलपर्वेति तन्मतम् ॥ 124
28.m: to be that on which the fullness of the Kula, the circle of the Nityās, occurs. / In their view, the last day of the bright fortnight of Māgha is the festival of the Kula (kulaparvan). // 124

28.s:
pūrṇatvaṃ tatra candrasya sā tithiḥ kulapūrṇimā /
dakṣiṇottaragaḥ kālaḥ kulākulatayoditaḥ // 125
28.d:
पूर्णत्वं तत्र चन्द्रस्य सा तिथिः कुलपूर्णिमा ।
दक्षिणोत्तरगः कालः कुलाकुलतयोदितः ॥ 125
28.m: There the moon attains fullness; that tithi is the full moon of the Kula. / Time proceeding south and north is taught as having the nature of Kula and Akula. // 125

28.s:
kulasya tasya carame dine pūrṇatvamucyate /
dakṣiṇāyanaṣaṇmāsakartavyatvamato vidhau // 126
28.d:
कुलस्य तस्य चरमे दिने पूर्णत्वमुच्यते ।
दक्षिणायनषण्मासकर्तव्यत्वमतो विधौ ॥ 126
28.m: Fullness is stated on the final day of that Kula; / hence, for the rite of the sacred thread, there is an obligation [extending over] the six months of the southern course, // 126

28.s:
pavitrake prakāśatvasiddhyai kṛṣṇasya vartmanaḥ /
tadetadbahuśāstroktaṃ rūpaṃ devo nyarūpayat // 127
28.d:
पवित्रके प्रकाशत्वसिद्ध्यै कृष्णस्य वर्त्मनः ।
तदेतद्बहुशास्त्रोक्तं रूपं देवो न्यरूपयत् ॥ 127
28.m: in order to achieve luminosity for the dark path. / The Lord explained this form, taught in many scriptures, // 127

28.s:
ekenaiva padena śrīratnamālākulāgame /
tadatra samaye sarvavidhisaṃpūraṇātmakaḥ // 128
28.d:
एकेनैव पदेन श्रीरत्नमालाकुलागमे ।
तदत्र समये सर्वविधिसंपूरणात्मकः ॥ 128
28.m: by a single word in the venerable scripture of the Ratnamālā Kula. / Therefore, at this time, consisting of the fulfillment of all rites, // 128

28.s:
pavitrakavidhiḥ kāryaḥ śuklapakṣe tu sarvathā /
pūraṇaṃ śaktiyogena śaktyātma ca sitaṃ dalam // 129
28.d:
पवित्रकविधिः कार्यः शुक्लपक्षे तु सर्वथा ।
पूरणं शक्तियोगेन शक्त्यात्म च सितं दलम् ॥ 129
28.m: the rite of the sacred thread must by all means be performed in the bright fortnight. / Fulfillment is through union with the power, and the bright fortnight is the nature of the power. // 129

28.s:
dakṣiṇāyanasājātyāt tena tadvidhirucyate /
ekadvitricatuḥpañcaṣaḍlataikatamaṃ mahat // 130
28.d:
दक्षिणायनसाजात्यात् तेन तद्विधिरुच्यते ।
एकद्वित्रिचतुःपञ्चषड्लतैकतमं महत् ॥ 130
28.m: Because of its common nature with the southern course, that rite is explained accordingly: / One of one, two, three, four, five, or six strands, large, // 130

28.s:
hemaratnāṅkitagranthi kuryānmuktāpavitrakam /
sauvarṇasūtraṃ triguṇaṃ saikagranthiśataṃ gurau // 131
28.d:
हेमरत्नाङ्कितग्रन्थि कुर्यान्मुक्तापवित्रकम् ।
सौवर्णसूत्रं त्रिगुणं सैकग्रन्थिशतं गुरौ ॥ 131
28.m: having knots marked with gold and gems, a pearl sacred thread should be made. / A golden thread, threefold, with one hundred and one knots, is for the guru; // 131

28.s:
pare gurau tu tryadhikamadhyabdhi parameṣṭhini /
prāksiddhācāryayogeśa viṣaye tu rasādhikam // 132
28.d:
परे गुरौ तु त्र्यधिकमध्यब्धि परमेष्ठिनि ।
प्राक्सिद्धाचार्ययोगेश विषये तु रसाधिकम् ॥ 132
28.m: for the supreme guru, however, having three more [i.e. 104]; for the Parameṣṭhin, [having four more, i.e.] 108; / in the case of the previously accomplished masters and lords of yoga, having six more [i.e. 106]; // 132

28.s:
aṣṭādhikaṃ śivasyoktaṃ citraratnaprapūritam /
vidyāpīṭhākṣasūtrādau guruvacchivavat punaḥ // 133
28.d:
अष्टाधिकं शिवस्योक्तं चित्ररत्नप्रपूरितम् ।
विद्यापीठाक्षसूत्रादौ गुरुवच्छिववत् पुनः ॥ 133
28.m: having eight more [i.e. 108] is taught for Śiva, filled with varied gems. / For the throne of knowledge, the rosary, and so forth, it is as for the guru; again, as for Śiva // 133

28.s:
vaṭuke kanakābhāve raupyaṃ tu parikalpayet /
pāṭṭasūtramatha kṣaumaṃ kārpāsaṃ tritritānitam // 134
28.d:
वटुके कनकाभावे रौप्यं तु परिकल्पयेत् ।
पाट्टसूत्रमथ क्षौमं कार्पासं त्रित्रितानितम् ॥ 134
28.m: for Vaṭuka. In the absence of gold, one should substitute silver. / Or a silk thread, or linen, or cotton, threefold-threefold spun; // 134

28.s:
tasmānnavaguṇāt sūtrāttriguṇādikramāt kuru /
caṇḍāṃśuguṇaparyantaṃ tato'pi triguṇaṃ ca vā // 135
28.d:
तस्मान्नवगुणात् सूत्रात्त्रिगुणादिक्रमात् कुरु ।
चण्डांशुगुणपर्यन्तं ततोऽपि त्रिगुणं च वा ॥ 135
28.m: from that ninefold thread, make [it] in the sequence beginning with three-fold / up to twelve-fold (the multiplier of the fierce-rayed Sun), or even threefold that. // 135

28.s:
tenāṣṭādaśatantūtthamadhamaṃ madhyamaṃ punaḥ /
aṣṭottaraśataṃ tasmāt triguṇaṃ tūttamaṃ matam // 136
28.d:
तेनाष्टादशतन्तूत्थमधमं मध्यमं पुनः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतं तस्मात् त्रिगुणं तूत्तमं मतम् ॥ 136
28.m: Therefore, that made of eighteen strands is the lowest; the middling is / of one hundred and eight; while that threefold from it is considered the best. // 136

28.s:
granthayastattvasaṃkhyātāḥ ṣaḍadhvakalanāvaśāt /
yadvā vyāsasamāsābhyāṃ citrāḥ sadgandhapūritāḥ // 137
28.d:
ग्रन्थयस्तत्त्वसंख्याताः षडध्वकलनावशात् ।
यद्वा व्याससमासाभ्यां चित्राः सद्गन्धपूरिताः ॥ 137
28.m: The knots are numbered according to the principles (tattva), by virtue of the enumeration of the six paths, / or else, in detailed or abbreviated forms, variegated and infused with fragrant scents. // 137

28.s:
viśeṣavidhinā pūrvaṃ pūjayitvārpayettataḥ /
pavitrakaṃ samastādhvaparipūrṇatvabhāvanāt // 138
28.d:
विशेषविधिना पूर्वं पूजयित्वार्पयेत्ततः ।
पवित्रकं समस्ताध्वपरिपूर्णत्वभावनात् ॥ 138
28.m: Having first worshipped it according to the special injunction, one should then offer / the sacred thread, through the contemplation of the complete fullness of all the paths, // 138

28.s:
gurvātmanorjānunābhikaṇṭhamūrdhāntagaṃ ca vā /
tato mahotsavaḥ kāryo gurupūjāpuraḥsaraḥ // 139
28.d:
गुर्वात्मनोर्जानुनाभिकण्ठमूर्धान्तगं च वा ।
ततो महोत्सवः कार्यो गुरुपूजापुरःसरः ॥ 139
28.m: reaching down to the knees, navel, throat, or head of the guru and oneself. / Then a great festival must be celebrated, preceded by worship of the guru. // 139

28.s:
tarpyāḥ śāsanagāḥ sarve dakṣiṇāvastrabhojanaiḥ /
mahotsavaḥ prakartavyo gītanṛttātmako mahān // 140
28.d:
तर्प्याः शासनगाः सर्वे दक्षिणावस्त्रभोजनैः ।
महोत्सवः प्रकर्तव्यो गीतनृत्तात्मको महान् ॥ 140
28.m: All followers of the teaching should be gratified with fees, garments, and food; / a great festival consisting of song and dance should be performed, // 140

28.s:
cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ vāpyalābhataḥ /
tadante kṣamayeddevaṃ maṇḍalādi visarjayet // 141
28.d:
चातुर्मास्यं सप्तदिनं त्रिदिनं वाप्यलाभतः ।
तदन्ते क्षमयेद्देवं मण्डलादि विसर्जयेत् ॥ 141
28.m: lasting four months, seven days, or three days if [resources are] lacking. / At its end, one should ask the Lord's forgiveness, and dismiss the maṇḍala and other items, // 141

28.s:
vahniṃ ca paścātkartavyaścakrayāgaḥ puroditaḥ /
māse māse caturmāse varṣe vāpi pavitrakam // 142
28.d:
वह्निं च पश्चात्कर्तव्यश्चक्रयागः पुरोदितः ।
मासे मासे चतुर्मासे वर्षे वापि पवित्रकम् ॥ 142
28.m: and the fire; and afterwards the previously explained sacrifice of the circle (cakrayāga) is to be performed. / Every month, every four months, or once a year, the sacred thread [rite] // 142

28.s:
sarvathaiva prakartavyaṃ yathāvibhavavistaram /
vittābhāve punaḥ kāryaṃ kāśairapi kuśombhitaiḥ // 143
28.d:
सर्वथैव प्रकर्तव्यं यथाविभवविस्तरम् ।
वित्ताभावे पुनः कार्यं काशैरपि कुशोम्भितैः ॥ 143
28.m: is by all means to be performed according to the extent of one's wealth. / But in the absence of wealth, it should still be performed, even with kāśa or kuśa grasses woven together. // 143

28.s:
sati vitte punaḥ śāṭhyaṃ vyādhaye narakāya ca /
nityapūjāsu pūrṇatvaṃ parvapūjāprapūraṇāt // 144
28.d:
सति वित्ते पुनः शाठ्यं व्याधये नरकाय च ।
नित्यपूजासु पूर्णत्वं पर्वपूजाप्रपूरणात् ॥ 144
28.m: If wealth exists, however, deceitfulness leads to disease and hell. / Fullness in the regular daily rites is due to the completion through the junction worship; // 144

28.s:
tatrāpi paripūrṇatvaṃ pavitrakasamarcanāt /
pavitrakavilope tu prāyaścittaṃ japetsudhīḥ // 145
28.d:
तत्रापि परिपूर्णत्वं पवित्रकसमर्चनात् ।
पवित्रकविलोपे तु प्रायश्चित्तं जपेत्सुधीः ॥ 145
28.m: and complete fullness even in that is through the worship of the sacred thread. / If the sacred thread rite is omitted, the wise one should recite an expiation, // 145

28.s:
suśuddhaḥ sanpunaḥ kuryādityājñā parameśituḥ /
atha triśirasi prokto likhyate tadvidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ // 146
28.d:
सुशुद्धः सन्पुनः कुर्यादित्याज्ञा परमेशितुः ।
अथ त्रिशिरसि प्रोक्तो लिख्यते तद्विधिः स्फुटः ॥ 146
28.m: and becoming thoroughly purified, perform it again: such is the command of the Supreme Lord. / Now that clear rite taught in the Triśirobhairava is written. // 146

28.s:
triprameyasya śaivasya pañcapañcātmakasya vā /
daśāṣṭādaśabhedasya ṣaṭsrotasa ihocyate // 147
28.d:
त्रिप्रमेयस्य शैवस्य पञ्चपञ्चात्मकस्य वा ।
दशाष्टादशभेदस्य षट्स्रोतस इहोच्यते ॥ 147
28.m: For the Śaiva doctrine consisting of three objects of knowledge, or comprising five times five [categories], / divided into ten and eighteen, having six streams, [the ritual] is stated here. // 147

28.s:
ye narāḥ samayabhraṣṭā guruśāstrādidūṣakāḥ /
nityanaimittikādyanyaparvasandhivivarjitāḥ // 148
28.d:
ये नराः समयभ्रष्टा गुरुशास्त्रादिदूषकाः ।
नित्यनैमित्तिकाद्यन्यपर्वसन्धिविवर्जिताः ॥ 148
28.m: Those men who have fallen from the rule, who revile the guru, the scriptures, and the like, / who are devoid of the daily, occasional, and other rites at festive junctures, // 148

28.s:
akāmāt kāmato vāpi sūkṣmapāpapravartinaḥ /
teṣāṃ praśamanārthāya pavitraṃ kriyate śive // 149
28.d:
अकामात् कामतो वापि सूक्ष्मपापप्रवर्तिनः ।
तेषां प्रशमनार्थाय पवित्रं क्रियते शिवे ॥ 149
28.m: or who commit subtle sins involuntarily or voluntarily— / for their pacification, the pavitraka rite is performed unto Śiva. // 149

28.s:
śrāvaṇādau kārtikānte śuklapakṣe śubhaprade /
natu duḥkhaprade kṛṣṇe kartṛrāṣṭranṛpādiṣu // 150
28.d:
श्रावणादौ कार्तिकान्ते शुक्लपक्षे शुभप्रदे ।
नतु दुःखप्रदे कृष्णे कर्तृराष्ट्रनृपादिषु ॥ 150
28.m: In the bright fortnight, which bestows auspiciousness, beginning in Śrāvaṇa and ending in Kārtika, / and not in the dark fortnight, which brings distress upon the patron, the realm, the king, and others. // 150

28.s:
pāṭṭasūtraṃ tu kauśeyaṃ kārpāsaṃ kṣaumameva ca /
cāturāśramikāṇāṃ tu subhruvā kartitokṣitam // 151
28.d:
पाट्टसूत्रं तु कौशेयं कार्पासं क्षौममेव च ।
चातुराश्रमिकाणां तु सुभ्रुवा कर्तितोक्षितम् ॥ 151
28.m: Silk thread, tussar silk, cotton, and flax— / spun and sprinkled by fair-browed women belonging to the four stages of life. // 151

28.s:
tridhā tu triguṇīkṛtya mānasaṃkhyāṃ tu kārayet /
aṣṭottaraṃ tantuśataṃ tadardhaṃ vā tadardhakam // 152
28.d:
त्रिधा तु त्रिगुणीकृत्य मानसंख्यां तु कारयेत् ।
अष्टोत्तरं तन्तुशतं तदर्धं वा तदर्धकम् ॥ 152
28.m: Folding it threefold and making it three-ply, one should establish the measure and count: / one hundred and eight threads, or half that, or half of that. // 152

28.s:
hrāsastu pūrvasaṃkhyāyā daśabhirdaśabhiḥ kramāt /
navabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ saptaviṃśatyā vā śivāditaḥ // 153
28.d:
ह्रासस्तु पूर्वसंख्याया दशभिर्दशभिः क्रमात् ।
नवभिः पञ्चभिः सप्तविंशत्या वा शिवादितः ॥ 153
28.m: The reduction from the initial number is by tens in succession, / or by nine, by five, or by twenty-seven, beginning from Śiva. // 153

28.s:
yādṛśastantuvinyāso granthīnkuryāttu tāvataḥ /
catuḥsamaviliptāṃstānathavā kuṅkumena tu // 154
28.d:
यादृशस्तन्तुविन्यासो ग्रन्थीन्कुर्यात्तु तावतः ।
चतुःसमविलिप्तांस्तानथवा कुङ्कुमेन तु ॥ 154
28.m: However many the arrangement of threads may be, one should tie that many knots, / anointed with catuḥsama unguent or with saffron. // 154

28.s:
vyakte jānutaṭāntaṃ syālliṅge pīṭhāvasānakam /
arcāsu śobhanaṃ mūrghni tritattvaparikalpanāt // 155
28.d:
व्यक्ते जानुतटान्तं स्याल्लिङ्गे पीठावसानकम् ।
अर्चासु शोभनं मूर्घ्नि त्रितत्त्वपरिकल्पनात् ॥ 155
28.m: On an anthropomorphic image it should reach the knees; on a liṅga, ending at the pedestal; / on images it looks splendid at the head, owing to the configuration of the three principles. // 155

28.s:
dvādaśagranthiśaktīnāṃ brahmavaktrārciṣāmapi /
vidyāpīṭhe cale liṅge sthaṇḍile ca gurorgaṇe // 156
28.d:
द्वादशग्रन्थिशक्तीनां ब्रह्मवक्त्रार्चिषामपि ।
विद्यापीठे चले लिङ्गे स्थण्डिले च गुरोर्गणे ॥ 156
28.m: There are twelve knots for the powers, and also for the flames of the faces of the Brahmans; / on the Vidyāpīṭha, on the movable liṅga, on the bare ground, and on the assembly of the guru, // 156

28.s:
ghaṇṭāyāṃ sruksruve śiṣyaliṅgiṣu dvāratoraṇe /
svadehe vahnipīṭhe ca yathāśobhaṃ tadiṣyate // 157
28.d:
घण्टायां स्रुक्स्रुवे शिष्यलिङ्गिषु द्वारतोरणे ।
स्वदेहे वह्निपीठे च यथाशोभं तदिष्यते ॥ 157
28.m: on the bell, on the ladle and spoon, on disciples and ascetics, on the door and archway, / on one's own body, and on the fire altar, it is desired according to propriety. // 157

28.s:
prāsāde yāgagehe ca kārayennavaraṅgikam /
vidyāpīṭhe tu khaśarāḥ pratimāliṅgapīṭhagam // 158
28.d:
प्रासादे यागगेहे च कारयेन्नवरङ्गिकम् ।
विद्यापीठे तु खशराः प्रतिमालिङ्गपीठगम् ॥ 158
28.m: On the temple and on the sacrificial pavilion, one should make it with nine colors; / on the Vidyāpīṭha, fifty; on the image, the liṅga, and the pedestal, // 158

28.s:
vasuvedaṃ ca ghaṇṭāyāṃ śarākṣyaṣṭādaśa sruve /
vedākṣi sruci ṣaṭtriṃśat prāsāde maṇḍape raviḥ // 159
28.d:
वसुवेदं च घण्टायां शराक्ष्यष्टादश स्रुवे ।
वेदाक्षि स्रुचि षट्त्रिंशत् प्रासादे मण्डपे रविः ॥ 159
28.m: forty-eight; on the bell, twenty-five; eighteen on the ladle; / twenty-four on the spoon; thirty-six on the temple; twelve on the pavilion; // 159

28.s:
rasendu snānagehe'bdhinetre dhyānagṛhe gurau /
sapta sādhakagāḥ pañca putrake sapta sāmaye // 160
28.d:
रसेन्दु स्नानगेहेऽब्धिनेत्रे ध्यानगृहे गुरौ ।
सप्त साधकगाः पञ्च पुत्रके सप्त सामये ॥ 160
28.m: sixteen in the bath-house; twenty-four in the chamber of meditation; on the guru / seven; five assigned to the adept; seven on the spiritual son; on the initiate into the rule // 160

28.s:
catvāro'thānyaśāstrasthe śiṣye pañcakamucyate /
liṅgināṃ kevalo granthistoraṇe daśa kalpayet // 161
28.d:
चत्वारोऽथान्यशास्त्रस्थे शिष्ये पञ्चकमुच्यते ।
लिङ्गिनां केवलो ग्रन्थिस्तोरणे दश कल्पयेत् ॥ 161
28.m: four; on a disciple adhering to another scripture, a group of five is prescribed; / for ascetics, a single knot; on an archway, one should fashion ten; // 161

28.s:
dvāreṣvaṣṭau granthayaḥ syuḥ kṛtvetthaṃ tu pavitrakam /
pūjayitvā mantrajālaṃ tatsthatvātmasthate tataḥ // 162
28.d:
द्वारेष्वष्टौ ग्रन्थयः स्युः कृत्वेत्थं तु पवित्रकम् ।
पूजयित्वा मन्त्रजालं तत्स्थत्वात्मस्थते ततः ॥ 162
28.m: at the doors there should be eight knots. Having made the pavitraka in this manner, / and having worshipped the collection of mantras, then [realizing] their presence in that [thread] and in oneself, // 162

28.s:
pavitrakāṇāṃ saṃpādya kuryātsaṃpātasaṃskriyām /
tataḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dhyāyedbhairavaṃ chidrasākṣiṇam // 163
28.d:
पवित्रकाणां संपाद्य कुर्यात्संपातसंस्क्रियाम् ।
ततः संवत्सरं ध्यायेद्भैरवं छिद्रसाक्षिणम् ॥ 163
28.m: and having prepared the pavitrakas, one should perform the consecration by dropping [clarified butter]. / Then, one should meditate upon the Year, Bhairava, the witness to omissions. // 163

28.s:
dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ devi praṇamenmantrabhairavam /
oṃ samastakriyādoṣapūraṇeśa vrataṃ prati // 164
28.d:
दत्त्वा पूर्णाहुतिं देवि प्रणमेन्मन्त्रभैरवम् ।
ओं समस्तक्रियादोषपूरणेश व्रतं प्रति ॥ 164
28.m: Having offered the full oblation, O goddess, one should bow to Mantra-Bhairava: / 'Om, Lord who makes whole the defects of all rites! In regard to my vow, // 164

28.s:
yatkiṃcidakṛtaṃ duṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vā mātṛnandana /
tatsarvaṃ mama deveśa tvatprasādātpraṇaśyatu // 165
28.d:
यत्किंचिदकृतं दुष्टं कृतं वा मातृनन्दन ।
तत्सर्वं मम देवेश त्वत्प्रसादात्प्रणश्यतु ॥ 165
28.m: whatever has been left undone, or done improperly, O delight of the Mother, / may all that perish through your grace, O Lord of gods! // 165

28.s:
sarvathā raśmicakreśa namastubhyaṃ prasīda me /
anena dadyāddevāya nimantraṇapavitrakam // 166
28.d:
सर्वथा रश्मिचक्रेश नमस्तुभ्यं प्रसीद मे ।
अनेन दद्याद्देवाय निमन्त्रणपवित्रकम् ॥ 166
28.m: In every way, O Lord of the wheel of rays, obeisance to you! Be pleased with me!' / With this [prayer], one should offer the invitation pavitraka to the deity. // 166

28.s:
yoginīkṣetramātṝṇāṃ baliṃ dadyāttato guruḥ /
pañcagavyaṃ caruṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ śiṣyaiḥ samantataḥ // 167
28.d:
योगिनीक्षेत्रमातॄणां बलिं दद्यात्ततो गुरुः ।
पञ्चगव्यं चरुं दन्तकाष्ठं शिष्यैः समन्ततः ॥ 167
28.m: Then the guru should offer oblations to the yoginīs, the fields, and the Mothers, / along with the five products of the cow, cooked oblation rice, and tooth-sticks through the disciples all around. // 167

28.s:
ācārya nidrāṃ kurvīta prātarutthāya cāhnikam /
tato vidhiṃ pūjayitvā pavitrāṇi samāharet // 168
28.d:
आचार्य निद्रां कुर्वीत प्रातरुत्थाय चाह्निकम् ।
ततो विधिं पूजयित्वा पवित्राणि समाहरेत् ॥ 168
28.m: Having eaten, the master should sleep; and having risen at dawn, [perform] the daily rite; / then, having worshipped according to rule, he should bring the pavitrakas. // 168

28.s:
dantakāṣṭhaṃ mṛcca dhātrī samṛddhātrī sahāmbunā /
catuḥsamaṃ ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ bhasma pañcasu yojayet // 169
28.d:
दन्तकाष्ठं मृच्च धात्री समृद्धात्री सहाम्बुना ।
चतुःसमं च तैः सार्धं भस्म पञ्चसु योजयेत् ॥ 169
28.m: Tooth-stick, clay, myrobalan, and wealthy emblic myrobalan together with water / and catuḥsama perfume—along with these, one should apply ash to the five. // 169

28.s:
prāgdakṣapaścimordhvasthavāmavaktreṣu vai kramāt /
pañcaitāni pavitrāṇi sthāpayecceśagocare // 170
28.d:
प्राग्दक्षपश्चिमोर्ध्वस्थवामवक्त्रेषु वै क्रमात् ।
पञ्चैतानि पवित्राणि स्थापयेच्चेशगोचरे ॥ 170
28.m: In succession on the east, south, west, upper, and north faces, / one should place these five pavitrakas in the domain of the Lord. // 170

28.s:
kuśedhma pañcagavyaṃ ca śarvāgre viniyojayet /
vāmāmṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ naivedyaṃ trividhaṃ tataḥ // 171
28.d:
कुशेध्म पञ्चगव्यं च शर्वाग्रे विनियोजयेत् ।
वामामृतादिसंयुक्तं नैवेद्यं त्रिविधं ततः ॥ 171
28.m: One should offer kuśa grass, firewood, and the five products of the cow before Śarva; / then the threefold food offering, joined with nectar of the left, and so forth. // 171

28.s:
dadyādasṛk tathā madyaṃ pānāni vividhāni ca /
tato homo mahākṣmājamāṃsaistilayutairatho // 172
28.d:
दद्यादसृक् तथा मद्यं पानानि विविधानि च ।
ततो होमो महाक्ष्माजमांसैस्तिलयुतैरथो ॥ 172
28.m: One should offer blood, liquor, and various drinks; / then the fire sacrifice with the flesh of the great tree combined with sesame seeds; or // 172

28.s:
tilairghṛtayutairyadvā taṇḍulairatha dhānyakaiḥ /
śarkarākhaṇḍasaṃyuktapañcāmṛtapariplutaiḥ // 173
28.d:
तिलैर्घृतयुतैर्यद्वा तण्डुलैरथ धान्यकैः ।
शर्कराखण्डसंयुक्तपञ्चामृतपरिप्लुतैः ॥ 173
28.m: with sesame seeds mixed with ghee, or with husked grains or other seeds, / mixed with pieces of sugar and drenched in the five nectars. // 173

28.s:
mūlaṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭoktaṃ triśaktau brahmavaktrakam /
arciṣāṃ tu śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet // 174
28.d:
मूलं सहस्रं साष्टोक्तं त्रिशक्तौ ब्रह्मवक्त्रकम् ।
अर्चिषां तु शतं साष्टं ततः पूर्णाहुतिं क्षिपेत् ॥ 174
28.m: The basic mantra is stated [to be recited] one thousand and eight times; for the three powers and the Brahman faces, / and for the flames, one hundred and eight; then one should cast the full oblation. // 174

28.s:
tato'ñjalau pavitraṃ tu gṛhītvā prapaṭhedidam /
akāmādathavā kāmādyanmayā na kṛtaṃ vibho // 175
28.d:
ततोऽञ्जलौ पवित्रं तु गृहीत्वा प्रपठेदिदम् ।
अकामादथवा कामाद्यन्मया न कृतं विभो ॥ 175
28.m: Then, taking the pavitraka in folded hands, one should recite this: / 'Whatever was not performed by me, O omnipresent Lord, involuntarily or voluntarily, // 175

28.s:
tadacchidraṃ mamāstvīśa pavitreṇa tavājñayā /
mūlamantraḥ pūrayeti kriyāniyamamityatha // 176
28.d:
तदच्छिद्रं ममास्त्वीश पवित्रेण तवाज्ञया ।
मूलमन्त्रः पूरयेति क्रियानियममित्यथ ॥ 176
28.m: may that become flawless for me, O Lord, through the pavitraka, by your command!' / Then the basic mantra, saying 'make whole the rule of action', // 176

28.s:
vauṣaḍantaṃ pavitraṃ ca dadyādbindvavasānakam /
nādāntaṃ samanāntaṃ cāpyunmanāntaṃ kramāttrayam // 177
28.d:
वौषडन्तं पवित्रं च दद्याद्बिन्द्ववसानकम् ।
नादान्तं समनान्तं चाप्युन्मनान्तं क्रमात्त्रयम् ॥ 177
28.m: ending with 'vauṣaṭ', and one should offer the pavitraka terminating at the point (bindu), / terminating at the resonance (nāda), terminating at samanā, and terminating at unmanā—three successively. // 177

28.s:
evaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ dadyādanulomena bhautikaḥ /
naiṣṭhikastu vilomena pavitrakacatuṣṭayam // 178
28.d:
एवं चतुष्टयं दद्यादनुलोमेन भौतिकः ।
नैष्ठिकस्तु विलोमेन पवित्रकचतुष्टयम् ॥ 178
28.m: Thus the householder should offer the four in the forward order; / but the perpetual celibate should offer the four pavitrakas in the reverse order. // 178

28.s:
yatkiñcidvividhaṃ vastracchatrālaṅkaraṇādikam /
tannivedyaṃ dīpamālāḥ suvarṇatilabhājanam // 179
28.d:
यत्किञ्चिद्विविधं वस्त्रच्छत्रालङ्करणादिकम् ।
तन्निवेद्यं दीपमालाः सुवर्णतिलभाजनम् ॥ 179
28.m: Whatever various garments, parasols, ornaments, and the like, / that food offering, rows of lamps, and a vessel of sesame with gold, // 179

28.s:
vastrayugmayutaṃ sarvasampūraṇanimittataḥ /
bhojanīyāḥ pūjanīyāḥ śivabhaktāstu śaktitaḥ // 180
28.d:
वस्त्रयुग्मयुतं सर्वसम्पूरणनिमित्ततः ।
भोजनीयाः पूजनीयाः शिवभक्तास्तु शक्तितः ॥ 180
28.m: along with a pair of cloths, for the purpose of completing everything— / the devotees of Śiva should be fed and honoured according to one's capacity. // 180

28.s:
catustridvyekamāsādidinaikāntaṃ mahotsavam /
kuryāttato na vrajeyuranyasthānaṃ kadācana // 181
28.d:
चतुस्त्रिद्व्येकमासादिदिनैकान्तं महोत्सवम् ।
कुर्यात्ततो न व्रजेयुरन्यस्थानं कदाचन ॥ 181
28.m: One should hold a great festival lasting four, three, two, or one month, down to a single day; / during that time, they should never depart for another place. // 181

28.s:
tatastu daiśikaḥ pūjyo gāmasmai kṣīriṇīṃ navām /
dadyātsuvarṇaratnādirupyavastravibhūṣitām // 182
28.d:
ततस्तु दैशिकः पूज्यो गामस्मै क्षीरिणीं नवाम् ।
दद्यात्सुवर्णरत्नादिरुप्यवस्त्रविभूषिताम् ॥ 182
28.m: Then the spiritual guide is to be worshipped; one should give him a fresh milch cow / adorned with gold, gems, silver, and cloth. // 182

28.s:
vadedguruśca saṃpūrṇo vidhistava bhavatviti /
vaktavyaṃ devadevasya punarāgamanāya ca // 183
28.d:
वदेद्गुरुश्च संपूर्णो विधिस्तव भवत्विति ।
वक्तव्यं देवदेवस्य पुनरागमनाय च ॥ 183
28.m: And the guru should say: 'May your rite be complete!' / And words must be spoken for the return of the God of gods. // 183

28.s:
tato visarjanaṃ kāryaṃ guptamābharaṇādikam /
naivedyaṃ gururādāya yāgārthe tanniyojayet // 184
28.d:
ततो विसर्जनं कार्यं गुप्तमाभरणादिकम् ।
नैवेद्यं गुरुरादाय यागार्थे तन्नियोजयेत् ॥ 184
28.m: Then the dismissal is to be performed; taking the concealed ornaments and the like / and the food offering, the guru should employ it for the sacrifice. // 184

28.s:
caturṇāmapi sāmānyaṃ pavitrakamiti smṛtam /
nāsmādvrataṃ paraṃ kiñcit kā vāsya stutirucyate // 185
28.d:
चतुर्णामपि सामान्यं पवित्रकमिति स्मृतम् ।
नास्माद्व्रतं परं किञ्चित् का वास्य स्तुतिरुच्यते ॥ 185
28.m: This pavitraka rite is held to be common to all four [castes]; / there is no observance higher than this—what praise can be spoken of it? // 185

28.s:
śeṣaṃ tvagādhe vāryoghe kṣipenna sthāpayetsthiram /
atha naimittikavidhiryaḥ purāsūtrito mayā // 186
28.d:
शेषं त्वगाधे वार्योघे क्षिपेन्न स्थापयेत्स्थिरम् ।
अथ नैमित्तिकविधिर्यः पुरासूत्रितो मया ॥ 186
28.m: The remains one should throw into a deep current of water, and not let them remain in place. / Now the occasional rite that was previously outlined by me // 186

28.s:
sa bhaṇyate tatra kāryā devasyārcā viśeṣataḥ /
cakrayāgaśca kartavyaḥ pūrvoktavidhinā budhaiḥ // 187
28.d:
स भण्यते तत्र कार्या देवस्यार्चा विशेषतः ।
चक्रयागश्च कर्तव्यः पूर्वोक्तविधिना बुधैः ॥ 187
28.m: is explained: in that rite, special worship of the deity is to be performed, / and the sacrifice of the wheel is to be performed by the wise according to the previously stated rule. // 187

28.s:
tatra yadyannijābhīṣṭabhogamokṣopakārakam /
pāramparyeṇa sākṣādvā bhaveccidacidātmakam // 188
28.d:
तत्र यद्यन्निजाभीष्टभोगमोक्षोपकारकम् ।
पारम्पर्येण साक्षाद्वा भवेच्चिदचिदात्मकम् ॥ 188
28.m: Therein, whatever aids one's desired enjoyment and liberation, / whether indirectly or directly, whether having the nature of consciousness or insentience, // 188

28.s:
tatpūjyaṃ tadupāyāśca pūjyāstanmayatāptaye /
tadupāyo'pi saṃpūjyo mūrtikālakriyādikaḥ // 189
28.d:
तत्पूज्यं तदुपायाश्च पूज्यास्तन्मयताप्तये ।
तदुपायोऽपि संपूज्यो मूर्तिकालक्रियादिकः ॥ 189
28.m: that is to be worshipped, and its means are to be worshipped in order to attain identity with it; / the means to that, too, such as the physical form, time, and action, should be thoroughly worshipped. // 189

28.s:
upeyasūtisāmarthyamupāyatvaṃ tadarcanāt /
tadrūpatanmayībhāvādupeyaṃ śīghramāpnuyāt // 190
28.d:
उपेयसूतिसामर्थ्यमुपायत्वं तदर्चनात् ।
तद्रूपतन्मयीभावादुपेयं शीघ्रमाप्नुयात् ॥ 190
28.m: The nature of a means is the capacity to produce the end; through worshipping that, / by absorption into and identification with its nature, one quickly attains the end. // 190

28.s:
yathā yathā ca naikaṭyamupāyeṣu tathā tathā /
avaśyaṃbhāvi kāryatvaṃ viśeṣāccārcanādike // 191
28.d:
यथा यथा च नैकट्यमुपायेषु तथा तथा ।
अवश्यंभावि कार्यत्वं विशेषाच्चार्चनादिके ॥ 191
28.m:
And in proportion as there is closeness to the means,
just so is its indispensability, especially in worship and the like.

28.s:
jñānasya kasyacitprāptirbhogamokṣopakāriṇaḥ /
yadā tanmukhyamevoktaṃ naimittikadinaṃ budhaiḥ // 192
28.d:
ज्ञानस्य कस्यचित्प्राप्तिर्भोगमोक्षोपकारिणः ।
यदा तन्मुख्यमेवोक्तं नैमित्तिकदिनं बुधैः ॥ 192
28.m:
When any attainment of knowledge occurs that is conducive to enjoyment and liberation,
that very day has been declared by the wise to be the primary occasion for occasional rites.

28.s:
tadupāyaḥ śāstramatra vaktāpyaupayiko guruḥ /
tadvidyo'pi gurubhrātā saṃvādājjñānadāyakaḥ // 193
28.d:
तदुपायः शास्त्रमत्र वक्ताप्यौपयिको गुरुः ।
तद्विद्योऽपि गुरुभ्राता संवादाज्ज्ञानदायकः ॥ 193
28.m:
The means to it is scripture here, and the speaker, the guru, is also the instrumental means;
and the guru's brother who knows that [teaching] is also a giver of knowledge through dialogue.

28.s:
guroḥ patnī tathā bhrātā putra ityādiko gaṇaḥ /
na yonisaṃbandhavaśādvidyāsaṃbandhajastu saḥ // 194
28.d:
गुरोः पत्नी तथा भ्राता पुत्र इत्यादिको गणः ।
न योनिसंबन्धवशाद्विद्यासंबन्धजस्तु सः ॥ 194
28.m:
The guru's wife, brother, son, and the rest of the group
arise not by virtue of physical connection, but by connection through spiritual knowledge.

28.s:
vīryāruṇaparīṇāmadehāhantāpratiṣṭhitāḥ /
dehopakārasantānā jñāteye pariniṣṭhitāḥ // 195
28.d:
वीर्यारुणपरीणामदेहाहन्ताप्रतिष्ठिताः ।
देहोपकारसन्ताना ज्ञातेये परिनिष्ठिताः ॥ 195
28.m:
Those who are anchored in an ego-sense identified with the body, which is a transformation of semen and ovum,
maintain lineages of bodily benefit and are firmly established in kinship relations.

28.s:
tathāca smṛtiśāstreṣu santaterdāyahāritā /
yuktaiva tāvānsa hyukto bhedāddūrāntikatvataḥ // 196
28.d:
तथाच स्मृतिशास्त्रेषु सन्ततेर्दायहारिता ।
युक्तैव तावान्स ह्युक्तो भेदाद्दूरान्तिकत्वतः ॥ 196
28.m:
And so in the legal treatises the inheritance of an estate is given to the lineage;
that is entirely fitting, for that [relation] has been stated according to divisions of distance and proximity.

28.s:
ye tu tyaktaśarīrāsthā bodhāhambhāvabhāginaḥ /
bodhopakārasantānadvayātte bandhutājuṣaḥ // 197
28.d:
ये तु त्यक्तशरीरास्था बोधाहम्भावभागिनः ।
बोधोपकारसन्तानद्वयात्ते बन्धुताजुषः ॥ 197
28.m:
Those, however, who have abandoned clinging to the body and partake of the I-consciousness of awareness
enjoy kinship because of the two continuities of benefit to awareness.

28.s:
tatretthaṃ prāgyadā paśyecchaktyunmīlitadṛkkriyaḥ /
dehastāvadayaṃ pūrvapūrvopādānanirmitaḥ // 198
28.d:
तत्रेत्थं प्राग्यदा पश्येच्छक्त्युन्मीलितदृक्क्रियः ।
देहस्तावदयं पूर्वपूर्वोपादाननिर्मितः ॥ 198
28.m:
In this regard, when earlier one sees with the power of vision and action awakened:
this body is produced from preceding material causes;

28.s:
ātmā vikārarahitaḥ śāśvatatvādahetukaḥ /
svātantryāt punarātmīyādayaṃ channa iva sthitaḥ // 199
28.d:
आत्मा विकाररहितः शाश्वतत्वादहेतुकः ।
स्वातन्त्र्यात् पुनरात्मीयादयं छन्न इव स्थितः ॥ 199
28.m:
the Self is free of modification, and, being eternal, has no cause;
yet, through its own absolute autonomy, it remains as if concealed,

28.s:
punaśca prakaṭībhūya bhairavībhāvabhājanam /
tatrāsya prakaṭībhāve bhuktimuktyātmake bhṛśam // 200
28.d:
पुनश्च प्रकटीभूय भैरवीभावभाजनम् ।
तत्रास्य प्रकटीभावे भुक्तिमुक्त्यात्मके भृशम् ॥ 200
28.m:
and having become manifest once again, it is the vessel of the state of Bhairava.
In that manifestation of it, whose nature is enjoyment and liberation,
whatever appropriate means exists is exceedingly this continuity of knowledge.

28.s:
ya upāyaḥ samucito jñānasantāna eṣa saḥ /
kramasphuṭībhavattādṛksadṛśajñānadhārayā // 201
28.d:
य उपायः समुचितो ज्ञानसन्तान एष सः ।
क्रमस्फुटीभवत्तादृक्सदृशज्ञानधारया ॥ 201
28.m:
By a stream of similar knowledge of such a kind becoming gradually manifest,
what is to be attained is quickly gained, because of the melting away of alien elements.

28.s:
galadvijātīyatayā prāpyaṃ śīghraṃ hi labhyate /
evaṃ cānādisaṃsārocitavijñānasantateḥ // 202
28.d:
गलद्विजातीयतया प्राप्यं शीघ्रं हि लभ्यते ।
एवं चानादिसंसारोचितविज्ञानसन्ततेः ॥ 202
28.m:
And so, upon the destruction of the continuity of consciousness suited to beginningless transmigration,
transmundane knowledge assumes a different continuity.

28.s:
dhvaṃse lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ santānāntaratāṃ śrayet /
asaṃsārocitodāratathāvijñānasantateḥ // 203
28.d:
ध्वंसे लोकोत्तरं ज्ञानं सन्तानान्तरतां श्रयेत् ।
असंसारोचितोदारतथाविज्ञानसन्ततेः ॥ 203
28.m:
The primary, first cause of such an exalted continuity of consciousness suited to non-transmigration
is that consciousness of the guru residing in oneself, clearly because of the complete transfer of his specific qualities into it.

28.s:
kāraṇaṃ mukhyamādyaṃ tadguruvijñānamātmagam /
atyantaṃ svaviśeṣāṇāṃ tatrārpaṇavaśāt sphuṭam // 204
28.d:
कारणं मुख्यमाद्यं तद्गुरुविज्ञानमात्मगम् ।
अत्यन्तं स्वविशेषाणां तत्रार्पणवशात् स्फुटम् ॥ 204

28.s:
upādānaṃ hi tadyuktaṃ dehabhede hi satyapi /
dehasantatigau bhedābhedau vijñānasantateḥ // 205
28.d:
उपादानं हि तद्युक्तं देहभेदे हि सत्यपि ।
देहसन्ततिगौ भेदाभेदौ विज्ञानसन्ततेः ॥ 205
28.m:
When a yogin imparts life to another's body and the like
without abandoning his own body, is he not the material cause of manifold consciousness?

28.s:
na tathātvāya yogīcchāviṣṭaśāvaśarīravat /
yoginaḥ paradehādijīvattāpādane nijam // 206
28.d:
न तथात्वाय योगीच्छाविष्टशावशरीरवत् ।
योगिनः परदेहादिजीवत्तापादने निजम् ॥ 206
28.m:
Therefore, because of the pre-eminence of the continuity of consciousness over physical lineage,
the lineage of the guru consists of each other, established in the knowledge of Śiva.

28.s:
dehamatyajato nānājñānopādānatā na kim /
tena vijñānasantānaprādhānyādyaunasantateḥ // 207
28.d:
देहमत्यजतो नानाज्ञानोपादानता न किम् ।
तेन विज्ञानसन्तानप्राधान्याद्यौनसन्ततेः ॥ 207
28.m:
This being established, the guru's group consists of three primary factors:
the cause, the auxiliary, and the effect of the single cause.

28.s:
anyonyaṃ gurusantāno yaḥ śivajñānaniṣṭhitaḥ /
itthaṃ sthite trayaṃ mukhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ sahakāri ca // 208
28.d:
अन्योन्यं गुरुसन्तानो यः शिवज्ञाननिष्ठितः ।
इत्थं स्थिते त्रयं मुख्यं कारणं सहकारि च ॥ 208
28.m:
The guru is said to be the cause here, and his wife is the auxiliary,
because without a consort he has no qualification for the sacrifice.

28.s:
ekakāraṇakāryaṃ ca vastvityeṣa gurorgaṇaḥ /
guruḥ kāraṇamatroktaṃ tatpatnī sahakāriṇī // 209
28.d:
एककारणकार्यं च वस्त्वित्येष गुरोर्गणः ।
गुरुः कारणमत्रोक्तं तत्पत्नी सहकारिणी ॥ 209
28.m:
Even without an external consort, one has the power of the exalted inner consciousness;
just as a yogin has capacity even without an auxiliary.

28.s:
yato niḥśaktikasyāsya na yāge'dhikṛtirbhavet /
antaḥsthodārasaṃvittiśakterbāhyāṃ vināpi tām // 210
28.d:
यतो निःशक्तिकस्यास्य न यागेऽधिकृतिर्भवेत् ।
अन्तःस्थोदारसंवित्तिशक्तेर्बाह्यां विनापि ताम् ॥ 210
28.m:
Brothers would be those born of the same [cause], and whoever is similar to that [is likewise one].
Furthermore, through the connection of succession, the lineage of gurus is also described.

28.s:
sāmarthyaṃ yogino yadvadvināpi sahakāriṇam /
ekajanyā bhrātaraḥ syustatsadṛgyastu ko'pi saḥ // 211
28.d:
सामर्थ्यं योगिनो यद्वद्विनापि सहकारिणम् ।
एकजन्या भ्रातरः स्युस्तत्सदृग्यस्तु कोऽपि सः ॥ 211
28.m:
This primary lineage is to be worshipped and honoured at all times.
And on the birth, initiation, and death of the guru and the others,

28.s:
punaḥ paramparāyogādguruvargo'pi bhaṇyate /
mukhya eṣa tu santānaḥ pūjyo mānyaśca sarvadā // 212
28.d:
पुनः परम्परायोगाद्गुरुवर्गोऽपि भण्यते ।
मुख्य एष तु सन्तानः पूज्यो मान्यश्च सर्वदा ॥ 212
28.m:
that day is indeed the cause of the body and other [instruments], which are the means to consciousness.
Thus one's own birthday is called a means to consciousness,

28.s:
gurvādīnāṃ ca sambhūtau dīkṣāyāṃ prāyaṇe'pi ca /
yadahastaddhi vijñānopāyadehādikāraṇam // 213
28.d:
गुर्वादीनां च सम्भूतौ दीक्षायां प्रायणेऽपि च ।
यदहस्तद्धि विज्ञानोपायदेहादिकारणम् ॥ 213
28.m:
