the cause of the body, which is the cause of such enjoyment, liberation, and so forth.
And the day on which a consecration such as initiation occurs for oneself,

28.s:
evaṃ svajanmadivaso vijñānopāya ucyate /
tādṛgbhogāpavargādihetordehasya kāraṇam // 214
28.d:
एवं स्वजन्मदिवसो विज्ञानोपाय उच्यते ।
तादृग्भोगापवर्गादिहेतोर्देहस्य कारणम् ॥ 214
28.m:
that would be the primary birthday, because of the birth of the continuity of knowledge.
One's own day of death, however, will be an occasional rite for others,

28.s:
dīkṣādikaśca saṃskāraḥ svātmano yatra cāhni tat /
bhavejjanmadinaṃ mukhyaṃ jñānasantānajanmataḥ // 215
28.d:
दीक्षादिकश्च संस्कारः स्वात्मनो यत्र चाह्नि तत् ।
भवेज्जन्मदिनं मुख्यं ज्ञानसन्तानजन्मतः ॥ 215
28.m:
since the dead one at that time becomes non-different from Śiva.
In that context, by way of digression, we explain clearly the true nature of death.

28.s:
svakaṃ mṛtidinaṃ yattu tadanyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati /
naimittikaṃ mṛto yasmācchivābhinnastadā bhavet // 216
28.d:
स्वकं मृतिदिनं यत्तु तदन्येषां भविष्यति ।
नैमित्तिकं मृतो यस्माच्छिवाभिन्नस्तदा भवेत् ॥ 216
28.m:
Though all-pervasive, Śiva, through the sealing of contraction fashioned by His own will,
partakes of various bodies under the sway of a torrent of actions with diverse fruits.

28.s:
tatra prasaṅgānmaraṇasvarūpaṃ brūmahe sphuṭam /
vyāpako'pi śivaḥ svecchākḷptasaṅkocamudraṇāt // 217
28.d:
तत्र प्रसङ्गान्मरणस्वरूपं ब्रूमहे स्फुटम् ।
व्यापकोऽपि शिवः स्वेच्छाकॢप्तसङ्कोचमुद्रणात् ॥ 217
28.m:
And partaking of a body consists merely in this: residing in the body within the womb,
there occurs the first rise of vital breathing from consciousness settled in the void.

28.s:
vicitraphalakarmaughavaśāttattaccharīrabhāk /
śarīrabhāktvaṃ caitāvadyattadgarbhasthadehagaḥ // 218
28.d:
विचित्रफलकर्मौघवशात्तत्तच्छरीरभाक् ।
शरीरभाक्त्वं चैतावद्यत्तद्गर्भस्थदेहगः ॥ 218
28.m:
Moreover, in the formation of the body within the womb, He alone is the Lord;
being uncontracted, He is the creator of the body and the rest, and therefore He is called the Lord.

28.s:
saṃvitteḥ śūnyarūḍhāyāḥ prathamaḥ prāṇanodayaḥ /
garbhasthadehanirmāṇe tasyaiveśvaratā punaḥ // 219
28.d:
संवित्तेः शून्यरूढायाः प्रथमः प्राणनोदयः ।
गर्भस्थदेहनिर्माणे तस्यैवेश्वरता पुनः ॥ 219
28.m:
That vital breath, having the nature of air, when the bodily machine has become firm,
moves about, impelled by the conscious Self, like air in a blacksmith's bellows.

28.s:
asaṅkocasya tanvādikartā teneśa ucyate /
sa vāyvātmā dṛḍhe tasmindehayantre cidātmanā // 220
28.d:
असङ्कोचस्य तन्वादिकर्ता तेनेश उच्यते ।
स वाय्वात्मा दृढे तस्मिन्देहयन्त्रे चिदात्मना ॥ 220
28.m:
Hence, like one awakened from deep sleep, it wakes up beforehand;
and gradually, along with the body, the vital functioning becomes stronger.

28.s:
preryamāṇo vicarati bhastrāyantragavāyuvat /
ataḥ prāggāḍhasaṃsuptotthitavatsa prabuddhyate // 221
28.d:
प्रेर्यमाणो विचरति भस्त्रायन्त्रगवायुवत् ।
अतः प्राग्गाढसंसुप्तोत्थितवत्स प्रबुद्ध्यते ॥ 221
28.m:
Even there, by the force of the destiny of karma, that vital functioning acquires senses,
because of an excess of touch-consciousness in the empty apertures.

28.s:
kramāddehena sākaṃ ca prāṇanā syādbalīyasī /
tatrāpi karmaniyatibalātsā prāṇanākṣatām // 222
28.d:
क्रमाद्देहेन साकं च प्राणना स्याद्बलीयसी ।
तत्रापि कर्मनियतिबलात्सा प्राणनाक्षताम् ॥ 222
28.m:
Thus, in this sequence, having his bodily and vital strength greatly nurtured,
residing in a body born of a womb or not born of a womb, he enjoys the karmically generated enjoyments.

28.s:
gṛhṇāti śūnyasuṣirasaṃvitsparśādhikatvataḥ /
evaṃ krameṇa saṃpuṣṭadehaprāṇabalo bhṛśam // 223
28.d:
गृह्णाति शून्यसुषिरसंवित्स्पर्शाधिकत्वतः ।
एवं क्रमेण संपुष्टदेहप्राणबलो भृशम् ॥ 223
28.m:
And it has been stated in the scripture named Gahvara by the Moon-crested Lord:
'Just as a householder, having built a house, occupies it,

28.s:
bhogānkarmakṛtānbhuṅkte yonyayonijadehagaḥ /
uktaṃ ca gahvarābhikhye śāstre śītāṃśumaulinā // 224
28.d:
भोगान्कर्मकृतान्भुङ्क्ते योन्ययोनिजदेहगः ।
उक्तं च गह्वराभिख्ये शास्त्रे शीतांशुमौलिना ॥ 224
28.m:
so the embodied soul, having made a body, devoid of the attributes of action and the rest,
possessing at first merely a slight pulsing, is also called without parts (niṣkala);

28.s:
yathā gṛhaṃ viniṣpādya gṛhī samadhitiṣṭhati /
tathā dehī tanuṃ kṛtvā kriyādiguṇavarjitaḥ // 225
28.d:
यथा गृहं विनिष्पाद्य गृही समधितिष्ठति ।
तथा देही तनुं कृत्वा क्रियादिगुणवर्जितः ॥ 225
28.m:
but when the reality of the senses and the rest has become manifest, it is declared to be with parts (sakala).'
This and more has been said in the venerable Gahvara; one should read much from that very work.

28.s:
kiñcitsphuraṇamātraḥ prāgniṣkalaḥ so'pi śabdyate /
sphuṭendriyāditattvastu sakalātmeti bhaṇyate // 226
28.d:
किञ्चित्स्फुरणमात्रः प्राग्निष्कलः सोऽपि शब्द्यते ।
स्फुटेन्द्रियादितत्त्वस्तु सकलात्मेति भण्यते ॥ 226
28.m:
When those karmas are exhausted, however, and the bodily machine undergoes deterioration,
the machine of the vital breath breaks down, and the body then becomes like a wall.

28.s:
ityādi śrīgahvaroktaṃ tata eva paṭhedbahu /
kṣaye tu karmaṇāṃ teṣāṃ dehayantre'nyathāgate // 227
28.d:
इत्यादि श्रीगह्वरोक्तं तत एव पठेद्बहु ।
क्षये तु कर्मणां तेषां देहयन्त्रेऽन्यथागते ॥ 227
28.m:
There are contraction and expansion in the channels in a reverse manner,
breaking, drying, or moisture, through the decrease or increase of wind, phlegm, and fire.

28.s:
prāṇayantraṃ vighaṭate dehaḥ syātkuḍyavattataḥ /
nāḍīcakreṣu saṅkocavikāsau viparītataḥ // 228
28.d:
प्राणयन्त्रं विघटते देहः स्यात्कुड्यवत्ततः ।
नाडीचक्रेषु सङ्कोचविकासौ विपरीततः ॥ 228
28.m:
Whatever destroys the previous constitution in such ways
is declared by the wise to be the breakdown of the bodily machine.

28.s:
bhaṅgaḥ śoṣaḥ klidirvātaśleṣmāgnyapacayoccayaiḥ /
ityevamādi yatkiñcit prāksaṃsthānopamardakam // 229
28.d:
भङ्गः शोषः क्लिदिर्वातश्लेष्माग्न्यपचयोच्चयैः ।
इत्येवमादि यत्किञ्चित् प्राक्संस्थानोपमर्दकम् ॥ 229
28.m:
When that machine has broken down, that consciousness assumes the nature of vital breathing
in another body, born of a womb or otherwise, variegated by karma.

28.s:
dehayantre vighaṭanaṃ tadevoktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ /
tasminvighaṭite yantre sā saṃvitprāṇanātmatām // 230
28.d:
देहयन्त्रे विघटनं तदेवोक्तं मनीषिभिः ।
तस्मिन्विघटिते यन्त्रे सा संवित्प्राणनात्मताम् ॥ 230
28.m:
That body then awakens like one risen from sleep.
For it too, enjoyment, its loss, and death occur just as before;

28.s:
gṛhṇāti yonije'nyatra vā dehe karmacitrite /
sa dehaḥ pratibudhyeta prasuptotthitavattadā // 231
28.d:
गृह्णाति योनिजेऽन्यत्र वा देहे कर्मचित्रिते ।
स देहः प्रतिबुध्येत प्रसुप्तोत्थितवत्तदा ॥ 231
28.m:
for these emissions, maintenances, and dissolutions are due to the power of karma,
and therefore they conform to the diversity of destiny, time, and so forth.

28.s:
tasyāpi bhogataddhānimṛtayaḥ prāgvadeva hi /
visṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārā ete karmabalādyataḥ // 232
28.d:
तस्यापि भोगतद्धानिमृतयः प्राग्वदेव हि ।
विसृष्टिस्थितिसंहारा एते कर्मबलाद्यतः ॥ 232
28.m:
Grace, however, which consists in cognition within one's own expanding essence,
how could it look to karma, destiny, and the like?

28.s:
ato niyatikālādivaicitryānuvidhāyinaḥ /
anugrahastu yaḥ so'yaṃ svasvarūpe vikasvare // 233
28.d:
अतो नियतिकालादिवैचित्र्यानुविधायिनः ।
अनुग्रहस्तु यः सोऽयं स्वस्वरूपे विकस्वरे ॥ 233
28.m:
Since karma, time, destiny, and the like have contraction as their very life,
how could they be the cause of this grace, whose nature is the destruction of contraction?

28.s:
jñaptyātmeti kathaṃ karmaniyatyādi pratīkṣate /
karmakālaniyatyādi yataḥ saṅkocajīvitam // 234
28.d:
ज्ञप्त्यात्मेति कथं कर्मनियत्यादि प्रतीक्षते ।
कर्मकालनियत्यादि यतः सङ्कोचजीवितम् ॥ 234
28.m:
And grace is differentiated as gradual or intense;
and this was previously explained at length, so what is the use of repetitions?

28.s:
saṅkocahānirūpe'sminkathaṃ heturanugrahe /
anugrahaśca kramikastīvraśceti vibhidyate // 235
28.d:
सङ्कोचहानिरूपेऽस्मिन्कथं हेतुरनुग्रहे ।
अनुग्रहश्च क्रमिकस्तीव्रश्चेति विभिद्यते ॥ 235
28.m:
Therefore, one whose bond of contraction has been burnt by initiation and the knowledge of Śiva
is Śiva alone at the end of the body, and has no remaining in another body.

28.s:
prāk caiṣa vistarātprokta iti kiṃ punaruktibhiḥ /
tena dīkṣāśivajñānadagdhasaṅkocabandhanaḥ // 236
28.d:
प्राक् चैष विस्तरात्प्रोक्त इति किं पुनरुक्तिभिः ।
तेन दीक्षाशिवज्ञानदग्धसङ्कोचबन्धनः ॥ 236
28.m: Even of those who have descended into the realities, following the command of Śaṅkara,

28.s:
dehānte śiva eveti nāsya dehāntarasthitiḥ /
ye'pi tattvāvatīrṇānāṃ śaṃkarājñānuvartinām // 237
28.d:
देहान्ते शिव एवेति नास्य देहान्तरस्थितिः ।
येऽपि तत्त्वावतीर्णानां शंकराज्ञानुवर्तिनाम् ॥ 237

28.s:
svayambhūmunidevarṣimanujādibhuvāṃ gṛhe /
mṛtāste tatpuraṃ prāpya pureśairdīkṣitāḥ kramāt // 238
28.d:
स्वयम्भूमुनिदेवर्षिमनुजादिभुवां गृहे ।
मृतास्ते तत्पुरं प्राप्य पुरेशैर्दीक्षिताः क्रमात् ॥ 238
28.m: Those who die in the abode of the self-born, sages, divine seers, men, and others, / reaching that realm, are initiated successively by the lords of the realm; // 238

28.s:
martye'vatīrya vā no vā śivaṃ yāntyapunarbhavāḥ /
tatra svayambhuvo dvedhā ke'pyanugrahatatparāḥ // 239
28.d:
मर्त्येऽवतीर्य वा नो वा शिवं यान्त्यपुनर्भवाः ।
तत्र स्वयम्भुवो द्वेधा केऽप्यनुग्रहतत्पराः ॥ 239
28.m: whether descending into the mortal world or not, free from rebirth, they go to Śiva. / Among them, the self-born are twofold: some intent upon bestowing grace, // 239

28.s:
ke'pi svakṛtyāyātāṃśasthānamātropasevinaḥ /
ye'nugrahārthamājñaptāsteṣu yo mriyate naraḥ // 240
28.d:
केऽपि स्वकृत्यायातांशस्थानमात्रोपसेविनः ।
येऽनुग्रहार्थमाज्ञप्तास्तेषु यो म्रियते नरः ॥ 240
28.m: And some [self-manifested abodes] are occupied merely as dwelling places for parts [of the divine] that have arrived on account of their own specific task. / A person who dies in the presence of those [manifestations] that are commanded to bestow grace // 240

28.s:
so'nugrahaṃ sphuṭaṃ yāti vinā martyāvatārataḥ /
yastu svakāryaṃ kurvāṇastatsthānaṃ nāṃśatastyajet // 241
28.d:
सोऽनुग्रहं स्फुटं याति विना मर्त्यावतारतः ।
यस्तु स्वकार्यं कुर्वाणस्तत्स्थानं नांशतस्त्यजेत् ॥ 241
28.m: clearly attains grace without having to descend into mortal [birth]. / But [as for a divinity] who, performing his own task, does not abandon that place with part [of himself], // 241

28.s:
yathā gaurī tapasyantī kaśmīreṣu guhāgatā /
tatraiva vā yathā dhyānoḍḍāre naraharirvibhuḥ // 242
28.d:
यथा गौरी तपस्यन्ती कश्मीरेषु गुहागता ।
तत्रैव वा यथा ध्यानोड्डारे नरहरिर्विभुः ॥ 242
28.m: just as Gaurī practicing tapas inside a cave in Kashmir, / or just as the omnipresent Narahari at Dhyānoḍḍāra in that very [country], // 242

28.s:
vitastāṃ nayato daityāṃstrāsayandṛpta utthitaḥ /
sāligrāme yathā viṣṇuḥ śivo vā svopabhoginaḥ // 243
28.d:
वितस्तां नयतो दैत्यांस्त्रासयन्दृप्त उत्थितः ।
सालिग्रामे यथा विष्णुः शिवो वा स्वोपभोगिनः ॥ 243
28.m: who, risen in majesty, terrified the Daityas as he brought the Vitastā; / or like Viṣṇu at Śāligrāma, or Śiva [in places] where they experience their own enjoyments; // 243

28.s:
tapasyantau badaryāṃ ca naranārāyaṇau tathā /
ityevamādayo devāḥ svakṛtyāṃśasthitāstathā // 244
28.d:
तपस्यन्तौ बदर्यां च नरनारायणौ तथा ।
इत्येवमादयो देवाः स्वकृत्यांशस्थितास्तथा ॥ 244
28.m: and likewise Nara and Nārāyaṇa practicing tapas at Badarī— / deities such as these who thus abide as a part [of themselves] for their own specific task, // 244

28.s:
ārādhitāḥ svocitaṃ tacchīghraṃ vidadhate phalam /
svakṛtyāṃśasthitānāṃ ca dhāmni ye'ntaṃ vrajanti te // 245
28.d:
आराधिताः स्वोचितं तच्छीघ्रं विदधते फलम् ।
स्वकृत्यांशस्थितानां च धाम्नि येऽन्तं व्रजन्ति ते ॥ 245
28.m: when worshiped, swiftly bestow the fruit appropriate to themselves. / And those who meet their end in the abode of those who abide as a part [of themselves] for their own specific task, // 245

28.s:
tatra bhogāṃstathā bhuktvā martyeṣvavatarantyapi /
martyāvatīrṇāste tattadaṃśakāstanmayāḥ punaḥ // 246
28.d:
तत्र भोगांस्तथा भुक्त्वा मर्त्येष्ववतरन्त्यपि ।
मर्त्यावतीर्णास्ते तत्तदंशकास्तन्मयाः पुनः ॥ 246
28.m: having enjoyed [various] enjoyments there, also descend among mortals. / Having descended as mortals, those portions of those [beings], composed of them, // 246

28.s:
taddīkṣājñānacaryādikramādyānti śivātmatām /
sthāvarādyāstiryagantāḥ paśavo'smindvaye mṛtāḥ // 247
28.d:
तद्दीक्षाज्ञानचर्यादिक्रमाद्यान्ति शिवात्मताम् ।
स्थावराद्यास्तिर्यगन्ताः पशवोऽस्मिन्द्वये मृताः ॥ 247
28.m: subsequently attain the state of Śiva by stages through initiation, knowledge, conduct, and the like in relation to that [deity]. / Immobile beings and the rest, ending with animals, who die in either of these two [types of places], // 247

28.s:
svakarmasaṃskriyāvedhāttalloke citratājuṣaḥ /
puṃsāṃ ca paśumātrāṇāṃ sālokyamavivekataḥ // 248
28.d:
स्वकर्मसंस्क्रियावेधात्तल्लोके चित्रताजुषः ।
पुंसां च पशुमात्राणां सालोक्यमविवेकतः ॥ 248
28.m: enjoy varied states in that world because of being penetrated by the latent impressions of their own karman. / And for mere bound souls among men, there is co-residence [with the deity] due to non-discrimination; // 248

28.s:
avivekastadviśeṣānunmeṣānmauḍhyatastathā /
sthāvarādyāstathābhāvamuttarottaratāṃ ca vā // 249
28.d:
अविवेकस्तद्विशेषानुन्मेषान्मौढ्यतस्तथा ।
स्थावराद्यास्तथाभावमुत्तरोत्तरतां च वा ॥ 249
28.m: non-discrimination [results] from the non-manifestation of its specific distinctions, as well as from delusion. / Immobile beings and the rest [obtain] that state or successively higher states; // 249

28.s:
prapadyante na te sākṣādrudratāṃ tāṃ kramātpunaḥ /
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇe nānātarukulākule // 250
28.d:
प्रपद्यन्ते न ते साक्षाद्रुद्रतां तां क्रमात्पुनः ।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णे नानातरुकुलाकुले ॥ 250
28.m: they do not attain that Rudrahood directly, but rather gradually in course of time. / In a [sanctuary] filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, crowded with various kinds of trees, // 250

28.s:
ityetadāgameṣūktaṃ tata eva pure pure /
kṣetramānaṃ bruve śrīmatsarvajñānādiṣūditam // 251
28.d:
इत्येतदागमेषूक्तं तत एव पुरे पुरे ।
क्षेत्रमानं ब्रुवे श्रीमत्सर्वज्ञानादिषूदितम् ॥ 251
28.m: so it is declared in the Āgamas; therefore, for each city, / I state the measure of the sacred field as taught in the venerable Sarvajñāna and other [texts]: // 251

28.s:
liṅgāddhastaśataṃ kṣetramācāryasthāpite sati /
svayambhūte sahasraṃ tu tadardhamṛṣiyojite // 252
28.d:
लिङ्गाद्धस्तशतं क्षेत्रमाचार्यस्थापिते सति ।
स्वयम्भूते सहस्रं तु तदर्धमृषियोजिते ॥ 252
28.m: The sacred field extends one hundred cubits from a liṅga installed by an ācārya; / but when it is self-manifested, a thousand; and half of that when established by a ṛṣi. // 252

28.s:
tattvavitsthāpite liṅge svayambhūsadṛśaṃ phalam /
atattvavidyadācāryo liṅgaṃ sthāpayate tadā // 253
28.d:
तत्त्ववित्स्थापिते लिङ्गे स्वयम्भूसदृशं फलम् ।
अतत्त्वविद्यदाचार्यो लिङ्गं स्थापयते तदा ॥ 253
28.m: At a liṅga installed by a knower of reality, the fruit is equal to a self-manifested one. / When an ācārya who does not know reality installs a liṅga, then // 253

28.s:
punarvidhirbhaveddoṣo hyanyathobhayadūṣakaḥ /
ahamanyaḥ parātmānyaḥ śivo'nya iti cenmatiḥ // 254
28.d:
पुनर्विधिर्भवेद्दोषो ह्यन्यथोभयदूषकः ।
अहमन्यः परात्मान्यः शिवोऽन्य इति चेन्मतिः ॥ 254
28.m: the rite must be performed again, for otherwise there would be a flaw defiling both. / If one has the notion: 'I am one, the supreme Self is another, Śiva is another,' // 254

28.s:
na mocayenna muktaśca sarvamātmamayaṃ yataḥ /
tasmāttattvavidā yadyatsthāpitaṃ liṅgamuttamam // 255
28.d:
न मोचयेन्न मुक्तश्च सर्वमात्ममयं यतः ।
तस्मात्तत्त्वविदा यद्यत्स्थापितं लिङ्गमुत्तमम् ॥ 255
28.m: he cannot liberate [others] nor is he himself liberated, since everything consists of the Self. / Therefore, whatever excellent liṅga is installed by a knower of reality, // 255

28.s:
tadevāyatanatvena saṃśrayedbhuktimuktaye /
uktaṃ śrīratnamālāyāṃ jñātvā kālamupasthitam // 256
28.d:
तदेवायतनत्वेन संश्रयेद्भुक्तिमुक्तये ।
उक्तं श्रीरत्नमालायां ज्ञात्वा कालमुपस्थितम् ॥ 256
28.m: that alone should be resorted to as a sanctuary for enjoyment and liberation. / It is stated in the venerable Ratnamālā: having recognized that one's time has arrived, // 256

28.s:
mokṣārthī na bhayaṃ gacchettyajeddehamaśaṅkitaḥ /
tīrthāyatanapuṇyeṣu kālaṃ vā vañcayetpriye // 257
28.d:
मोक्षार्थी न भयं गच्छेत्त्यजेद्देहमशङ्कितः ।
तीर्थायतनपुण्येषु कालं वा वञ्चयेत्प्रिये ॥ 257
28.m: the seeker of liberation should not succumb to fear, but cast off the body free from doubt; / or, O dear one, one may cheat death in holy places, sanctuaries, and sacred spots. // 257

28.s:
ayogināmayaṃ panthā yogī yogena vañcayet /
vañcane tvasamarthaḥ san kṣetramāyatanaṃ vrajet // 258
28.d:
अयोगिनामयं पन्था योगी योगेन वञ्चयेत् ।
वञ्चने त्वसमर्थः सन् क्षेत्रमायतनं व्रजेत् ॥ 258
28.m: This is the way for non-yogins; a yogin should cheat [death] through yoga. / But being unable to cheat it, one should go to a sacred field or a sanctuary; // 258

28.s:
tīrthe samāśrayāttasya vañcanaṃ tu vijāyate /
anena ca dharādyeṣu tattveṣvabhyāsayogataḥ // 259
28.d:
तीर्थे समाश्रयात्तस्य वञ्चनं तु विजायते ।
अनेन च धराद्येषु तत्त्वेष्वभ्यासयोगतः ॥ 259
28.m: by taking refuge in a holy place, however, the cheating of [death] does take place for him. / And by this means, through the application of practice on the tattvas beginning with earth, // 259

28.s:
tāvatsiddhijuṣo'pyuktā muktyai kṣetropayogitā /
samyagjñānini vṛttāntaḥ purastāttūpadekṣyate // 260
28.d:
तावत्सिद्धिजुषोऽप्युक्ता मुक्त्यै क्षेत्रोपयोगिता ।
सम्यग्ज्ञानिनि वृत्तान्तः पुरस्तात्तूपदेक्ष्यते ॥ 260
28.m: the usefulness of the sacred field for liberation is taught even for those who enjoy [merely] mundane spiritual accomplishments. / But the account regarding one possessed of complete knowledge will be taught later. // 260

28.s:
paśūnāmeṣa vṛttānto ye tu tattattvadīkṣitāḥ /
te tadīśasamīpatvaṃ yānti svaucityayogataḥ // 261
28.d:
पशूनामेष वृत्तान्तो ये तु तत्तत्त्वदीक्षिताः ।
ते तदीशसमीपत्वं यान्ति स्वौचित्ययोगतः ॥ 261
28.m: This is the account concerning bound souls. As for those who have received initiation into the various tattvas, / they attain proximity to the Lord of that [tattva] according to their own suitability. // 261

28.s:
yogyatāvaśasaṃjātā yasya yatraiva vāsanā /
sa tatraiva niyoktavyaḥ pureśāccordhvaśuddhibhāk // 262
28.d:
योग्यतावशसंजाता यस्य यत्रैव वासना ।
स तत्रैव नियोक्तव्यः पुरेशाच्चोर्ध्वशुद्धिभाक् ॥ 262
28.m: In whatever [tattva] one has a latent impression born under the sway of one's fitness, / he should be assigned right there, and subsequently receives purification above it from the lord of that city. // 262

28.s:
iti śrīpūrvakathitaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve'pica /
yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogānsa tatraiva niyojitaḥ // 263
28.d:
इति श्रीपूर्वकथितं श्रीमत्स्वायम्भुवेऽपिच ।
यो यत्राभिलषेद्भोगान्स तत्रैव नियोजितः ॥ 263
28.m: So it is declared in the venerable Pūrva [Mālinīvijayottara], and also in the venerable Svāyambhuva: / 'Whatever enjoyments one may desire in whatever place, he is assigned right there; // 263

28.s:
siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyādityādyanyatra varṇitam /
ye tu tattattvavijñānamantracaryādivartinaḥ // 264
28.d:
सिद्धिभाङ्मन्त्रसामर्थ्यादित्याद्यन्यत्र वर्णितम् ।
ये तु तत्तत्त्वविज्ञानमन्त्रचर्यादिवर्तिनः ॥ 264
28.m: he participates in accomplishment through the efficacy of the mantra,' etc., as described elsewhere. / But those wise ones who abide in the knowledge, mantra, conduct, and other practices of the various tattvas, // 264

28.s:
mṛtāste tatra tadrudrasayuktvaṃ yānti kovidāḥ /
teṣāṃ sayuktvaṃ yātānāmapi saṃskārato nijāt // 265
28.d:
मृतास्ते तत्र तद्रुद्रसयुक्त्वं यान्ति कोविदाः ।
तेषां सयुक्त्वं यातानामपि संस्कारतो निजात् ॥ 265
28.m: when they die, they attain unity with the Rudra of that [tattva]. / Even for those who have attained unity, on account of their own latent impressions, // 265

28.s:
tathā tathā vicitraḥ syādavatārastadaṃśataḥ /
siddhāntādau purāṇeṣu tathāca śrūyate bahu // 266
28.d:
तथा तथा विचित्रः स्यादवतारस्तदंशतः ।
सिद्धान्तादौ पुराणेषु तथाच श्रूयते बहु ॥ 266
28.m: there may be a descent as a portion of him in various ways. / And so it is frequently heard in the Siddhānta and other [texts], and in the Purāṇas, // 266

28.s:
tulye rudrāvatāratve citratvaṃ karmabhogayoḥ /
anekaśaktikhacitaṃ yato bhāvasya yadvapuḥ // 267
28.d:
तुल्ये रुद्रावतारत्वे चित्रत्वं कर्मभोगयोः ।
अनेकशक्तिखचितं यतो भावस्य यद्वपुः ॥ 267
28.m: that although the descent as Rudra is equal, there is diversity in action and enjoyment. / Because the nature of an entity is inlaid with manifold powers, // 267

28.s:
śaktibhyo'rthāntaraṃ naiṣa tatsamūhādṛte bhavet /
tena śaktisamūhākhyāt tasmādrudrādyadaṃśataḥ // 268
28.d:
शक्तिभ्योऽर्थान्तरं नैष तत्समूहादृते भवेत् ।
तेन शक्तिसमूहाख्यात् तस्माद्रुद्राद्यदंशतः ॥ 268
28.m: it cannot be a distinct reality from those powers, apart from their totality. / Therefore, from that Rudra, which is called an aggregate of powers, whatever portion // 268

28.s:
kṛtyaṃ taducitaṃ siddhyet so'ṃśo'vatarati sphuṭam /
ye cādharaprāptadīkṣāstadāsthānujjhitāḥ pare // 269
28.d:
कृत्यं तदुचितं सिद्ध्येत् सोऽंशोऽवतरति स्फुटम् ।
ये चाधरप्राप्तदीक्षास्तदास्थानुज्झिताः परे ॥ 269
28.m: can accomplish the task suitable to it—that portion clearly descends. / And those who have received initiation into a lower [tattva], but have not abandoned their devotion to it, // 269

28.s:
tattve mṛtāḥ kāṣṭhavatte'dhare'pyutkarṣabhāginaḥ /
ye tūjjhitatadutkarṣāste taduttarabhāginaḥ // 270
28.d:
तत्त्वे मृताः काष्ठवत्तेऽधरेऽप्युत्कर्षभागिनः ।
ये तूज्झिततदुत्कर्षास्ते तदुत्तरभागिनः ॥ 270
28.m: when they die in a higher tattva, like logs of wood, they attain preeminence in the lower [tattva] too. / But those who have abandoned [attachment to] that lower preeminence share in that higher [state]. // 270

28.s:
ye'pyūrdhvatattvadīkṣāste vinā tāvadvivekataḥ /
prāptādharāntā api taddīkṣāphalasubhāginaḥ // 271
28.d:
येऽप्यूर्ध्वतत्त्वदीक्षास्ते विना तावद्विवेकतः ।
प्राप्ताधरान्ता अपि तद्दीक्षाफलसुभागिनः ॥ 271
28.m: Even those initiated into a higher tattva who, lacking discernment, / have reached an inferior end, still partake fully of the fruit of that initiation. // 271

28.s:
atyaktāsthā hi te tatra dīkṣāyāmapi śāstritāt /
vinā vivekādāsthāṃ te śritā lokaprasiddhitaḥ // 272
28.d:
अत्यक्तास्था हि ते तत्र दीक्षायामपि शास्त्रितात् ।
विना विवेकादास्थां ते श्रिता लोकप्रसिद्धितः ॥ 272
28.m: For they have not abandoned devotion to that [higher tattva] in their initiation as prescribed by scripture, / [though] without discernment they had adopted devotion [to a lower deity] because of worldly convention. // 272

28.s:
paśumātrasya sālokyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ dīkṣitasya tu /
tatparasya tu sāyujyamityuktaṃ parameśinā // 273
28.d:
पशुमात्रस्य सालोक्यं सामीप्यं दीक्षितस्य तु ।
तत्परस्य तु सायुज्यमित्युक्तं परमेशिना ॥ 273
28.m: Co-residence belongs to the mere bound soul, but proximity belongs to the initiate; / union, however, belongs to the one devoted to Him: so it is taught by the Supreme Lord. // 273

28.s:
yastūrdhvaśāstragastatra tyaktāsthaḥ saṃśayena saḥ /
vrajannāyatanaṃ naiva phalaṃ kiñcitsamaśnute // 274
28.d:
यस्तूर्ध्वशास्त्रगस्तत्र त्यक्तास्थः संशयेन सः ।
व्रजन्नायतनं नैव फलं किञ्चित्समश्नुते ॥ 274
28.m: However, he who follows a higher scripture but abandons devotion to it out of doubt, / receives no fruit whatsoever when resorting to [that] sanctuary. // 274

28.s:
uktaṃ tadviṣayaṃ caitaddevadevena yadvṛthā /
dīkṣā jñānaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tasyetyādi savistaram // 275
28.d:
उक्तं तद्विषयं चैतद्देवदेवेन यद्वृथा ।
दीक्षा ज्ञानं तथा तीर्थं तस्येत्यादि सविस्तरम् ॥ 275
28.m: And on this subject, it has been stated at length by the God of gods: 'Useless / are initiation, knowledge, and likewise the holy place for him,' and so forth. // 275

28.s:
yastu tāvadayogyo'pi tathāste sa śivālaye /
paścādāsthānibandhena tāvadeva phalaṃ bhajet // 276
28.d:
यस्तु तावदयोग्योऽपि तथास्ते स शिवालये ।
पश्चादास्थानिबन्धेन तावदेव फलं भजेत् ॥ 276
28.m: Yet one who, even though unfit, resides in an abode of Śiva, / will subsequently, on account of devotion, obtain that very fruit. // 276

28.s:
nadīnagahradaprāyaṃ yacca puṇyaṃ na tanmṛtau /
utkṛṣṭaṃ tanmṛtānāṃ tu svargabhogopabhogitā // 277
28.d:
नदीनगह्रदप्रायं यच्च पुण्यं न तन्मृतौ ।
उत्कृष्टं तन्मृतानां तु स्वर्गभोगोपभोगिता ॥ 277
28.m: Whatever sacred place consists mainly of rivers, mountains, and lakes does not lead to the highest [fruit] upon death; / for those who die there, there is merely the experience of heavenly enjoyments. // 277

28.s:
ye punaḥ prāptavijñānavivekā maraṇāntike /
adharāyataneṣvāsthāṃ śritāste'tra tirohitāḥ // 278
28.d:
ये पुनः प्राप्तविज्ञानविवेका मरणान्तिके ।
अधरायतनेष्वास्थां श्रितास्तेऽत्र तिरोहिताः ॥ 278
28.m: Those, however, who have attained discernment and knowledge, but at the approach of death / adhere to lower sanctuaries, become obscured in this matter. // 278

28.s:
tajjñānadūṣaṇoktaṃ yatteṣāṃ syātkila pātakam /
tattatpureśadīkṣādikramānnaśyediti sthitiḥ // 279
28.d:
तज्ज्ञानदूषणोक्तं यत्तेषां स्यात्किल पातकम् ।
तत्तत्पुरेशदीक्षादिक्रमान्नश्येदिति स्थितिः ॥ 279
28.m: Whatever sin they incur that is described as a fault against that knowledge / will perish by stages through the initiation and other rites of the lords of those cities: such is the established rule. // 279

28.s:
dīkṣāyatanavijñānadūṣiṇo ye tu cetasā /
ācaranti ca tatte'tra sarve nirayagāminaḥ // 280
28.d:
दीक्षायतनविज्ञानदूषिणो ये तु चेतसा ।
आचरन्ति च तत्तेऽत्र सर्वे निरयगामिनः ॥ 280
28.m: Those, however, who mentally disparage initiation, sanctuaries, and knowledge / and act accordingly, all go to hell in this world. // 280

28.s:
jñānāyatanadīkṣādāvāsthābandhaparicyutiḥ /
vyāpāravyāhṛtairjñeyā tānyapi dvividhāni ca // 281
28.d:
ज्ञानायतनदीक्षादावास्थाबन्धपरिच्युतिः ।
व्यापारव्याहृतैर्ज्ञेया तान्यपि द्विविधानि च ॥ 281
28.m: A lapse in the bond of devotion toward knowledge, sanctuaries, initiation, and the like / is to be recognized by actions and words; and these are also of two kinds: // 281

28.s:
yāni jātucidapyeva svāsthye nodamiṣanpunaḥ /
asvāsthye dhātudoṣotthānyeva tadbhogamātrakam // 282
28.d:
यानि जातुचिदप्येव स्वास्थ्ये नोदमिषन्पुनः ।
अस्वास्थ्ये धातुदोषोत्थान्येव तद्भोगमात्रकम् ॥ 282
28.m: those that never manifested while in good health, / but arose in illness solely from a disorder of the bodily humors—they are merely an experience of that [illness]. // 282

28.s:
dhātudoṣācca saṃsārasaṃskārāste prabodhitāḥ /
chidragā api bhūyiṣṭhajñānadagdhā na rohiṇaḥ // 283
28.d:
धातुदोषाच्च संसारसंस्कारास्ते प्रबोधिताः ।
छिद्रगा अपि भूयिष्ठज्ञानदग्धा न रोहिणः ॥ 283
28.m: And from the disorder of bodily humors, those latent impressions of saṃsāra are awakened; / though finding an opening, being mostly burned by knowledge, they do not sprout. // 283

28.s:
ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ svāsthye'nunmiṣitāḥ sadā /
asvāsthye conmiṣantyete saṃskārāḥ śaktipātataḥ // 284
28.d:
ये तु कैवल्यभागीयाः स्वास्थ्येऽनुन्मिषिताः सदा ।
अस्वास्थ्ये चोन्मिषन्त्येते संस्काराः शक्तिपाततः ॥ 284
28.m: Those [impressions], however, that pertain to liberation never manifest during health, / but through the descent of power, these latent impressions do manifest during illness, // 284

28.s:
yataḥ sāṃsārikāḥ pūrvagāḍhābhyāsopasaṃskṛtāḥ /
ityūce bhujagādhīśastacchidreṣviti sūtrataḥ // 285
28.d:
यतः सांसारिकाः पूर्वगाढाभ्यासोपसंस्कृताः ।
इत्यूचे भुजगाधीशस्तच्छिद्रेष्विति सूत्रतः ॥ 285
28.m: because worldly [impressions] are reinforced by deep previous practice. / Thus the Lord of Serpents [Patañjali] taught in the sūtra: 'In the intervals thereof...' // 285

28.s:
ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ pratyayāste na jātucit /
abhyastāḥ saṃsṛterbhāvāttenaite śaktipātataḥ // 286
28.d:
ये तु कैवल्यभागीयाः प्रत्ययास्ते न जातुचित् ।
अभ्यस्ताः संसृतेर्भावात्तेनैते शक्तिपाततः ॥ 286
28.m: Those cognitions, however, that pertain to liberation have never been / cultivated because of the nature of transmigratory existence; therefore, they occur through the descent of power. // 286

28.s:
vyāpāravyāhṛtaistena dhātudoṣaprakopitaiḥ /
aprāptaniścayāmarśaiḥ suptamattopamānakaiḥ // 287
28.d:
व्यापारव्याहृतैस्तेन धातुदोषप्रकोपितैः ।
अप्राप्तनिश्चयामर्शैः सुप्तमत्तोपमानकैः ॥ 287
28.m: Therefore, through [states] brought about by activities, agitated by disturbances of bodily humours, / devoid of determinate reflective awareness, resembling sleep or intoxication, // 287

28.s:
viparītairapi jñānadīkṣāgurvādidūṣakaiḥ /
tirobhāvo na vijñeyo hṛdaye rūḍhyabhāvataḥ // 288
28.d:
विपरीतैरपि ज्ञानदीक्षागुर्वादिदूषकैः ।
तिरोभावो न विज्ञेयो हृदये रूढ्यभावतः ॥ 288
28.m: and even through contrary [states] reviling knowledge, initiation, the guru, and the like, / one should not understand that concealment occurs, because [these] have no root in the heart. // 288

28.s:
ata eva prabuddho'pi karmotthānbhogarūpiṇaḥ /
yamakiṅkarasarpādipratyayāndehago bhajet // 289
28.d:
अत एव प्रबुद्धोऽपि कर्मोत्थान्भोगरूपिणः ।
यमकिङ्करसर्पादिप्रत्ययान्देहगो भजेत् ॥ 289
28.m: For this very reason, even an awakened one, dwelling in the body, may experience / cognitions arising from karma that take the form of experiences—such as the messengers of Yama, serpents, and so on. // 289

28.s:
naitāvatā na mukto'sau mṛtirbhogo hi janmavat /
sthitivacca tato duḥkhasukhābhyāṃ maraṇaṃ dvidhā // 290
28.d:
नैतावता न मुक्तोऽसौ मृतिर्भोगो हि जन्मवत् ।
स्थितिवच्च ततो दुःखसुखाभ्यां मरणं द्विधा ॥ 290
28.m: Not by this much is he unliberated, for dying is an experience just like birth / and just like life; therefore death is twofold through pain and pleasure. // 290

28.s:
ato yathā prabuddhasya sukhaduḥkhavicitratāḥ /
sthitau na ghnanti muktatvaṃ maraṇe'pi tathaiva tāḥ // 291
28.d:
अतो यथा प्रबुद्धस्य सुखदुःखविचित्रताः ।
स्थितौ न घ्नन्ति मुक्तत्वं मरणेऽपि तथैव ताः ॥ 291
28.m: Therefore, just as the varied experiences of pleasure and pain of an awakened one / during life do not destroy his state of liberation, so too do they not destroy it at death. // 291

28.s:
ye punaryoginaste'pi yasmiṃstattve subhāvitāḥ /
cittaṃ niveśayantyeva tattattvaṃ yāntyaśaṅkitāḥ // 292
28.d:
ये पुनर्योगिनस्तेऽपि यस्मिंस्तत्त्वे सुभाविताः ।
चित्तं निवेशयन्त्येव तत्तत्त्वं यान्त्यशङ्किताः ॥ 292
28.m: Moreover, yogins too, steeped in whatever reality, / enter it without doubt just by directing their consciousness into it. // 292

28.s:
śrīsvacchande tataḥ proktaṃ gandhadhāraṇayā mṛtāḥ /
ityādi mālinīśāstre dhāraṇānāṃ tathā phalam // 293
28.d:
श्रीस्वच्छन्दे ततः प्रोक्तं गन्धधारणया मृताः ।
इत्यादि मालिनीशास्त्रे धारणानां तथा फलम् ॥ 293
28.m: Therefore it was stated in the venerable Svacchanda: 'those who die through concentration on smell...', / and likewise in the Mālinī treatise regarding the fruit of concentrations. // 293

28.s:
eteṣāṃ maraṇābhikhyo bhogo nāsti tu ye tanum /
dhāraṇābhistyajantyāśu paradehapraveśavat // 294
28.d:
एतेषां मरणाभिख्यो भोगो नास्ति तु ये तनुम् ।
धारणाभिस्त्यजन्त्याशु परदेहप्रवेशवत् ॥ 294
28.m: For those, however, who quickly abandon the body by means of concentrations, / as in entering another's body, the experience called dying does not exist. // 294

28.s:
etāvānmṛtibhogo hi marmacchinmūḍhatākṣagā /
dhvāntābilatvaṃ manasi taccaiteṣu na vidyate // 295
28.d:
एतावान्मृतिभोगो हि मर्मच्छिन्मूढताक्षगा ।
ध्वान्ताबिलत्वं मनसि तच्चैतेषु न विद्यते ॥ 295
28.m: For such an experience of dying is the cutting of vital spots, delusion occurring in the senses, / and turbid darkness in the mind; and that is not present in these [yogins]. // 295

28.s:
tathāhi mānasaṃ yatnaṃ tāvatsamadhitiṣṭhati /
ahaṃrūḍhyā pare dehe yāvatsyādbuddhisaṃcaraḥ // 296
28.d:
तथाहि मानसं यत्नं तावत्समधितिष्ठति ।
अहंरूढ्या परे देहे यावत्स्याद्बुद्धिसंचरः ॥ 296
28.m: To explain: mental effort persists to that extent, / by establishing the sense of 'I' in the other body, as long as the transition of the intellect occurs. // 296

28.s:
prāṇacakraṃ tadāyattamapi saṃcarate pathā /
tenaivātaḥ prabuddhyeta paradehe'kṣacakrakam // 297
28.d:
प्राणचक्रं तदायत्तमपि संचरते पथा ।
तेनैवातः प्रबुद्ध्येत परदेहेऽक्षचक्रकम् ॥ 297
28.m: The circle of vital breaths, dependent on it, also moves along that very same / path; therefore, the circle of senses awakens in the other body. // 297

28.s:
makṣikā makṣikārājaṃ yathotthitamanūtthitāḥ /
sthitaṃ cānuviśantyevaṃ cittaṃ sarvākṣavṛttayaḥ // 298
28.d:
मक्षिका मक्षिकाराजं यथोत्थितमनूत्थिताः ।
स्थितं चानुविशन्त्येवं चित्तं सर्वाक्षवृत्तयः ॥ 298
28.m: Just as flies rise up after the queen bee rises / and settle after it settles, so do all sense operations [follow] the mind. // 298

28.s:
ato'sya paradehādisaṃcāre nāsti melanam /
akṣāṇāṃ madhyagaṃ sūkṣmaṃ syādetaddehavatpunaḥ // 299
28.d:
अतोऽस्य परदेहादिसंचारे नास्ति मेलनम् ।
अक्षाणां मध्यगं सूक्ष्मं स्यादेतद्देहवत्पुनः ॥ 299
28.m: Therefore, in his transition to another body or the like, there is no assembly / of the senses in the subtle intermediate [body]; it becomes just like this [physical] body again. // 299

28.s:
evaṃ paraśarīrādicāriṇāmiva yoginām /
tattattattvaśarīrāntaścāriṇāṃ nāsti mūḍhatā // 300
28.d:
एवं परशरीरादिचारिणामिव योगिनाम् ।
तत्तत्तत्त्वशरीरान्तश्चारिणां नास्ति मूढता ॥ 300
28.m: Thus, just as for yogins moving into another body and the like, / for those moving within the body of this or that reality there is no delusion. // 300

28.s:
te cāpi dvividhā jñeyā laukikā dīkṣitāstathā /
pūrve śivāḥ syuḥ kramaśaḥ pare tadbhogamātrataḥ // 301
28.d:
ते चापि द्विविधा ज्ञेया लौकिका दीक्षितास्तथा ।
पूर्वे शिवाः स्युः क्रमशः परे तद्भोगमात्रतः ॥ 301
28.m: And they should be understood as twofold: the worldly and the initiated. / The former become Śiva by degrees, the latter through mere enjoyment of that [reality]. // 301

28.s:
dīkṣāpyūrdhvādharānekabhedayojanikāvaśāt /
bhidyamānā yogināṃ syādvicitraphaladāyinī // 302
28.d:
दीक्षाप्यूर्ध्वाधरानेकभेदयोजनिकावशात् ।
भिद्यमाना योगिनां स्याद्विचित्रफलदायिनी ॥ 302
28.m: Initiation too, being differentiated through the power of connection to higher and lower multiple divisions, / grants manifold fruits to yogins. // 302

28.s:
ye tu vijñāninaste'tra dvedhā kampretaratvataḥ /
tatra ye kampravijñānāste dehānted śivāḥ sphuṭam // 303
28.d:
ये तु विज्ञानिनस्तेऽत्र द्वेधा कम्प्रेतरत्वतः ।
तत्र ये कम्प्रविज्ञानास्ते देहान्तेद् शिवाः स्फुटम् ॥ 303
28.m: Those, however, who possess higher knowledge are twofold here, through being wavering or otherwise. / Among them, those whose higher knowledge is wavering clearly become Śiva at the end of the body. // 303

28.s:
yato vijñānameteṣāmutpannaṃ naca susphuṭam /
vikalpāntarayogena nacāpyunmūlitātmakam // 304
28.d:
यतो विज्ञानमेतेषामुत्पन्नं नच सुस्फुटम् ।
विकल्पान्तरयोगेन नचाप्युन्मूलितात्मकम् ॥ 304
28.m: Because their higher knowledge, though arisen, is not entirely clear, / nor is its nature uprooted by connection with other conceptual constructs. // 304

28.s:
ato dehe pramādottho vikalpo dehapātataḥ /
naśyedavaśyaṃ taccāpi budhyate jñānamuttamam // 305
28.d:
अतो देहे प्रमादोत्थो विकल्पो देहपाततः ।
नश्येदवश्यं तच्चापि बुध्यते ज्ञानमुत्तमम् ॥ 305
28.m: Therefore, the conceptual construct arising from negligence in the body will necessarily / perish at the fall of the body, and that supreme knowledge is also realized. // 305

28.s:
saṃskārakalpanātiṣṭhadadhvastīkṛtamantarā /
prāptapākaṃ saṃvarīturapāye bhāsate hi tat // 306
28.d:
संस्कारकल्पनातिष्ठदध्वस्तीकृतमन्तरा ।
प्राप्तपाकं संवरीतुरपाये भासते हि तत् ॥ 306
28.m: For that [knowledge], remaining as an imaginative construct of latent traces and undamaged within, / having reached maturity, shines forth when the obscuring factor disappears. // 306

28.s:
ye tu svabhyastavijñānamayāḥ śivamayāḥ sadā /
jīvanmuktā hi te naiṣāṃ mṛtau kāpi vicāraṇā // 307
28.d:
ये तु स्वभ्यस्तविज्ञानमयाः शिवमयाः सदा ।
जीवन्मुक्ता हि ते नैषां मृतौ कापि विचारणा ॥ 307
28.m: Those, however, whose nature consists of well-practised higher knowledge are always identical with Śiva; / indeed, they are liberated while living. For them there is no inquiry whatever concerning death. // 307

28.s:
yathāhi jīvanmuktānāṃ sthitau nāsti vicāraṇā /
sukhiduḥkhivimūḍhatve, mṛtāvapi tathā na sā // 308
28.d:
यथाहि जीवन्मुक्तानां स्थितौ नास्ति विचारणा ।
सुखिदुःखिविमूढत्वे, मृतावपि तथा न सा ॥ 308
28.m: For just as for those liberated while living there is no deliberation during life / when they are happy, sorrowful, or bewildered, so too there is none at death. // 308

28.s:
śrīratnamālāśāstre taduvāca parameśvaraḥ /
svaśāstre cāpyahīśāno viśvādhāradhurandharaḥ // 309
28.d:
श्रीरत्नमालाशास्त्रे तदुवाच परमेश्वरः ।
स्वशास्त्रे चाप्यहीशानो विश्वाधारधुरन्धरः ॥ 309
28.m: The Supreme Lord declared that in the venerable Ratnamālā scripture, / and so did the lord of serpents, bearer of the burden of the foundation of the universe, in his own treatise: // 309

28.s:
rathyāntare mūtrapurīṣamadhye caṇḍālagehe niraye śmaśāne /
sacintako vā gatacintako vā jñānī vimokṣaṃ labhate'pi cānte // 310
28.d:
रथ्यान्तरे मूत्रपुरीषमध्ये चण्डालगेहे निरये श्मशाने ।
सचिन्तको वा गतचिन्तको वा ज्ञानी विमोक्षं लभतेऽपि चान्ते ॥ 310
28.m: "In an alleyway, amidst urine and feces, in an outcaste's house, in hell, or in a cremation ground, / whether full of anxious thought or free from anxious thought, the knower attains liberation even at the end." // 310

28.s:
apiceti dhvanirjīvanmuktatāmasya bhāṣate /
sacintācintakatvoktiretāvatsaṃbhavasthitim // 311
28.d:
अपिचेति ध्वनिर्जीवन्मुक्ततामस्य भाषते ।
सचिन्ताचिन्तकत्वोक्तिरेतावत्संभवस्थितिम् ॥ 311
28.m: The particle 'even' expresses his state of being liberated while living; / the mention of being with or without thought refers to the status of such a possibility. // 311

28.s:
tīrthe śvapacagṛhe vā naṣṭasmṛtirapi parityajeddeham /
jñānasamakālamuktaḥ kaivalyaṃ yāti hataśokaḥ // 312
28.d:
तीर्थे श्वपचगृहे वा नष्टस्मृतिरपि परित्यजेद्देहम् ।
ज्ञानसमकालमुक्तः कैवल्यं याति हतशोकः ॥ 312
28.m: "In a sacred place or in a dog-cooker's hut, he may abandon his body even having lost memory; / liberated simultaneously with knowledge, he attains isolation, his sorrow destroyed." // 312

28.s:
anantakārikā caiṣā prāhedaṃ bandhakaṃ kila /
sukṛtaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ cāsya śaṅkyaṃ taccāsya no bhavet // 313
28.d:
अनन्तकारिका चैषा प्राहेदं बन्धकं किल ।
सुकृतं दुष्कृतं चास्य शङ्क्यं तच्चास्य नो भवेत् ॥ 313
28.m: And this verse of Ananta declared: "This [merit and demerit] is indeed binding; / both good deed and bad deed might be suspected for him, but that does not happen for him." // 313

28.s:
apiśabdādaluptasmṛtyā vā saṃbhāvyate kila /
mṛtirnaṣṭasmṛtereva mṛteḥ prāk sāstu kiṃ tayā // 314
28.d:
अपिशब्दादलुप्तस्मृत्या वा संभाव्यते किल ।
मृतिर्नष्टस्मृतेरेव मृतेः प्राक् सास्तु किं तया ॥ 314
28.m: By the word 'even', death is conceived as occurring with unlost memory / or indeed only with lost memory; let that be prior to death, for what does it matter? // 314

28.s:
liṅca saṃbhāvanāyāṃ syādiyatsaṃbhāvyate kila /
saca kāladhvaniḥ prāha mṛtermuktāvahetutām // 315
28.d:
लिङ्च संभावनायां स्यादियत्संभाव्यते किल ।
सच कालध्वनिः प्राह मृतेर्मुक्तावहेतुताम् ॥ 315
28.m: And the optative expresses possibility: "so much is indeed possible"; / and that temporal expression affirms that death is not a cause of liberation. // 315

28.s:
kaivalyamiti cāśaṅkāpadaṃ yāpyabhavattanuḥ /
bhedapradatvenaiṣāpi dhvastā tena viśokatā // 316
28.d:
कैवल्यमिति चाशङ्कापदं याप्यभवत्तनुः ।
भेदप्रदत्वेनैषापि ध्वस्ता तेन विशोकता ॥ 316
28.m: And by the word 'isolation', even the body, which was an object of suspicion / as bestowing difference, is also destroyed by that; hence the state of being free from sorrow. // 316

28.s:
paradehādisaṃbandho yathā nāsya vibhedakaḥ /
tathā svadehasaṃbandho jīvanmuktasya yadyapi // 317
28.d:
परदेहादिसंबन्धो यथा नास्य विभेदकः ।
तथा स्वदेहसंबन्धो जीवन्मुक्तस्य यद्यपि ॥ 317
28.m: Although connection with another's body or the like does not bring division to him, / so too connection with his own body [does not] for one liberated while living; // 317

28.s:
ataśca na viśeṣo'sya viśvākṛtinirākṛteḥ /
śivābhinnasya dehe vā tadabhāve'pi vā kila // 318
28.d:
अतश्च न विशेषोऽस्य विश्वाकृतिनिराकृतेः ।
शिवाभिन्नस्य देहे वा तदभावेऽपि वा किल ॥ 318
28.m: and therefore there is no distinction for him, whose universal form is formless, / whether in the body or in its absence, being indivisible from Śiva; // 318

28.s:
tathāpi prācyatadbhedasaṃskārāśaṅkanasthiteḥ /
adhunoktaṃ kevalatvaṃ yadvā mātrantarāśrayāt // 319
28.d:
तथापि प्राच्यतद्भेदसंस्काराशङ्कनस्थितेः ।
अधुनोक्तं केवलत्वं यद्वा मात्रन्तराश्रयात् ॥ 319
28.m: nevertheless, because of the persistence of suspicion from previous latent impressions of difference, / isolation is stated now, or else because of relying on other subjects. // 319

28.s:
tānyenaṃ na vidurbhinnaṃ taiḥ sa mukto'bhidhīyate /
śrīmattraiśirase'pyuktaṃ sūryendupuṭavarjite // 320
28.d:
तान्येनं न विदुर्भिन्नं तैः स मुक्तोऽभिधीयते ।
श्रीमत्त्रैशिरसेऽप्युक्तं सूर्येन्दुपुटवर्जिते ॥ 320
28.m: They do not know him as separate; by them he is spoken of as liberated. / It is also said in the venerable Traiśirasa: "Free from the enclosure of sun and moon, // 320

28.s:
jugupsābhāvabhaṅgasthe sarvataḥ stambhavatsthite /
sarvavyāpattirahite pramāṇapratyayātige // 321
28.d:
जुगुप्साभावभङ्गस्थे सर्वतः स्तम्भवत्स्थिते ।
सर्वव्यापत्तिरहिते प्रमाणप्रत्ययातिगे ॥ 321
28.m: abiding in the cessation of repulsion and existence, standing everywhere like a pillar, / devoid of all afflictions, transcending means of knowledge and cognitions, // 321

28.s:
tasminbodhāntare līnaḥ karmakartāpyanañjanaḥ /
pradhānaṃ ghaṭa ākāśa ātmā maṣṭe ghaṭe'pi kham // 322
28.d:
तस्मिन्बोधान्तरे लीनः कर्मकर्ताप्यनञ्जनः ।
प्रधानं घट आकाश आत्मा मष्टे घटेऽपि खम् ॥ 322
28.m: dissolved in that internal consciousness, even doing actions he is unstained; / the matrix is the pot, the self is space, and even when the pot is destroyed, space // 322

28.s:
na naśyettadvadevāsāvātmā śivamayo bhavet /
svatantro'vasthito jñānī prasaretsarvavastuṣu // 323
28.d:
न नश्येत्तद्वदेवासावात्मा शिवमयो भवेत् ।
स्वतन्त्रोऽवस्थितो ज्ञानी प्रसरेत्सर्ववस्तुषु ॥ 323
28.m: is not destroyed: just so, this self becomes identical with Śiva; / established as autonomous, the knower expands into all things. // 323

28.s:
tasya bhāvo nacābhāvaḥ saṃsthānaṃ naca kalpanā /
etadevāntarāgūrya gururgītāsvabhāṣata // 324
28.d:
तस्य भावो नचाभावः संस्थानं नच कल्पना ।
एतदेवान्तरागूर्य गुरुर्गीतास्वभाषत ॥ 324
28.m: For him there is neither existence nor non-existence, neither configuration nor mental projection." / Having grasped this internally, the Guru declared in the Gītā: // 324

28.s:
yaṃ yaṃ vāpi smaranbhāvaṃ tyajatyante kalevaram /
taṃ tamevaiti kaunteya sadā tadbhāvabhāvitaḥ // 325
28.d:
यं यं वापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम् ।
तं तमेवैति कौन्तेय सदा तद्भावभावितः ॥ 325
28.m: "Whatever state one remembers when abandoning the body at the end, / to that very one he goes, O son of Kuntī, constantly cultivated in that state. // 325

28.s:
tasmātsarveṣu kāleṣu māmanusmara yudhya ca /
yadā sattve vivṛddhe tu pralīnastvūrdhvagastadā // 326
28.d:
तस्मात्सर्वेषु कालेषु मामनुस्मर युध्य च ।
यदा सत्त्वे विवृद्धे तु प्रलीनस्त्वूर्ध्वगस्तदा ॥ 326
28.m: Therefore, at all times remember Me and fight! / But when one dissolves as sattva has increased, then one goes upward; // 326

28.s:
kramādrajastamolīnaḥ karmayonivimūḍhagaḥ /
tatrendriyāṇāṃ saṃmohaśvāsāyāsaparītatā // 327
28.d:
क्रमाद्रजस्तमोलीनः कर्मयोनिविमूढगः ।
तत्रेन्द्रियाणां संमोहश्वासायासपरीतता ॥ 327
28.m: dissolving in rajas and tamas successively, one goes to wombs of action and delusion." / In that regard, the bewilderment of the senses, being overcome by the toil of breathing, // 327

28.s:
ityādimṛtibhogo'yaṃ dehe na tyajanaṃ tanoḥ /
yastvasau kṣaṇa evaikaścaramaḥ prāṇanātmakaḥ // 328
28.d:
इत्यादिमृतिभोगोऽयं देहे न त्यजनं तनोः ।
यस्त्वसौ क्षण एवैकश्चरमः प्राणनात्मकः ॥ 328
28.m: and so forth—this is the experience of dying in the body, not the abandoning of the body. / But that which is a single final moment consisting of vitalization, // 328

28.s:
yadanantaramevaiṣa dehaḥ syātkāṣṭhakuḍyavat /
sā dehatyāgakālāṃśakalā dehaviyoginī // 329
28.d:
यदनन्तरमेवैष देहः स्यात्काष्ठकुड्यवत् ।
सा देहत्यागकालांशकला देहवियोगिनी ॥ 329
28.m: immediately after which this body becomes like wood or a wall— / that fraction of time of discarding the body is separate from the body. // 329

28.s:
tata eva hi taddehasukhaduḥkhādikojjhitā /
tasyāṃ yadeva smarati prāksaṃskāraprabodhataḥ // 330
28.d:
तत एव हि तद्देहसुखदुःखादिकोज्झिता ।
तस्यां यदेव स्मरति प्राक्संस्कारप्रबोधतः ॥ 330
28.m: For this very reason, it is free from the pleasure, pain, and the like of that body; / in that [moment], whatever one remembers through the awakening of prior latent traces // 330

28.s:
adṛṣṭābhyāsabhūyastvaśaktipātādihetukāt /
tadeva rūpamabhyeti sukhiduḥkhivimūḍhakam // 331
28.d:
अदृष्टाभ्यासभूयस्त्वशक्तिपातादिहेतुकात् ।
तदेव रूपमभ्येति सुखिदुःखिविमूढकम् ॥ 331
28.m: caused by destiny, repeated practice, or the descent of power and the like, / that very form—happy, sorrowful, or bewildered—he attains. // 331

28.s:
yadvā niḥsukhaduḥkhādi yadi vānandarūpakam /
kasmādeti tadevaiṣa yataḥ smarati saṃvidi // 332
28.d:
यद्वा निःसुखदुःखादि यदि वानन्दरूपकम् ।
कस्मादेति तदेवैष यतः स्मरति संविदि ॥ 332
28.m:
Or [a state] free of pleasure, pain, and the like, or characterized by bliss.
Why does it attain precisely that? Because in consciousness it remembers [it]. // 332

28.s:
prāk prasphuredyadadhikaṃ deho'sau cidadhiṣṭhiteḥ /
yadeva prāgadhiṣṭhānaṃ citā tādātmyavṛttitaḥ // 333
28.d:
प्राक् प्रस्फुरेद्यदधिकं देहोऽसौ चिदधिष्ठितेः ।
यदेव प्रागधिष्ठानं चिता तादात्म्यवृत्तितः ॥ 333
28.m:
What pulsed most prominently beforehand was this body, because of its governance by consciousness.
Indeed, prior governance by consciousness arises through the relation of identity [with it]. // 333

28.s:
saivātra līnatā proktā sattve rajasi tāmase /
nīlapītādike jñeye yataḥ prākkalpitāṃ tanum // 334
28.d:
सैवात्र लीनता प्रोक्ता सत्त्वे रजसि तामसे ।
नीलपीतादिके ज्ञेये यतः प्राक्कल्पितां तनुम् ॥ 334
28.m:
Just that is taught here to be dissolution in sattva, in rajas, in tamas,
[or] in knowables such as blue, yellow, and the rest; because, having governed // 334

28.s:
adhiṣṭhāyaiva saṃvittiradhiṣṭhānaṃ karotyalam /
ato'dhiṣṭheyamātrasya śarīratve'pi kuḍyataḥ // 335
28.d:
अधिष्ठायैव संवित्तिरधिष्ठानं करोत्यलम् ।
अतोऽधिष्ठेयमात्रस्य शरीरत्वेऽपि कुड्यतः ॥ 335
28.m:
only a previously conceptualized body, consciousness fully exercises governance.
Therefore, even though mere governed objects have the status of a body, as in the case of a wall, // 335

28.s:
dehasyāsti viśeṣo yatsarvādhiṣṭheyapūrvatā /
tādātmyavṛttiranyeṣāṃ tanna satyapi vedyate // 336
28.d:
देहस्यास्ति विशेषो यत्सर्वाधिष्ठेयपूर्वता ।
तादात्म्यवृत्तिरन्येषां तन्न सत्यपि वेद्यते ॥ 336
28.m:
there is a distinctive feature of the [physical] body: its priority to everything governed.
The relation of identity with other [objects] is not experienced even when they are present; // 336

28.s:
vedyānāṃ kintu dehasya nityāvyabhicaritvataḥ /
sā ca tasyaiva dehasya pūrvamṛtyantajanmanā // 337
28.d:
वेद्यानां किन्तु देहस्य नित्याव्यभिचरित्वतः ।
सा च तस्यैव देहस्य पूर्वमृत्यन्तजन्मना ॥ 337
28.m:
they are mere knowables, whereas with the body it is invariable and perpetual.
And that [identity] belongs to that very body through its birth culminating in its prior death, // 337

28.s:
smṛtyā prācyānubhavanakṛtasaṃskāracitrayā /
yuktyānayāsmatsantānaguruṇā kallaṭena yat // 338
28.d:
स्मृत्या प्राच्यानुभवनकृतसंस्कारचित्रया ।
युक्त्यानयास्मत्सन्तानगुरुणा कल्लटेन यत् ॥ 338
28.m:
by means of memory variegated by traces produced by previous experience.
By this reasoning, that which was stated by Kallaṭa, the guru of our lineage: // 338

28.s:
dehāviśeṣe prāṇākhyadārḍhyaṃ heturudīritam /
tadyuktamanyathā prāṇadārḍhye ko heturekataḥ // 339
28.d:
देहाविशेषे प्राणाख्यदार्ढ्यं हेतुरुदीरितम् ।
तद्युक्तमन्यथा प्राणदार्ढ्ये को हेतुरेकतः ॥ 339
28.m:
'Given that embodiment is identical, firmness called breath is declared the cause,'
is established. Otherwise, what single cause would there be for the firmness of breath, // 339

28.s:
dehatvasyāviśeṣe'pītyeṣa praśno na śāmyati /
smaranniti śatā hetau tadrūpaṃ pratipadyate // 340
28.d:
देहत्वस्याविशेषेऽपीत्येष प्रश्नो न शाम्यति ।
स्मरन्निति शता हेतौ तद्रूपं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 340
28.m:
given that the condition of having a body is indistinguishable? This question would never subside.
By the present participle 'remembering' denoting the cause, it assumes that nature. // 340

28.s:
prāk smaryate yato dehaḥ prākcitādhiṣṭhitaḥ sphuran /
ataḥ smaraṇamantyaṃ yattadasarvajñamātṛṣu // 341
28.d:
प्राक् स्मर्यते यतो देहः प्राक्चिताधिष्ठितः स्फुरन् ।
अतः स्मरणमन्त्यं यत्तदसर्वज्ञमातृषु ॥ 341
28.m:
Because it is remembered beforehand, the body, having been governed by consciousness beforehand, flashes forth.
Therefore, as for the final memory, among non-omniscient subjects // 341

28.s:
na jātu gocaro yasmāddehāntaraviniścayaḥ /
yattu bandhupriyāputrapānādismaraṇaṃ sphuṭam // 342
28.d:
न जातु गोचरो यस्माद्देहान्तरविनिश्चयः ।
यत्तु बन्धुप्रियापुत्रपानादिस्मरणं स्फुटम् ॥ 342
28.m:
it never has as its object the determination of another body;
whereas that which is the vivid memory of kin, beloved, son, drinking, and the like // 342

28.s:
na taddehāntarāsaṅgi na tadantyaṃ yato bhavet /
kasyāpi tu śarīrānte vāsanā yā prabhotsyate // 343
28.d:
न तद्देहान्तरासङ्गि न तदन्त्यं यतो भवेत् ।
कस्यापि तु शरीरान्ते वासना या प्रभोत्स्यते ॥ 343
28.m:
is not attached to another body, because it cannot be the final [thought].
However, whatever latent impression awakens in someone at the end of the body, // 343

28.s:
dehasattve tadaucityājjāyetānubhavaḥ sphuṭaḥ /
yathā purāṇe kathitaṃ mṛgapotakatṛṣṇayā // 344
28.d:
देहसत्त्वे तदौचित्याज्जायेतानुभवः स्फुटः ।
यथा पुराणे कथितं मृगपोतकतृष्णया ॥ 344
28.m:
while the body still exists, a vivid experience arises in accordance with it,
just as related in the Purāṇa: through longing for a young fawn, // 344

28.s:
muniḥ ko'pi mṛgībhāvamabhyuvāhādhivāsitaḥ /
tatra so'nubhavo heturna janmāntarasūtaye // 345
28.d:
मुनिः कोऽपि मृगीभावमभ्युवाहाधिवासितः ।
तत्र सोऽनुभवो हेतुर्न जन्मान्तरसूतये ॥ 345
28.m:
a certain sage, perfumed [by that desire], attained the state of a deer.
There, that experience is not the cause for bringing about another birth; // 345

28.s:
tasyaitadvāsanā hetuḥ kākatālīyavat sa tu /
nanu kasmāttadevaiṣa smarati ityāha yatsadā // 346
28.d:
तस्यैतद्वासना हेतुः काकतालीयवत् स तु ।
ननु कस्मात्तदेवैष स्मरति इत्याह यत्सदा ॥ 346
28.m:
the latent impression of it is the cause, but that [experience] is purely accidental.
[Objection:] 'Why does it remember precisely that?' To this it is replied: 'Because, always // 346

28.s:
tadbhāvabhāvitastena tadevaiṣa smaratyalam /
evamasmi bhaviṣyāmītyeṣa tadbhāva ucyate // 347
28.d:
तद्भावभावितस्तेन तदेवैष स्मरत्यलम् ।
एवमस्मि भविष्यामीत्येष तद्भाव उच्यते ॥ 347
28.m:
permeated by the condition of that, therefore it completely remembers precisely that.'
'Thus I am, I will be'—this is called 'the condition of that'. // 347

28.s:
bhaviṣyato hi bhavanaṃ bhāvyate na sataḥ kvacit /
kramātsphuṭatvakaraṇaṃ bhāvanaṃ parikīrtyate // 348
28.d:
भविष्यतो हि भवनं भाव्यते न सतः क्वचित् ।
क्रमात्स्फुटत्वकरणं भावनं परिकीर्त्यते ॥ 348
28.m:
Indeed, what is yet to be is cultivated [in thought], never that which is already present.
Bringing about vividness in a gradual manner is celebrated as cultivation [or visualization]. // 348

28.s:
sphuṭasya cānubhavanaṃ na bhāvanamidaṃ sphuṭam /
tadaharjātabālasya paśoḥ kīṭasya vā taroḥ // 349
28.d:
स्फुटस्य चानुभवनं न भावनमिदं स्फुटम् ।
तदहर्जातबालस्य पशोः कीटस्य वा तरोः ॥ 349
28.m:
And the direct experience of what is vivid is not this cultivation; this is clear.
In the case of a child born that very day, an animal, an insect, or a tree, // 349

28.s:
mūḍhatve'pi tadānīṃ prāgbhāvanā hyabhavatsphuṭā /
sā tanmūḍhaśarīrānte saṃskārapratibodhanāt // 350
28.d:
मूढत्वेऽपि तदानीं प्राग्भावना ह्यभवत्स्फुटा ।
सा तन्मूढशरीरान्ते संस्कारप्रतिबोधनात् ॥ 350
28.m:
even though dull at that time, a prior cultivation was indeed vivid.
That, at the end of that dull body, through the awakening of traces, // 350

28.s:
smṛtidvāreṇa taddehavaicitryaphaladāyinī /
deśādivyavadhāne'pi vāsanānāmudīritāt // 351
28.d:
स्मृतिद्वारेण तद्देहवैचित्र्यफलदायिनी ।
देशादिव्यवधानेऽपि वासनानामुदीरितात् ॥ 351
28.m:
by means of memory yields the fruit of that bodily variety.
Even when separated by space and time, latent impressions are declared [efficacious] // 351

28.s:
ānantaryaikarūpatvātsmṛtisaṃskārayorataḥ /
tathānubhavanārūḍhyā sphuṭasyāpi tu bhāvitā // 352
28.d:
आनन्तर्यैकरूपत्वात्स्मृतिसंस्कारयोरतः ।
तथानुभवनारूढ्या स्फुटस्यापि तु भाविता ॥ 352
28.m:
because memory and latent impression share the nature of unbroken contiguity.
Therefore, through such ascendancy of experience, that which is cultivated even when vivid, // 352

28.s:
bhāvyamānā na kiṃ sūte tatsantānasadṛgvapuḥ /
tattādṛktādṛśairbandhuputramitrādibhiḥ saha // 353
28.d:
भाव्यमाना न किं सूते तत्सन्तानसदृग्वपुः ।
तत्तादृक्तादृशैर्बन्धुपुत्रमित्रादिभिः सह ॥ 353
28.m:
being cultivated, does it not produce a body similar to that continuous flow,
together with such and such kin, sons, friends, and the like? // 353

28.s:
bhāsate'pi pare loke svapnavadvāsanākramāt /
nanu mātrantarairbandhuputrādyaistattathā na kim // 354
28.d:
भासतेऽपि परे लोके स्वप्नवद्वासनाक्रमात् ।
ननु मात्रन्तरैर्बन्धुपुत्राद्यैस्तत्तथा न किम् ॥ 354
28.m:
It appears even in the next world, like a dream, through the sequence of latent impressions.
[Objection:] 'Is it not the case that other subjects, such as kin and sons, do not cognize it thus?' // 354

28.s:
vedyate ka idaṃ prāha sa tāvadveda vedyatām /
vyāpāravyāhṛtivrātavedye mātrantaravraje // 355
28.d:
वेद्यते क इदं प्राह स तावद्वेद वेद्यताम् ।
व्यापारव्याहृतिव्रातवेद्ये मात्रन्तरव्रजे ॥ 355
28.m:
Who said this? He only knows knowability.
Regarding the crowd of other subjects known through the manifold of actions and words, // 355

28.s:
svapne nāsti sa ityeṣā vākpramāṇavivarjitā /
ya evaite tu dṛśyante jāgratyete mayekṣitāḥ // 356
28.d:
स्वप्ने नास्ति स इत्येषा वाक्प्रमाणविवर्जिता ।
य एवैते तु दृश्यन्ते जाग्रत्येते मयेक्षिताः ॥ 356
28.m:
the claim that 'it does not exist in a dream' is devoid of any valid means of knowledge.
[Opponent:] 'Only those seen in waking are seen by me [as real]; // 356

28.s:
svapna ityastu mithyaitattatpramātṛvacobalāt /
yānapaśyamahaṃ svapne pramātṝṃste na kecana // 357
28.d:
स्वप्न इत्यस्तु मिथ्यैतत्तत्प्रमातृवचोबलात् ।
यानपश्यमहं स्वप्ने प्रमातॄंस्ते न केचन ॥ 357
28.m:
let a dream be false on the strength of the statements of those subjects.
Those subjects whom I did not see in the dream do not grieve, nor do they see me'— // 357

28.s:
na śocanti na cekṣante māmityatrāsti kā pramā /
yataḥ sarvānumānānāṃ svasaṃvedananiṣṭhitau // 358
28.d:
न शोचन्ति न चेक्षन्ते मामित्यत्रास्ति का प्रमा ।
यतः सर्वानुमानानां स्वसंवेदननिष्ठितौ ॥ 358
28.m: what proof is there for this? For, since all inferences are grounded in self-awareness, // 358

28.s:
pramātrantarasadbhāvaḥ saṃvinniṣṭho na tadgataḥ /
ghaṭāderastitā saṃvinniṣṭhitā natu tadgatā // 359
28.d:
प्रमात्रन्तरसद्भावः संविन्निष्ठो न तद्गतः ।
घटादेरस्तिता संविन्निष्ठिता नतु तद्गता ॥ 359
28.m:
the existence of another subject is grounded in consciousness, not residing in that [other subject].
The existence of a pot or the like is grounded in consciousness, not residing in that [object]; // 359

28.s:
tadvanmātrantare'pyeṣā saṃvinniṣṭhā na tadgatā /
tena sthitamidaṃ yadyadbhāvyate tattadeva hi // 360
28.d:
तद्वन्मात्रन्तरेऽप्येषा संविन्निष्ठा न तद्गता ।
तेन स्थितमिदं यद्यद्भाव्यते तत्तदेव हि ॥ 360
28.m:
likewise, in the case of another subject too, this [existence] is grounded in consciousness, not residing in that [subject].
Therefore it is established: whatever is cultivated is indeed precisely that which // 360

28.s:
dehānte budhyate no cet syādanyādṛkprabodhanam /
tathāhyantyakṣaṇe brahmavidyākarṇanasaṃskṛtaḥ // 361
28.d:
देहान्ते बुध्यते नो चेत् स्यादन्यादृक्प्रबोधनम् ।
तथाह्यन्त्यक्षणे ब्रह्मविद्याकर्णनसंस्कृतः ॥ 361
28.m:
is cognized at the end of the body; if not, there would be a different kind of awakening.
Thus, at the final moment, one refined by the hearing of the lore of Brahman // 361

28.s:
mucyate janturityuktaṃ prāksaṃskārabalatvataḥ /
nipātābhyāmantaśabdātsmaraṇācchaturantyataḥ // 362
28.d:
मुच्यते जन्तुरित्युक्तं प्राक्संस्कारबलत्वतः ।
निपाताभ्यामन्तशब्दात्स्मरणाच्छतुरन्त्यतः ॥ 362
28.m:
is liberated, a living being—so it is declared—by the power of prior latent traces.
Through the two particles, through the word 'end', through 'remembering', through the fourth ending, // 362

28.s:
pādācca nikhilādardhaślokācca samanantarāt /
līnaśabdācca sarvaṃ taduktamarthasatattvakam // 363
28.d:
पादाच्च निखिलादर्धश्लोकाच्च समनन्तरात् ।
लीनशब्दाच्च सर्वं तदुक्तमर्थसतत्त्वकम् ॥ 363
28.m:
and through the entire quarter and the immediately following half-verse,
and through the word 'dissolved', all that true nature of the matter has been stated. // 363

28.s:
ajñātvaitattu sarve'pi kuśakāśāvalambinaḥ /
yattadorvyatyayaṃ kecitkecidanyādṛśaṃ kramam // 364
28.d:
अज्ञात्वैतत्तु सर्वेऽपि कुशकाशावलम्बिनः ।
यत्तदोर्व्यत्ययं केचित्केचिदन्यादृशं क्रमम् ॥ 364
28.m:
Failing to understand this, however, all [commentators], clutching at straws,
explain an inversion of 'yat' and 'tat', some another kind of sequence, // 364

28.s:
bhinnakramau nipātau ca tyajatīti ca saptamīm /
vyācakṣate tacca sarvaṃ nopayogyuktayojane // 365
28.d:
भिन्नक्रमौ निपातौ च त्यजतीति च सप्तमीम् ।
व्याचक्षते तच्च सर्वं नोपयोग्युक्तयोजने ॥ 365
28.m:
a split syntax of the two particles, and the locative in 'abandons'.
All of that is useless for the proper interpretation, // 365

28.s:
naca taddarśitaṃ mithyā svāntasammohadāyakam /
taditthaṃprāyaṇasyaitattattvaṃ śrīśambhunāthataḥ // 366
28.d:
नच तद्दर्शितं मिथ्या स्वान्तसम्मोहदायकम् ।
तदित्थंप्रायणस्यैतत्तत्त्वं श्रीशम्भुनाथतः ॥ 366
28.m:
and has not been shown, as it is false and produces confusion in the heart.
Thus, having obtained from revered Śambhunātha this reality concerning dying, // 366

28.s:
adhigamyoditaṃ tena mṛtyorbhītirvinaśyati /
viditamṛtisatattvāḥ saṃvidambhonidhānādacalahṛdayavīryākarṣaniṣpīḍanottham /
amṛtamiti nigīrṇe kālakūṭe'tra devā yadi pivatha tadānīṃ niścitaṃ vaḥ śivatvam // 367
28.d:
अधिगम्योदितं तेन मृत्योर्भीतिर्विनश्यति ।
विदितमृतिसतत्त्वाः संविदम्भोनिधानादचलहृदयवीर्याकर्षनिष्पीडनोत्थम् ।
अमृतमिति निगीर्णे कालकूटेऽत्र देवा यदि पिवथ तदानीं निश्चितं वः शिवत्वम् ॥ 367
28.m:
it has been expounded by him, whereby the fear of death is destroyed.
O gods who know the true nature of death! When the kālakūṭa poison here has been swallowed,
if you drink the nectar arisen from the squeezing and pulling of the vigor of the steadfast heart
from the receptacle of the ocean of consciousness, then your state of Śiva is certain! // 367

28.s:
utsavo'pi hi yaḥ kaścillaukikaḥ so'pi saṃmadam /
saṃvidabdhitaraṅgābhaṃ sūte tadapi parvavat // 368
28.d:
उत्सवोऽपि हि यः कश्चिल्लौकिकः सोऽपि संमदम् ।
संविदब्धितरङ्गाभं सूते तदपि पर्ववत् ॥ 368
28.m:
Even whatever ordinary worldly festival there is, that too generates intense joy
resembling a wave on the ocean of consciousness; therefore, it too is like an auspicious occasion. // 368

28.s:
etena ca vipaddhvaṃsapramodādiṣu parvatā /
vyākhyātā tena tatrāpi viśeṣāddevatārcanam // 369
28.d:
एतेन च विपद्ध्वंसप्रमोदादिषु पर्वता ।
व्याख्याता तेन तत्रापि विशेषाद्देवतार्चनम् ॥ 369
28.m:
And by this, the nature of an auspicious occasion in the destruction of calamity, joy, and the like
is explained; therefore, on such occasions too, the worship of the deities is performed with particularity. // 369

28.s:
purakṣobhādyadbhutaṃ yattatsvātantrye svasaṃvidaḥ /
dārḍhyadāyīti tallābhadine vaiśeṣikārcanam // 370
28.d:
पुरक्षोभाद्यद्भुतं यत्तत्स्वातन्त्र्ये स्वसंविदः ।
दार्ढ्यदायीति तल्लाभदिने वैशेषिकार्चनम् ॥ 370
28.m:
That which is wondrous, such as the agitation of a city, imparts firmness to the absolute autonomy
of one's own consciousness; therefore, on the day of its attainment, specific worship [is held]. // 370

28.s:
yoginīmelako dvedhā haṭhataḥ priyatastathā /
prācye cchidrāṇi saṃrakṣetkāmacāritvamuttare // 371
28.d:
योगिनीमेलको द्वेधा हठतः प्रियतस्तथा ।
प्राच्ये च्छिद्राणि संरक्षेत्कामचारित्वमुत्तरे ॥ 371
28.m:
The gathering of Yoginīs is twofold: by force and through love;
in the former, one should protect vulnerable points, [while] in the latter there is freedom to act as one pleases. // 371

28.s:
sa ca dvayo'pi mantroddhṛtprasaṅge darśayiṣyate /
yoginīmelakāccaiṣo'vaśyaṃ jñānaṃ prapadyate // 372
28.d:
स च द्वयोऽपि मन्त्रोद्धृत्प्रसङ्गे दर्शयिष्यते ।
योगिनीमेलकाच्चैषोऽवश्यं ज्ञानं प्रपद्यते ॥ 372
28.m:
And both will be shown in the context of the extraction of mantras.
And from the gathering of Yoginīs, one inevitably attains knowledge; // 372

28.s:
tena tatparva tadvacca svasantānādimelanam /
saṃvitsarvātmikā dehabhedādyā saṅkucettu sā // 373
28.d:
तेन तत्पर्व तद्वच्च स्वसन्तानादिमेलनम् ।
संवित्सर्वात्मिका देहभेदाद्या सङ्कुचेत्तु सा ॥ 373
28.m:
therefore, it is an auspicious occasion, as is similarly the assembly of one's own lineage and others.
Consciousness is all-pervading, but it contracts through distinctions of the body and the like; // 373

28.s:
melake'nyonyasaṅghaṭṭapratibimbādvikasvarā /
ucchalannijaraśmyoghaḥ saṃvitsu pratibimbitaḥ // 374
28.d:
मेलकेऽन्योन्यसङ्घट्टप्रतिबिम्बाद्विकस्वरा ।
उच्छलन्निजरश्म्योघः संवित्सु प्रतिबिम्बितः ॥ 374
28.m:
in an assembly, blooming through mutual contact and reflection,
the flood of its own rays surging up and reflected in consciousnesses, // 374

28.s:
bahudarpaṇavaddīptaḥ sarvāyetāpyayatnataḥ /
ata eva gītagītaprabhṛtau bahuparṣadi // 375
28.d:
बहुदर्पणवद्दीप्तः सर्वायेताप्ययत्नतः ।
अत एव गीतगीतप्रभृतौ बहुपर्षदि ॥ 375
28.m:
blazing like multiple mirrors, effortlessly becomes all-inclusive.
Therefore, in singing, chanting, and the like before a large assembly, // 375

28.s:
yaḥ sarvatanmayībhāve hlādo natvekakasya saḥ /
ānandanirbharā saṃvitpratyekaṃ sā tathaikatām // 376
28.d:
यः सर्वतन्मयीभावे ह्लादो नत्वेककस्य सः ।
आनन्दनिर्भरा संवित्प्रत्येकं सा तथैकताम् ॥ 376
28.m:
that delight which exists in becoming completely identified with it does not belong to a solitary person.
Consciousness, brimming with bliss, similarly attains oneness in each individual. // 376

28.s:
nṛttādau viṣaye prāptā pūrṇānandatvamaśnute /
īrṣyāsūyādisaṅkocakāraṇābhāvato'tra sā // 377
28.d:
नृत्तादौ विषये प्राप्ता पूर्णानन्दत्वमश्नुते ।
ईर्ष्यासूयादिसङ्कोचकारणाभावतोऽत्र सा ॥ 377
28.m: having reached an object such as dance, attains full bliss, / because in this state there is no cause of contraction, such as jealousy and malice. // 377

28.s:
vikasvarā niṣpratighaṃ saṃvidānandayoginī /
atanmaye tu kasmiṃścittatrasthe pratihanyate // 378
28.d:
विकस्वरा निष्प्रतिघं संविदानन्दयोगिनी ।
अतन्मये तु कस्मिंश्चित्तत्रस्थे प्रतिहन्यते ॥ 378
28.m: Consciousness expands unobstructed, united with bliss; / but it is hindered when someone who does not share that nature is present there, // 378

28.s:
sthapuṭasparśavatsaṃvidvijātīyatayā sthite /
ataścakrārcanādyeṣu vijātīyamatanmayam // 379
28.d:
स्थपुटस्पर्शवत्संविद्विजातीयतया स्थिते ।
अतश्चक्रार्चनाद्येषु विजातीयमतन्मयम् ॥ 379
28.m: just like the touch of an uneven surface, because [such a person] exists as of an alien kind. / Therefore, in the worship of the circle and the like, [the master] should by no means // 379

28.s:
naiva praveśayetsaṃvitsaṅkocananibandhanam /
yāvantyeva śarīrāṇi svāṅgavatsyuḥ sunirbharām // 380
28.d:
नैव प्रवेशयेत्संवित्सङ्कोचननिबन्धनम् ।
यावन्त्येव शरीराणि स्वाङ्गवत्स्युः सुनिर्भराम् ॥ 380
28.m: allow an alien person who does not share that nature to enter, as this causes the contraction of consciousness. / Only as many bodies as are like one's own limbs, firmly filled [with oneness], // 380

28.s:
ekāṃ saṃvidamāviśya cakre tāvanti pūjayet /
praviṣṭaścetpramādena saṅkocaṃ na vrajettataḥ // 381
28.d:
एकां संविदमाविश्य चक्रे तावन्ति पूजयेत् ।
प्रविष्टश्चेत्प्रमादेन सङ्कोचं न व्रजेत्ततः ॥ 381
28.m: having entered into a single consciousness, should he worship in the circle. / If an [alien person] enters by negligence, he should not undergo contraction on that account; // 381

28.s:
prastutaṃ svasamācāraṃ tena sākaṃ samācaret /
sa tvanugrahaśaktyā cedviddhastattanmayībhavet // 382
28.d:
प्रस्तुतं स्वसमाचारं तेन साकं समाचरेत् ।
स त्वनुग्रहशक्त्या चेद्विद्धस्तत्तन्मयीभवेत् ॥ 382
28.m: he should perform his current ritual observance together with him. / If that person is pierced by the power of grace, he will become identified with it; // 382

28.s:
vāmāviddhastu tannindetpaścāttaṃ ghātayedapi /
śrīmatpicumate coktamādau yatnena rakṣayet // 383
28.d:
वामाविद्धस्तु तन्निन्देत्पश्चात्तं घातयेदपि ।
श्रीमत्पिचुमते चोक्तमादौ यत्नेन रक्षयेत् ॥ 383
28.m: but if pierced by the adverse power, he will revile it, and later [the goddess or master] would even cause him to be slain. / And it is stated in the venerable Picumata: 'At first he should guard against // 383

28.s:
praveśaṃ saṃpaviṣṭasya na vicāraṃ tu kārayet /
lokācārasthito yastu praviṣṭe tādṛśe tu saḥ // 384
28.d:
प्रवेशं संपविष्टस्य न विचारं तु कारयेत् ।
लोकाचारस्थितो यस्तु प्रविष्टे तादृशे तु सः ॥ 384
28.m: the entry [of outsiders] with effort, but he should not institute an investigation of one who has entered. / However, for one who adheres to worldly conduct, when such a one enters, // 384

28.s:
akṛtvā taṃ samācāraṃ punaścakraṃ prapūjayet /
atha vacmi guroḥ śāstravyākhyākramamudāhṛtam // 385
28.d:
अकृत्वा तं समाचारं पुनश्चक्रं प्रपूजयेत् ।
अथ वच्मि गुरोः शास्त्रव्याख्याक्रममुदाहृतम् ॥ 385
28.m: he should worship the circle again without performing that [secret] rite.' / Now I explain the method of the guru's exposition of the scriptures, as taught // 385

28.s:
devyāyāmalaśāstrādau tuhinābhīśumaulinā /
kalpavittatsamūhajñaḥ śāstravitsaṃhitārthavit // 386
28.d:
देव्यायामलशास्त्रादौ तुहिनाभीशुमौलिना ।
कल्पवित्तत्समूहज्ञः शास्त्रवित्संहितार्थवित् ॥ 386
28.m: in the Devyāyāmala and other scriptures by the Moon-crested Lord: / One who knows the rituals (kalpavid), one who knows their collection, one who knows the scripture, one who knows the meaning of the Saṃhitā, // 386

28.s:
sarvaśāstrārthavicceti gururbhinno'padiśyate /
yo yatra śāstre svabhyastajñāno vyākhyāṃ carettu saḥ // 387
28.d:
सर्वशास्त्रार्थविच्चेति गुरुर्भिन्नोऽपदिश्यते ।
यो यत्र शास्त्रे स्वभ्यस्तज्ञानो व्याख्यां चरेत्तु सः ॥ 387
28.m: and one who knows the meaning of all scriptures: thus the guru is taught to be manifold. / He who has well-practised knowledge in whichever scripture may deliver the exposition [of that scripture], // 387

28.s:
nānyathā tadabhāvaścetsarvathā so'pyathācaret /
śrībhairavakule coktaṃ kalpādijñatvamīdṛśam // 388
28.d:
नान्यथा तदभावश्चेत्सर्वथा सोऽप्यथाचरेत् ।
श्रीभैरवकुले चोक्तं कल्पादिज्ञत्वमीदृशम् ॥ 388
28.m: not otherwise; if there is a total lack of such [knowledgeable masters], even he may do so under any circumstance. / And such knowledge of the rituals and the rest is stated in the venerable Bhairavakula. // 388

28.s:
gurorlakṣaṇametāvatsaṃpūrṇajñānataiva yā /
tatrāpi yāsya cidvṛttikarmibhit sāpyavāntarā // 389
28.d:
गुरोर्लक्षणमेतावत्संपूर्णज्ञानतैव या ।
तत्रापि यास्य चिद्वृत्तिकर्मिभित् साप्यवान्तरा ॥ 389
28.m: This alone is the definition of a guru, which is complete knowledge itself; / even there, whatever [guru] divides the activities of the mental states of consciousness is secondary. // 389

28.s:
devyāyāmala uktaṃ taddvāpañcāśāhva āhnike /
deva eva gurutvena tiṣṭhāsurdaśadhā bhavet // 390
28.d:
देव्यायामल उक्तं तद्द्वापञ्चाशाह्व आह्निके ।
देव एव गुरुत्वेन तिष्ठासुर्दशधा भवेत् ॥ 390
28.m: In the Devyāyāmala, in the daily lesson called the fifty-second, it is stated: / The Lord himself, desiring to remain in the status of a guru, becomes tenfold: // 390

28.s:
ucchuṣmaśavaracaṇḍagumataṅgaghorāntakograhalahalakāḥ /
krodhī huluhulurete daśa guravaḥ śivamayāḥ pūrve // 391
28.d:
उच्छुष्मशवरचण्डगुमतङ्गघोरान्तकोग्रहलहलकाः ।
क्रोधी हुलुहुलुरेते दश गुरवः शिवमयाः पूर्वे ॥ 391
28.m: Ucchuṣma, Śavara, Caṇḍagu, Mataṅga, Ghorāntaka, Ugra, Halahalaka, / Krodhin, [and] Huluhulu—these are the ten ancient gurus consisting of Śiva. // 391

28.s:
te svāṃśacittavṛttikrameṇa pauruṣaśarīramāsthāya /
anyonyabhinnasaṃvitkriyā api jñānaparipūrṇāḥ // 392
28.d:
ते स्वांशचित्तवृत्तिक्रमेण पौरुषशरीरमास्थाय ।
अन्योन्यभिन्नसंवित्क्रिया अपि ज्ञानपरिपूर्णाः ॥ 392
28.m: Having assumed human bodies according to the sequence of the mental states of their own portions, / though differing from one another in their consciousness and actions, they are complete in knowledge. // 392

28.s:
sarve'limāṃsanidhuvanadīkṣārcanaśāstrasevane niratāḥ /
abhimānaśamakrodhakṣamādiravāntaro bhedaḥ // 393
28.d:
सर्वेऽलिमांसनिधुवनदीक्षार्चनशास्त्रसेवने निरताः ।
अभिमानशमक्रोधक्षमादिरवान्तरो भेदः ॥ 393
28.m: All are devoted to wine, meat, sexual union, initiation, worship, and the study of scripture; / their secondary differences consist of pride, tranquillity, anger, patience, and the like. // 393

28.s:
itthaṃ vijñāya sadā śiṣyaḥ sampūrṇaśāstraboddhāram /
vyākhyāyai gurumabhyarthayeta pūjāpuraḥsaraṃ matimān // 394
28.d:
इत्थं विज्ञाय सदा शिष्यः सम्पूर्णशास्त्रबोद्धारम् ।
व्याख्यायै गुरुमभ्यर्थयेत पूजापुरःसरं मतिमान् ॥ 394
28.m: Knowing thus, the intelligent disciple should always request the guru who knows the complete scripture, / preceded by worship, to deliver an exposition. // 394

28.s:
so'pi svaśāsanīye paraśiṣye'pivāpi tādṛśaṃ śāstram /
śrotuṃ yogye kuryādvyākhyānaṃ vaiṣṇavādyadhare // 395
28.d:
सोऽपि स्वशासनीये परशिष्येऽपिवापि तादृशं शास्त्रम् ।
श्रोतुं योग्ये कुर्याद्व्याख्यानं वैष्णवाद्यधरे ॥ 395
28.m: He too should deliver an exposition to his own pupil, or even to the pupil of another, who is qualified / to hear such a scripture, [even] to an inferior such as a Vaiṣṇava. // 395

28.s:
karuṇārasaparipūrṇo guruḥ punarmarmadhāmaparivarjam /
adhame'pi hi vyākuryātsambhāvya hi śaktipātavaicitryam // 396
28.d:
करुणारसपरिपूर्णो गुरुः पुनर्मर्मधामपरिवर्जम् ।
अधमेऽपि हि व्याकुर्यात्सम्भाव्य हि शक्तिपातवैचित्र्यम् ॥ 396
28.m: Furthermore, the guru filled with the nectar of compassion should deliver an exposition even to a base person, / omitting the secret parts, considering the diversity of the descent of power. // 396

28.s:
liptāyāṃ bhuvi pīṭhe caturasre paṅkajatrayaṃ kajage /
kuryādvidyāpīṭhaṃ syādrasavahnyaṅgulaṃ tvetat // 397
28.d:
लिप्तायां भुवि पीठे चतुरस्रे पङ्कजत्रयं कजगे ।
कुर्याद्विद्यापीठं स्याद्रसवह्न्यङ्गुलं त्वेतत् ॥ 397
28.m: On smeared ground, on a square altar, on an eight-petaled lotus, / he should make three lotuses; this seat of knowledge should be thirty-six finger-widths. // 397

28.s:
madhye vāgīśānīṃ dakṣottarayorgurūngaṇeśaṃ ca /
adhare kaje ca kalpeśvaraṃ prapūjyārghapuṣpatarpaṇakaiḥ // 398
28.d:
मध्ये वागीशानीं दक्षोत्तरयोर्गुरून्गणेशं च ।
अधरे कजे च कल्पेश्वरं प्रपूज्यार्घपुष्पतर्पणकैः ॥ 398
28.m: Having worshipped Vāgīśānī in the center, the gurus on the right and left, and Gaṇeśa, / and the Lord of Rituals (Kalpeśvara) on the lower lotus, with offerings of water, flowers, and libations, // 398

28.s:
sāmānyavidhiniyuktārghapātrayogena cakramatha samyak /
santarpya vyākhyānaṃ kuryātsambandhapūrvakaṃ matimān // 399
28.d:
सामान्यविधिनियुक्तार्घपात्रयोगेन चक्रमथ सम्यक् ।
सन्तर्प्य व्याख्यानं कुर्यात्सम्बन्धपूर्वकं मतिमान् ॥ 399
28.m: and then having properly gratified the circle by means of the general offering-vessel prescribed by rule, / the intelligent one should deliver an exposition preceded by the connection [of the text]. // 399

28.s:
sūtrapadavākyapaṭalagranthakramayojanena sambandhāt /
avyāhatapūrvāparamupavṛhya nayeta vākyāni // 400
28.d:
सूत्रपदवाक्यपटलग्रन्थक्रमयोजनेन सम्बन्धात् ।
अव्याहतपूर्वापरमुपवृह्य नयेत वाक्यानि ॥ 400
28.m: By arranging the sequence of aphorisms, words, sentences, chapters, and the treatise through contextual connection, / he should elucidate the statements by strengthening them so that earlier and later parts are uncontradicted. // 400

28.s:
maṇḍūkaplavasiṃhāvalokanādyairyathāyathaṃ nyāyaiḥ /
avihatapūrvāparakaṃ śāstrārthaṃ yojayedasaṅkīrṇam // 401
28.d:
मण्डूकप्लवसिंहावलोकनाद्यैर्यथायथं न्यायैः ।
अविहतपूर्वापरकं शास्त्रार्थं योजयेदसङ्कीर्णम् ॥ 401
28.m: Applying principles appropriately, such as the frog's leap and the lion's backward glance, / he should articulate the unconfused meaning of the scripture so that earlier and later parts are consistent. // 401

28.s:
tantrāvartanabādhaprasaṅgatarkādibhiśca sannyāyaiḥ /
vastu vadedvākyajño vastvantarato viviktatāṃ vidadhat // 402
28.d:
तन्त्रावर्तनबाधप्रसङ्गतर्कादिभिश्च सन्न्यायैः ।
वस्तु वदेद्वाक्यज्ञो वस्त्वन्तरतो विविक्ततां विदधत् ॥ 402
28.m: And by sound logical methods such as repeated application, invalidation, context, and reasoning, / he who knows language should explain the real entity, distinguishing it from other entities. // 402

28.s:
yadyadvyāhṛtipadavīmāyāti tadeva dṛḍhatarairnyāyaiḥ /
balavatkuryāddūṣyaṃ yadyapyagre bhaviṣyatsyāt // 403
28.d:
यद्यद्व्याहृतिपदवीमायाति तदेव दृढतरैर्न्यायैः ।
बलवत्कुर्याद्दूष्यं यद्यप्यग्रे भविष्यत्स्यात् ॥ 403
28.m: Whatever enters the path of exposition, he should render strong with firmer arguments, / even if it will later become an object of refutation. // 403

28.s:
dṛḍharacitapūrvapakṣaproddharaṇapathena vastu yadvācyam /
śiṣyamatāvārohati tadāśu saṃśayaviparyayairvikalam // 404
28.d:
दृढरचितपूर्वपक्षप्रोद्धरणपथेन वस्तु यद्वाच्यम् ।
शिष्यमतावारोहति तदाशु संशयविपर्ययैर्विकलम् ॥ 404
28.m: When an entity to be spoken of ascends to the disciple's intellect along the path of refuting firmly constructed objections, / it promptly enters [the intellect] free from doubts and errors. // 404

28.s:
bhāṣā nyāyo vādo layaḥ kramo yadyadeti śiṣyasya /
sambodhopāyatvaṃ tathaiva gururāśrayedvyākhyām // 405
28.d:
भाषा न्यायो वादो लयः क्रमो यद्यदेति शिष्यस्य ।
सम्बोधोपायत्वं तथैव गुरुराश्रयेद्व्याख्याम् ॥ 405
28.m: Language, logic, debate, absorption, or sequence—whatever serves as / the means of comprehension for the disciple, in that very manner the guru should adopt the exposition. // 405

28.s:
vācyaṃ vastu samāpya pratarpaṇaṃ pūjanaṃ bhaveccakre /
punaraparaṃ vastu vadetpaṭalādūrdhvaṃ tu no jalpet // 406
28.d:
वाच्यं वस्तु समाप्य प्रतर्पणं पूजनं भवेच्चक्रे ।
पुनरपरं वस्तु वदेत्पटलादूर्ध्वं तु नो जल्पेत् ॥ 406
28.m: Having concluded the subject matter, there should be libation and worship in the circle; / he may speak on another subject, but he should not discourse beyond the chapter. // 406

28.s:
vyākhyānte kṣamayitvā visṛjya sarvaṃ kṣipedagādhajale /
śāstrādimadhyanidhane viśeṣataḥ pūjanaṃ kuryāt // 407
28.d:
व्याख्यान्ते क्षमयित्वा विसृज्य सर्वं क्षिपेदगाधजले ।
शास्त्रादिमध्यनिधने विशेषतः पूजनं कुर्यात् ॥ 407
28.m: At the conclusion of the exposition, having begged forgiveness and dismissed [the deities], he should throw everything into deep water. / He should perform special worship at the beginning, middle, and end of the scripture. // 407

28.s:
viśeṣapūjanaṃ kuryātsamayebhyaśca niṣkṛtau /
avikalpamaterna syuḥ prāyaścittāni yadyapi // 408
28.d:
विशेषपूजनं कुर्यात्समयेभ्यश्च निष्कृतौ ।
अविकल्पमतेर्न स्युः प्रायश्चित्तानि यद्यपि ॥ 408
28.m: He should also perform special worship as an expiation for [breaches of] vows. / Although there are no expiations for one whose mind is free of conceptual constructs, // 408

28.s:
tathāpyatattvavidvargānugrahāya tathā caret /
śrīpicau ca smṛtereva pāpaghnatve kathaṃ vibho // 409
28.d:
तथाप्यतत्त्वविद्वर्गानुग्रहाय तथा चरेत् ।
श्रीपिचौ च स्मृतेरेव पापघ्नत्वे कथं विभो ॥ 409
28.m: nevertheless he should act thus to extend grace to the class of those who do not know reality. / And in the venerable Picu, [it is asked]: 'Since remembrance alone destroys sin, how, O Lord, // 409

28.s:
prāyaścittavidhiḥ prokta iti devyā pracodite /
satyaṃ smaraṇameveha sakṛjjaptaṃ vimocayet // 410
28.d:
प्रायश्चित्तविधिः प्रोक्त इति देव्या प्रचोदिते ।
सत्यं स्मरणमेवेह सकृज्जप्तं विमोचयेत् ॥ 410
28.m: has a rule of expiation been proclaimed?' When thus questioned by the Goddess, [the Lord said]: / 'True, remembrance alone, recited once in this world, frees // 410

28.s:
sarvasmātkarmaṇo jālātsmṛtitattvakalāvidaḥ /
tathāpi sthitirakṣārthaṃ kartavyaścodito vidhiḥ // 411
28.d:
सर्वस्मात्कर्मणो जालात्स्मृतितत्त्वकलाविदः ।
तथापि स्थितिरक्षार्थं कर्तव्यश्चोदितो विधिः ॥ 411
28.m: from the entire web of action for one who knows the principles of the truth of remembrance. / Nevertheless, for the sake of preserving order, the prescribed rule must be observed. // 411

28.s:
atattvavedino ye hi caryāmātraikaniṣṭhitāḥ /
teṣāṃ dolāyite citte jñānahāniḥ prajāyate // 412
28.d:
अतत्त्ववेदिनो ये हि चर्यामात्रैकनिष्ठिताः ।
तेषां दोलायिते चित्ते ज्ञानहानिः प्रजायते ॥ 412
28.m: For those who do not know reality and are devoted solely to external practice, / when their mind wavers, loss of knowledge occurs. // 412

28.s:
tasmādvikalparahitaḥ saṃvṛtyuparato yadi /
śāstracaryāsadāyattaiḥ saṅkaraṃ tadvivarjayet // 413
28.d:
तस्माद्विकल्परहितः संवृत्युपरतो यदि ।
शास्त्रचर्यासदायत्तैः सङ्करं तद्विवर्जयेत् ॥ 413
28.m: Therefore, if one who is free from conceptual constructs has ceased from conventional behavior, / he should avoid mingling with those who are constantly devoted to scriptural ritual. // 413

28.s:
saṅkaraṃ vā samanvicchetprāyaścittaṃ samācaret /
yathā teṣāṃ na śāstrārthe dolārūḍhā matirbhavet // 414
28.d:
सङ्करं वा समन्विच्छेत्प्रायश्चित्तं समाचरेत् ।
यथा तेषां न शास्त्रार्थे दोलारूढा मतिर्भवेत् ॥ 414
28.m: Or, if he desires to mingle, he should perform expiation / so that their minds do not waver regarding the meaning of the scripture.' // 414

28.s:
yatsvayaṃ śivahastākhye vidhau saṃcoditaṃ purā /
śataṃ japtvāsya cāstrasya mucyate strīvadhādṛte // 415
28.d:
यत्स्वयं शिवहस्ताख्ये विधौ संचोदितं पुरा ।
शतं जप्त्वास्य चास्त्रस्य मुच्यते स्त्रीवधादृते ॥ 415
28.m: As was personally enjoined earlier in the rite known as the hand of Śiva: / 'Having recited this weapon-mantra a hundred times, one is freed [from sin], except for the murder of a woman. // 415

28.s:
śaktināśānmahādoṣo narakaṃ śāśvataṃ priye /
iti śrīratnamālāyāṃ samayollaṅghane kṛte // 416
28.d:
शक्तिनाशान्महादोषो नरकं शाश्वतं प्रिये ।
इति श्रीरत्नमालायां समयोल्लङ्घने कृते ॥ 416
28.m: From the destruction of a female power comes a grave fault, eternal hell, O beloved.' / Thus, in the venerable Ratnamālā, when a transgression of vows has been committed, // 416

28.s:
kulajānāṃ samākhyātā niṣkṛtirduṣṭakartarī /
śrīpūrve samayānāṃ tu śodhanāyoditaṃ yathā // 417
28.d:
कुलजानां समाख्याता निष्कृतिर्दुष्टकर्तरी ।
श्रीपूर्वे समयानां तु शोधनायोदितं यथा ॥ 417
28.m: the expiation named 'the destructive pair of scissors' is declared for members of the Kula. / As is stated in the venerable Pūrva for the purification of vows: // 417

28.s:
mālinī mātṛkā vāpi japyā lakṣatrayāntakam /
pratiṣṭhitasya pūrāderdarśane'nadhikāriṇā // 418
28.d:
मालिनी मातृका वापि जप्या लक्षत्रयान्तकम् ।
प्रतिष्ठितस्य पूरादेर्दर्शनेऽनधिकारिणा ॥ 418
28.m: Either the Mālinī or the Mātṛkā should be recited up to three hundred thousand times. / When an established city or [sanctuary] is seen by an unqualified person, // 418

28.s:
prāyaścittaṃ prakartavyamiti śrībrahmayāmale /
brahmaghno gurutalpastho vīradravyaharastathā // 419
28.d:
प्रायश्चित्तं प्रकर्तव्यमिति श्रीब्रह्मयामले ।
ब्रह्मघ्नो गुरुतल्पस्थो वीरद्रव्यहरस्तथा ॥ 419
28.m: expiation must be performed. Thus, in the venerable Brahmayāmala: / One who slays a brāhmaṇa, one who violates the guru's bed, likewise one who steals an initiate hero's property, // 419

28.s:
devadravyahṛdākāraprahartā liṅgabhedakaḥ /
nityādilopakṛdbhraṣṭasvakamātrāparicchadaḥ // 420
28.d:
देवद्रव्यहृदाकारप्रहर्ता लिङ्गभेदकः ।
नित्यादिलोपकृद्भ्रष्टस्वकमात्रापरिच्छदः ॥ 420
28.m: one who steals the property of the deity, an assailant, a destroyer of the liṅga, / one who causes the omission of daily rites and the rest, one who has abandoned one's own standard equipment— // 420

28.s:
śaktivyaṅgatvakṛdyogijñānihantā vilopakaḥ /
naimittikānāṃ lakṣādikramāddvidviguṇaṃ japet // 421
28.d:
शक्तिव्यङ्गत्वकृद्योगिज्ञानिहन्ता विलोपकः ।
नैमित्तिकानां लक्षादिक्रमाद्द्विद्विगुणं जपेत् ॥ 421
28.m:
